items.statement: Advertising spend at INR5.8 crores for quarter; full-year budget 5-6% of revenue vs current 2-2.5%

items.quote: part of our communication costs have been brought down by our better pricing that we have been able to engage with our telecom service providers. So yes, part of the savings are due to group-related synergies as well

items.quote: B2B contribute d around 25.5% of our revenues a nd this particular B2B contribution ha s been sort of similar for now last four quarters, five quarters

items.statement: Advertising optimized for quality traffic in top revenue categories; not chasing volume at any cost
items.quote: whatever spends that we are doing, those are highly optimized towards our top revenue -generating categories. At the same time, we do not insanely go after traffic to buy it at any cost if we find that my monetization is not adequate

items.quote: Effective tax rate stood at 8.2%, which is lower in this fiscal due to reversal of deferred tax on part of our treasury, which is moving from short -term to long -term bucket in fiscal '25

items.statement: Long-term effective tax rate expected 18-20% as older treasury taxed at LTCG rates and new investments at full corporate rate

items.statement: Jio IPL advertising pilot delayed to next season; unit economics must justify salesperson productivity
items.quote: for the recently concluded IPL, we could not sort of take it up because we started planning it a bit later. But for next season or any other such properties , we could possibly explore what all synergies can be in place. Just to clarify there also unit economics matters for us

items.statement: Clients shifting savings from cost takeout to fund high-priority transformation programs and AI foundational investments; early signs of recovery in BFSI and TMT
items.quote: Clients continue to focus on efficiency via cost takeout or vendor consolidation deals. items.statement: Q1 FY25 order inflow at $1.4 billion; multiple new MSAs signed with top-tier BFS institutions; several deals on cusp of signing moved into Q2
items.quote: Our order inflow for the quarter was US $1.4 billion. In the current business landscape with a focus on cost takeout and vendor consolidation, clients appreciate the clear value proposition we bring, and we believe we have significant runway ahead of us to capitalize on this aspect.

items.statement: EBIT margin 15% in Q1 FY25, up 30 bps sequentially; improvement driven by absence of project cancellation impact and operational efficiencies, partially offset by 50 bps visa cost headwind and higher SG&A
items.quote: EBIT for the quarter was INR13.7 billion, translating into an operating margin of 15% compared with 14.7% in the previous quarter. The absence of project cancellation impact of the last quarter and operational efficiencies led to margin improvement of more than 100 basis points.

items.statement: Depreciation and lease costs up sharply due to real estate investments in office capacity post-COVID and employee engagement programs; levels are sustainable
items.quote: It's primarily as you have called out depreciation and lease are both relating to real estate investments that we have been making in terms of increasing our office capacity. items.statement: Utilization excluding trainees rose to 88.3% from 86.9% in Q4 FY24; above comfort range of 85-86%; hiring to increase in Q2 to meet demand pipeline

items.statement: TTM attrition stable at 14.4%; onboarded 1,400 freshers in Q1 FY25, exhausting prior offer backlog; fresher hiring plan on track for remaining quarters; significant lateral hiring increase expected in Q2
items.quote: For the quarter, our TTM attrition remained stable at 14.4%. We onboarded around 1,400 freshers this quarter.

items.statement: Billed DSO improved to 55 days from 57 days in Q4; total receivable days including unbilled at 78 days, down 2 days sequentially; operating cash flow to PAT 109.9%, free cash flow to PAT 88.6%

items.statement: Visa costs increased 50 bps headwind to margins in Q1; wage hike planned for Q3 FY25, quantum and timing not yet decided
items.quote: This was partially offset by headwinds from higher visa cost of 50 basis points and higher SG&A on account of travel and marketing events.

items.statement: AI-related demand driving growth in data engineering, data governance, lineage, explainability, platform build-out (Canvas.ai, Fosfor), digital engineering, and ERP; 85% of top 100 clients engaged in AI initiatives
items.quote: More than 85% of enterprises are looking to accelerate their AI-related investments. Scaling of these AI solutions within the enterprise will require investments in infrastructure, data governance, data lineage, explainability, etc.

items.statement: Top 40 clients showed broad-based growth YoY and QoQ; tail rationalization ongoing; vendor consolidation wins in BFSI with multiple new MSAs signed
items.quote: If you look at the top 40 clients they have shown broad-based growth both on Y-o-Y as well as Q-o-Q basis. So I think we are more keen to track it on a slightly longer duration rather than just looking at quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Revenue $1.1 billion, up 3.7% YoY CC and 3.5% YoY USD; sequential growth 2.5% USD; BFSI +2.9% QoQ, -2.7% YoY; TMT +7.9% QoQ, +11.9% YoY; Manufacturing & Resources +1.8% QoQ, +10.5% YoY
items.quote: We are pleased to announce Q1 revenues of US $1.1 billion, growing 3.7% in constant currency and 3.5% in dollar terms on a year-on-year basis. Our sequential revenue growth in dollar terms was 2.5%.

items.statement: Americas 75.1% of revenue, grew 4.4% QoQ; Europe 14.4%; Rest of World 10.5%; cash flow hedges $3,740 million, balance sheet hedges $269 million
items.quote: In terms of geographies, America, which made up 75.1% of our revenue, has grown by 4.4% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. Europe made up 14.4%, and the Rest of the World made up 10.5% of our revenue.

items.statement: Regulatory compliance remains key spend area in BFSI alongside data+AI, consumer experience, and vendor consolidation
items.quote: Regulatory compliance continues to be a key spend area, followed by data plus AI, consumer experience and vendor consolidation.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia JV with Aramco in incorporation stage awaiting multi-jurisdiction approvals; ramp-up timeline and margin profile to be guided post-incorporation
items.quote: Saudi JV is in the incorporation stage right now. Multiple jurisdictions need to give us approvals for the incorporation to be completed. So we are in that process right now. It will take time to ramp up. So once we incorporate and start to ramp, we will give you more guidance on that at that time.

items.statement: Macro environment unchanged with focus on cost takeout; elections in next 18-24 months could disrupt client spending assumptions; margin target timeline deferred by a few quarters
items.quote: The broader macro environment has remained unchanged, and businesses continue to adopt agile strategies to cope with the economic conditions. We expect the market to follow this path for FY '25, where the focus will continue to be on cost takeout, but also on select high priority transformations.

items.statement: Management intends to mitigate regulatory margin impact primarily through restructuring distributor pay-outs using deferment and clawbacks.
items.quote: We endeavour to achieve this primarily through restructuring distributor pay -outs using a combination of deferment and clawbacks.

items.statement: Q1 product mix: ULIPs 38%, non-par savings 35%, participating 16%, term 6%, annuities 5% based on individual APE; ULIP mix moderated to ~35% exit rate in June.
items.quote: Regarding our product mix for the quarter, ULIPs accounted for 38%, non -par savings for 35%, participating products for 16%, term for 6%, and annuities for 5%, based on individual APE.

items.statement: Non-par savings grew 41% YoY; Click2Achieve latest variant garnered Rs 100 crore new business in 16 days.
items.quote: We have observed strong growth in non-par products, with the segment achieving a YoY increase of 41% . Additionally, our continued introduction of newer variants within the Click2Achieve umbrella has resonated well with customers, with the latest variant garnering Rs 100 crore of new business in merely 16 days.

items.statement: Individual APE grew 31% YoY (21% 2-year CAGR); policies up 22%, ticket size up 7%; growth outpaced private sector and industry.
items.quote: We have kicked off the year on a strong note, achieving a robust YoY growth of 31% based on individual APE, translating to a 2 -year CAGR of 21%.

items.statement: Retail protection grew 28% YoY (36% 2-year CAGR); retail sum assured grew 46% driven by protection expansion and rider attachment.
items.quote: Retail protection experienced significant growth of 28% based on individual APE and a robust 36% on a two -year CAGR basis. This is despite us continuing to follow a calibrated pricing and risk management approach.

items.statement: Credit protect segment flat due to slower disbursements and competitive intensity; prepared to step away from unviable segments.
items.quote: The credit protect segment remained flat due to slower disbursement in certain lines of business and increased competitive intensity across select partners. Our focus remains on building a sustainable and profitable business in this segment, and we are prepared to temporarily step away if a segment or a partnership becomes unviable.

items.statement: New to HDFC Life customers exceed 70% in Q1; agency channel term mix 12-13% vs HDFC Bank 3-4%, potential uplift to 5%.
items.quote: The proportion of 'New to HDFC Life' customers in Q1 remains robust, exceeding 70%.

items.statement: HDFC Bank counter share reached 66% end of Q1, up from 56.5% in Q1 previous year.
items.quote: Our counter share in HDFC Bank continued to be healthy, reaching 66% by the end of the quarter, up from 56.5% in Q1 of the previous year.

items.statement: Investing in geographical reach, new customer segments, agency network expansion (60 new branches, 18,500 net agent additions), technology and capability development.
items.quote: We are committed to investing for long -term growth by expanding our geographical reach and tapping into new customer segments. These initiatives will help drive our growth trajectory over the next 3-4 years.

items.statement: Project Inspire technology transformation on track; group business transformation launch targeted between Q3 and Q4 FY25.
items.quote: We are on track to launch our group business transformation between Q3 and Q4 this year.

items.statement: Plan to raise sub-debt up to Rs 2,000 crore in one or more tranches over next 12 months to strengthen solvency and fuel growth.
items.quote: To strengthen our solvency position, we will be raising sub -debt up to Rs 2,000 crore, in one or more tranches, over the next 12 months. This sub -debt raise will help fuel our growth aspirations.

items.statement: VNB grew 18% YoY and 2-year CAGR to Rs 718 crore; PAT grew 15% YoY to Rs 478 crore; embedded value Rs 49,611 crore with operating ROEV 15.5%.
items.quote: Our Q1 value of new business was Rs. 718 crores, reflecting a healthy 18% growth both YoY and on a two -year CAGR basis.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 186%; regulatory headroom for sub-debt raise approx Rs 2,000 crore; comfortable solvency range 180-190%.
items.quote: Our solvency ratio stands at 186%.

items.statement: Persistency improved: 13th month 88% (+108 bps YoY), 61st month 56% (+282 bps YoY); renewal collections grew 10% YoY.
items.quote: Persistency for the 13th and 61st months improved to 88% and 56%, respectively, marking increases of 108 basis points and 282 basis points versus the previous year.

items.statement: IRDAI Master Circular reforms welcomed; new surrender value rules effective Oct 1; existing products self-certified, no IRDA approval needed for compliance changes.
items.quote: From 1st of October. So last date of selling under the current structure is 30th of September.

items.statement: Tax sensitivity assumes current 12.5%+surcharge rate moving to 25% on all policyholder and shareholder surplus, no exemptions factored.
items.quote: It's assuming that the current tax rate of 12.5% plus surcharge changes to 25%. And the policyholder and shareholder segment surplus get taxed at the higher rate . Essentially, everything gets taxed at the higher rate.

items.statement: Retail protection pricing calibrated; above-60 segment saw up to 5% price change (<0.1% of business); pricing evolves with experience, reinsurer talks, competition.
items.quote: For one segment which is above 60 there was up to a 5% change in price and this business is less than 0.1% of our overall business. So honestly not hing of any consequence at all a nd pricing will evolve based on how deep we go into the country in terms of customer segments.

items.statement: Credit life pricing competitive; margins stable; letting go business where quality poor or disbursements slow; calibrated strategy on value penetration.
items.quote: We are working to ensure that our margins remain stable. I don't think it is true that our margins have decreased. In some places where quality of business is not good, we are letting some of that business go.

items.statement: GTI (Group Term Insurance) pricing remains competitive annually; calibrated approach due to stamp duty on annual renewals; market share maintained.
items.quote: That remains competitive as every year. In most cases there were a few players who have been looking at it, but that is sometimes balanced more with the relationship that we have with that particular corporate and the overall relationships we have got.

items.statement: Regulatory surrender value changes may compress margins ~100 bps; mitigation via distributor payout restructuring; industry flux expected but manageable.
items.quote: We anticipate a gross impact of approximately 100 bps on the company's new business margin due to higher surrender value payable on early exits. Impact for us is limited due to our balanced approach to business.

items.statement: Tax rate increase risk: sensitivity shows VNB impact if corporate tax moves to 25% on all surplus; DTC treatment uncertain.
items.quote: We will have to wait and see how this really pans out, but this assumes that everything gets taxed at this rate. And it's not factoring any other exemptions that may or may not be available in the future.

items.statement: HDFC Pension AUM grew 67% YoY to >Rs 88,000 crore; market share >43%; expanding in GIFT City via Dubai subsidiary for NRI segment.
items.quote: The AUM of HDFC Pension Fund Management grew by 67% YoY and surpassed Rs. 88,000 crores. We continue to build the pension business, maintaining a market share of over 43%.

items.statement: New partnerships with Upstox, Fino Payments Bank, Peerless Financial Services to reach new segments and markets.
items.quote: Further, we continue to actively forge strategic partnerships and have recently partnered with Upstox, Fino Payments Bank, Peerless Financial Services, amongst others.

items.statement: Q1 margin gap driven by product mix shift to ULIP (38% vs 25% YoY), offset by positive fixed cost absorption of 0.3%
items.quote: In the Q1 context, everything is pretty much product mix because the scale is back. The growth was 31% for the period. You will see a positive fixed cost absorption of 0.3%, but we have a 1.3% negative on the product mix, which is largely the unit -linked mix increasing from 25% to 38% on a like-to-like basis.

items.statement: ULIP mix was 38% in Q1 but exit rate in June dropped to ~35%
items.quote: I just want to add tha t, while for the quarter, ULIP mix was 38%, but exit rate in June has come down to about 35%.

items.statement: Sub-debt headroom of INR 2,000 crores approved for 12 months; full raise would add 20-22% to solvency
items.quote: Our headroom today, based on the regulatory limit is about INR 2,000 crores. We will see in terms of how we want to go about it. We have an approval to raise this over a 12 -month period in one or more tranches.

items.statement: Expect risk-based capital regime in 12-18 months, enabling more business with same capital
items.quote: We are also expecting over the next 12 to 18 months risk -based capital regime to kick in. When that happens, our understanding is that we will be able to write more business with the same amount of capital.

items.statement: HDFC Bank counter share rose from 56-57% to ~65% in last 7-8 months; target 70-72%
items.quote: In the last 7-8 months, counter share has gone up very meaningfully from 56% -57% to ~65%, in that range. And as far as 70%-72% share is concerned, I think it is a matter of time before some of that organic movement upward should happen regardless of surrender charges, no surrender charges .

items.statement: Non-par savings seeing broad traction across ticket sizes (above/below 5L) and tiers (1,2,3)
items.quote: We are seeing good traction in this category. We are seeing traction both in above 5 lakhs and below 5 lakhs. We are seeing traction in Tier 1, 2 and 3. So any which way we cut non-par, we are seeing traction.

items.statement: ULIP weighted average sum assured multiple increased from ~20x to ~30x; rider attachment still nascent
items.quote: So, I mentioned the 20x was the number some time back. Now it is close to 30x.

items.statement: Longer policy tenures (21 vs 16 years) driven by Click 2 Achieve; longer terms improve margins meaningfully
items.quote: On your second question in terms of the increase in tenure, that is something that we have been consciously driving because longer-term products can offer better value to customers. And this has been enabled by our new launch of Click 2 Achieve that we had launched a few months back.

items.statement: Higher surrender values post Oct 1 neutral to margins; paid-up value linked to G-Sec rates, no surrender profit assumed
items.quote: Economically, the value to the company will not be different because if you see how the surrender value has been defined, it is linked to the paid -up value and it is a present value of the paid-up benefit at the current G-Sec rate. So, for company it will be very neutral, whether the policyholder continues in a paid-up status, or he surrenders.

items.statement: No change in new business strain from higher surrender values due to prudent pricing and assumptions
items.quote: Not in our case because of what all Eshwari had mentioned , prudence in pricing as well as surrender assumptions does not result in a very significant change in our reserves. So that does not affect our accounting profit.

items.statement: VNB assumption changes in mortality and persistency across segments; small non-material margin impact
items.quote: We have changed the assumptions in mortality, persistency across product segments. It had a small nonmaterial impact on the margin, which is what is getting carried forward to the quarter 1 of this year because whatever was reported in last Q1 didn't have this assumption change.

items.statement: Unwind rate 8.1% (down 10bps YoY); economic variance INR 400 cr mainly from equity (markets up 8-9%)
items.quote: The unwind rate is 8.1%. It's mainly due to the yield curve change offset by some positive outlook on equity. Last year, it was 8.2%, this year is 8.1 %, 10 basis point reduction. On the economic variances, it is mainly coming from equity.

items.statement: Guaranteed return products priced at 5.5-6.5% to customer; earn spread above G-Sec+50bps discount rate
items.quote: So, the rates that we offer to the customer ranges anywhere between, in the current context, maybe, from say, 5.5 to maybe 6.5. So, for us to give the customer 5.5 to 6.5, we need to have a spread to manage our risk as well as account for the baseline profitability and cost of capital.

items.statement: EoM ratio ~22% in Q1 due to infrastructure/people investments in partner branches, not commission changes
items.quote: For quarter 1, the change that you see in the expense ratio is more in terms of the investments that we made in terms of infrastructure as well as people that we have deployed in partner branches, nothing much to do with the commercial arrangements.

items.statement: Composite license hopeful to pass Parliament; internal product ideas ready if approved
items.quote: So, we are hopeful that it gets introduced in both the houses of parliament. And hopefully, it gets passed. We have been waiting for quite a long time. And if that were to happen, we will evaluate our options.

items.statement: Proposed final dividend impacts solvency by ~5%
items.quote: Around 5% impact on solvency after assuming impact of dividend payout.

items.statement: Investing in agency: 60 new branches in Tier 2/3, retiral advisory program, Exide channel integration
items.quote: On the growth in the Tier 2, Tier 3 market, we have expanded to some 60 branches. We are looking at it in terms of the number of new agents that we have added, that continues to be the best in market also. There is an NOP strategy that we are putting into place. We have invested heavily in our retiral advisory financial consultant program.

items.statement: Annuity growth calibrated; stepping back from irrational pricing pockets in annuity and credit life
items.quote: There is some irrational pricing in certain pockets. We have to take that into account, and we are not in the business of writing business which is not viable for us in terms of either managing the risk or the pricing. We will take these calibrated calls.

items.statement: HDFC Bank channel mix: ULIP in 40s%, non-par mid-to-late 30s%, term rising steadily
items.quote: Unit -linked is in the 40s in HDFC Bank, and non-par is fairly healthy in the mid - to -late 30s. And as Vibha mentioned earlier, the term mix is increasing fairly steadily.

items.statement: Sub-debt negative carry minimal (~20-30bps historically); large book allows duration mismatch to minimize carry
items.quote: In the past the sub-debt that we carry has a fairly negligible negative carry of about 20- 30 basis points because we have the ability to invest. All the sub debt that will be raised will get invested and we don't expect negative carry on that to be significant because we don't necessarily need to match the duration of what we raised with where we invest given that we have a fairly large book.

items.statement: Solvency ratios declining industry-wide due to longer-term contracts; prefer raising capital ahead of growth
items.quote: The solvency ratio for all the players is coming down because of the reason that Niraj just mentioned , the type of contracts the companies are writing. So maybe some companies have been at 300% solvency ratio , may not be raising capital, but if you see the trend for every company the solvency ratio is coming down.

items.statement: Trail commission discussions early; regulator expects back-ended payouts; no immediate distributor agreement
items.quote: We are in very early stages right now. No one will agree immediately. I'm sure there will be some bit of convincing, some bit of expectation from regulator and so on. So, I think those conversations are on as we speak.

items.statement: Group protection (credit protect & GTI) flat YoY; GTI small and will remain small
items.quote: So, both are almost flattish. And yes, these are profitable segments when you get it right. But credit life is a lot more impactful than GTI. GTI for us is small, it will probably remain small.

items.statement: Targets roughly 20% PAT margin and 23-24% EBITDA margin; anything beyond that will be aggressively invested for growth
items.quote: We have said that generally roughly around 20% PAT and roughly around 23%, 24% EBITDA that's kind of a target number we are carrying today on our mind.

items.statement: Revenue grew 25% YoY to INR315 crores in Q1 FY25; growth across regions with EMEA 25%, India 20%, APAC 65%, US 13%
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter reached INR315 crores representing a 25% Y-o-Y growth. There was good business growth across regions with EMEA region growing at 25% Y-o-Y. India at 20% Y-o-Y. APAC has come back on the growth path with 65% AOI in the quarter and U.S. region was at 13% growth.

items.statement: Annuity revenue 60% of annual revenue (ATS, AMC, SaaS, support); license 18-20%; implementation 21-22%; distribution expected similar this year
items.quote: We have about 60% of revenue coming in from the annuity streams. We have three annuity streams which is the ATS, AMC, the SaaS revenue and the support revenues together they comprise 60% of our revenues on an annual basis. We have about 18% to 20% in any particular year coming in from the license revenue and then we have the implementation revenue which is a service component which is again 21%, 2

items.statement: Average deal sizes grew substantially ~20-25% last year; early to judge this quarter due to smaller quarter
items.quote: So I think our average deal sizes last year has substantially grown I think, from -- around 20%, 25% because our number of deals were at the same level, but the average deal size has grown substantially.

items.statement: R&D expenses fully expensed in P&L, not capitalized
items.quote: We expense off always in P&L. We don't capitalize any expenses.

items.statement: Hired ~500 campus hires since January; tactical lateral hiring ongoing; no layoffs
items.quote: So what has helped, I think we have hired roughly around 500 campus people since January to until now. So they are already on board most of them maybe. There is some tactical hiring laterals going on.

items.statement: Net trade receivables INR402 crores, net DSO 112 days as of June 30, 2024; collections grew 18% YoY
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, our net trade receivables were at INR402 crores as of 30th June 2024, which resulted in net DSO of 112 days. Our collection for the quarter has witnessed a growth of 18% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Existing customers contribute 80-85% of annual revenue; new logos max 15-20% of annual revenue; new logos predominantly in banking, financial services, insurance, shared services, BPO, government
items.quote: So Vinay, generally at the annual basis the existing customers contribute roughly around 80% to 85% of our business. So that also means new deals in those orders. It does not mean the repeat of business because you have to sell more. And for the same year because if you book also orders you may not be able to realize all. So for the same year, you will be only able to get around 15% in a great yea

items.statement: Partner revenue ~20% of total, direct 80%; ratio stable; partner channel not growing faster than direct
items.quote: So generally, I think it remains static on an annual basis, at around 20% of revenues, which is partner-related and 80% is still direct. So with the growth is both the engines, there is not a significant shift that the partner one is going at a faster pace.

items.statement: Revenue growth sustained 24-30% range for last 8-9 quarters; Q1 growth in line with trend
items.quote: No, not really. I think it is in trend, it's in line with where we have been going for the last 8, 9 quarters and we have been growing in the range of 24% to 30% in last 8, 9 quarters. So it's a line with that growth.

items.statement: Added senior management globally especially sales and marketing; campus and lateral hiring to support growth plans
items.quote: We continue to build on our global workforce and have made additions to the senior management across the globe especially on the sales and marketing side. The quarter also saw new hiring, both campus and lateral to support our growth plans.

items.statement: US growth conservative at 13%; early signs of revival but no big momentum shift; mature market penetration taking time
items.quote: We'll still target our growth which can be healthy rate, but I don't think substantially the equation for us has changed. And again I may not we are not probably the best judges of the market because we are slightly away from that business, not like service companies.

items.statement: CSR initiative: inaugurated Newgen Digital Discovery Paathshala skill development center in New Delhi for mothers of students
items.quote: Reinforcing our commitment in nurturing talent and fostering inclusive growth, Newgen unveiled the pioneering initiative aimed at accelerating the skill development and digital prowress of women in underserved communities. The company inaugurated a dedicated skill development center in New Delhi to serve as a hub for imparting skill training and essential digital education to the mothers of studen

items.statement: Partnered with Finastra to offer best-in-class banking solutions and jointly expand market base
items.quote: During the quarter, we partnered with Finastra, a global financial -- provider of financial software application to offer best-in-class banking solutions for existing customers and also jointly expand the market base.

items.statement: Seasonality reducing: Q1 share of annual revenue moved from 17% to 20-21% over last 3 years; annuity revenue non-seasonal, license deals lumpier in Q3/Q4
items.quote: I think we have moved from the Q1 generally falls between roughly around 17% to 21% of our annual revenue for the same year. And from 17% to 20%, 21%, we have moved over the last 3 years. So there is a 3%, 4% shift happening every year and Q1, Q2 are leaner quarters in Q2 and Q4, Q4 being the largest quarter.

items.statement: Mid-term guidance: top line CAGR 17-18%, operating EBITDA margin 27-28%, PAT margin 12.5-13% by FY26
items.quote: We expect to achieve a top line CAGR of around 17% to 18% and an operating EBITDA margin of approximately 27% to 28%, and a PAT margin of about 12.5% to 13% by FY '26.

items.statement: Near-term revenue guidance: FY25 Rs 690-700 cr, FY26 ~Rs 850 cr
items.quote: Our revenue for FY '25 is expected to be somewhere around Rs. 690 crores to Rs. 700 crores. And in FY '26 it's around approximately Rs. 850 crores.

items.statement: Second solar project 6 MW at Jamshedpur, capex ~Rs 30 cr funded 75% debt, 25% internal accruals
items.quote: We are launching a second solar energy project in Jamshedpur with an approximate capacity of 6 megawatts. The capital expenditure for the project would be about Rs. 30 crores funded 75% by debt and 25% by internal accruals.

items.statement: Optimum utilisation assumed at 70%; ramp-up typically 1-2 quarters but dependent on customer
items.quote: So, we assume optimum utilization to be anywhere in the 70% range. And typically, it would take anywhere between one and two quarters to scale it up. But however, having said that, please appreciate that these are typical numbers. We are reliant on a different party for helping us ramp up. And so, while typically it may be one to two quarters, I would also like to put a disclaimer over here, it ca

items.statement: Margins stable due to conversion model with flat per-tonne fee; zinc cost pass-through; not affected by steel cycle
items.quote: See, we are doing a conversion business where the cost of goods sold, I mean, the raw material cost is not in our books. So, as stated by our MD sir already in the call, we are not affected by the steel cycle. So, maintaining the margin with 1 basis point plus/minus is very much possible in our business.

items.statement: No oversupply risk foreseen for at least two years; steel demand growing with economy
items.quote: No, I mean, at least you can see two years down, I can't even see that much. But I don’t foresee a oversupply situation. I think we are a growing economy; steel plays a very large part in that. And as the economy continues to grow, uses of steel, fabrication, structural will continue to grow

items.statement: No take-or-pay commitments; long-term contracts for full capacity; expected order load equals capacity (530k MT) but practical utilisation ~70%
items.quote: So, we do not have specific order books per say, we have long term contracts for the entire capacity that we operate for the customers. And so, in some way if my tubes capacity is 530,000 tons, that's the expected order load. But like I said, let us say 70% of that to be practical.

items.statement: Key customer TATA Steel: tubes contract extended to Aug 2024, CRM contract to Sep 2024, TMT contract to Nov 2025; negotiations ongoing for 3-5 year renewals
items.quote: We have already extended a number of times the current tubes contract has been extended up to August, and the CRM contract is up to September. The TMT contract is up to November 25.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved from 130 days (Jun'23) to 53 days (Jun'24)
items.quote: We have seen a steady improvement in our cash conversion cycle from 130 days in June '23 to 53 days in June '24.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 117 cr (Jun'24) vs Rs 221 cr (Jun'23); net debt/equity 0.17, net debt/EBITDA 0.69; gross debt Rs 107 cr excludes Phase-2 debt
items.quote: Net debt remains at a stable level and stood at Rs. 117 crores in June '24 as compared to Rs. 221 crores in June '23. Net debt by equity stood at 0.17 and net debt by operating EBITDA stood at 0.69 in June 24.

items.statement: Contract compensation fixed in absolute per-tonne terms, not percentage; zinc cost pass-through
items.quote: Absolute terms. The margins are not fixed, the compensation of the contract is fixed

items.statement: HR coil and CR coil supplied free by customers; company does not purchase raw materials
items.quote: So, Miraj, we do not buy the HR or the CR, right? It's free, supplied by the customers. So, I do not think any of us are adequately qualified to answer that question.

items.statement: Solar capacity limited by regulations: 5 MW in West Bengal, 6 MW in Jamshedpur; will expand if regulations allow
items.quote: It's actually location based, so in West Bengal I can only do 5 megawatts, and in Jamshedpur currently with the mix of space and regulations, I can only do 6 megawatts.

items.statement: TMT utilisation reached 82% in Q1 FY25 (target was FY26); FY25 production ~250k MT assumed safe
items.quote: So, based on our assumptions, we expect the numbers to hold for the rest of the year. However, should there be any material change on the customer side in terms of steady supply, we will keep you guys updated in the following quarters. But as things stand now, I think it is a very safe assumption to meet the numbers for the full year.

items.statement: Aggregate demand environment shows little change; OEMs split between those with strong balance sheets investing through transition and those balancing investments with short-term needs
items.quote: At an aggregate level, we're not really seeing any drop in demand. What we have seen over the last couple of years is that there are specific customer related issues that are impacting the quantum of investment and the speed of investment.

items.statement: Three large deals won in Q1: battery pack design for global EV battery manufacturer, turnkey cab development for North American commercial vehicle OEM, and first/business class seat development for European Aerospace Tier 1
items.quote: Q1 was also a solid quarter in terms of deal signings, with 3 large deals won during April, May and June.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin at 18.2% in Q1 vs 18.4% previous quarter; net profit increased 3.1% sequentially; aim for 20%+ EBITDA margin long term
items.quote: Despite the decline in revenue in Q1, our margin performance remained resilient with operating EBITDA coming in at 18.2% in Q1 compared with 18.4% in the previous quarter. Moreover, net profit increased by 3.1% sequentially.

items.statement: Confident in sequential growth from Q2 onwards; expect consistent quarter-on-quarter growth through fiscal year; no specific revenue guidance provided
items.quote: We are confident in the quarter-on-quarter growth that should see the business at the end of the year being much improved in terms of volumes from where we are today.

items.statement: BMW joint venture expected to launch in second half of fiscal year; regulatory approvals and team confirmation underway; business plan execution on track
items.quote: We expect the joint venture to be launched in the second half of this fiscal year. I announced in April that we have to go through regulatory approval. We have to confirm the seed team and confirm the leadership team that will run that organization.

items.statement: Headcount reduced 1.4% to 12,505; utilization improved 50 bps to 86.5%; focus on pyramid optimization with campus hires and strategic hiring in growth areas
items.quote: The total headcount stood at about 12,505 at the end of the quarter, a reduction of about 1.4%, reflecting about 183 employees compared with the previous quarter and this reflects an optimization of our capacity between full-time employees and the outsourced resources.

items.statement: Last 12-month attrition down to 13.7% from 14.5% in Q4; annualized attrition at 12.8%; expect further reduction in coming quarter
items.quote: Trends on attrition levels continue to remain favorable as we saw our last 12-month attrition coming down again this quarter to 13.7% compared with 14.5%, which it stood in Q4.

items.statement: DSO at 84 days vs 83 days previous quarter; billed DSO 58 days, unbilled DSO 26 days; free cash flow INR 220 crores; net working capital release of INR 70 crores
items.quote: We've maintained robust collection efficiency with a total DSO of 84 days compared with 83 days of the previous quarter and 96 days in the same quarter of last year, and billed DSO came in at 58 days, while unbilled DSO stood at 26 days at the end of Q1.

items.statement: Remain debt-free; net cash $131.4 million vs $146.3 million previous quarter after $49 million dividend payout in June
items.quote: At the end of first quarter, we continue to remain debt free and the net cash on our balance sheet stood at a healthy $131.4 million compared with $146.3 million at the end of the previous quarter. This balance is after a dividend payout of $49 million that we did during the month of June.

items.statement: Services revenue down 1% sequentially due to VinFast ramp-down and project phasing; Technology Solutions down 7.4% due to product seasonality; education vertical grew 4% sequentially
items.quote: In Services, we also recorded a sequential revenue decline of 1% on account of the short-term phasing of a number of large programs and the completion of our ramp down at VinFast.

items.statement: Anchor customers Tata Motors and JLR showing strong results informing capex confidence; BMW JV building presence in Germany; Airbus relationship growing with new seat manufacturer deal
items.quote: We are engaged obviously with our anchor customers, Tata Motors and JLR. They have had a very good set of results themselves in the recent past and that's informing their confidence in terms of capex and investment in new products.

items.statement: Offshore revenue mix improved 130 bps sequentially to 39%; services ex-VinFast grew ~26% year-on-year and ~1% sequentially
items.quote: Regarding our mix of on-site and offshore revenues, revenues generated from outside our delivery centers in India and Romania and executed offshore improved by 130 basis points sequentially, reaching 39%.

items.statement: EV adoption not following smooth curve but IEA projects 17M units in 2024 and 50% of global car sales by 2035; North America volatility from potential legislation changes; aerospace highly regulated requiring capability demonstration
items.quote: We believe that most technology transitions, including EVs, do not follow a smooth adoption curve. Despite growth rates tapering in 2024, the International Energy Agency continues to assert that global EV sales are likely to increase to somewhere close to 17 million units this year.

items.statement: Operating expenses down 2.2% QoQ; employee benefits flat; other expenses up 11.5% from professional fees, CSR, travel; outsourcing charges down 12.4% from subcontracting optimization
items.quote: We continue to exercise strong operating discipline during the quarter with the operating expenses reducing by 2.2%, thereby enabling us to maintain a relatively stable EBITDA margin that came in at 18.2% compared with 18.4% of the previous quarter.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle sector accelerating software-defined vehicle investments; expanding beyond passenger vehicles into off-highway and truck sectors with middleware and full vehicle capabilities
items.quote: Notably, we are now starting to witness the accelerated adoption of software-defined capabilities within the commercial and off-highway vehicle space. This growing demand should help us extend our ambitions beyond our traditional focus upon passenger vehicles.

items.statement: BMW JV requires regulatory approval before launch in H2 FY25; aerospace engagements require process and capability compliance demonstration before larger projects
items.quote: I announced in April that we have to go through regulatory approval. We have to confirm the seed team and confirm the leadership team that will run that organization.

items.statement: Targets 4%+ PAT margin and 6-7% EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: So, somewhere around like we are looking the 4% plus PAT margin, we are looking. And the EBITDA margin is around like 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Plans to open 3 new stores in FY25, targeting 20 stores by FY28
items.quote: We plan to open three new stores in FY '25, aiming to increase the total number of stores from eight in FY '24 to 20 by FY '28.

items.statement: Targets diamond studded jewellery revenue share increase from 6% to 15%
items.quote: Our target is to increase the revenue share from diamond studded jewellery from 6% to 15%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 6-8 crore for three new stores in FY25 plus Rs 100 crore inventory
items.value: Rs 6-8 cr capex, Rs 100 cr inventory
items.quote: CAPEX, we require somewhere around Rs. 6 crores to Rs. 8 crores to build a new showroom, because we are coming up with three new stores in FY '25. And for inventory, we require somewhere around Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: New stores in Neemuch, Ajmer and Ratlam flagship (8,000-10,000 sq ft) to open in FY25
items.quote: Similarly, we are going to open new stores in Neemuch, Madhya Pradesh and Ajmer, Rajasthan in this financial year which are estimated to start in the next two to three months. Our Ratlam store, which is our hope town from where we have started our journey, that store also needs renovation as per the changing time, so we are also coming up with a new and improved flagship store and Ratlam, and we w

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 8% on Rs 504 crore revenue, PAT up 60% to Rs 25 crore
items.quote: Despite elevated gold price and weak industry demand, our consolidated revenue impressively grew by 7% year-over-year to Rs. 504 crores. Our EBITDA soared by 51% to Rs. 38 crores with a strong margin of 8% during Q1 FY '25. Our profit after tax surged to Rs. 25 crores, reflecting a remarkable growth of 60%.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margin 6-8% for full year FY25
items.quote: But this EBITDA 8%, we will be able to maintain it around 6% to 8% somewhere.

items.statement: Making charges 9-10% for gold jewellery, 15-17% for diamond studded
items.quote: And average making charges for our pure gold jewellery is like 9% to 10%, and for the diamond studded, it is like 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Diamond studded share 6% of sales, targeting 10-15% in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, right now and before, our studded ratio is 6% and now we are like planning to achieve like between 10% to 15% of the studded ratio, the gold versus studded reserve ratio.

items.statement: Wedding jewellery 52% of sales, implementing shop-in-shop model across stores
items.quote: Like out of total sales, 52% is the wedding jewellery sales. So, technically every 5 out of 10 customer comes in for the wedding jewellery. So, in Indore we have implemented one shop-in-shop model where which is an exclusive outlet for the wedding customers, where there is a different hospitality, different field, different D. P. Abhushan Limited July 19, 2024 designs, enhanced designs. So, in all

items.statement: Q1 demand weak due to elections and fewer wedding dates (25-27 vs normal 45-60), expects recovery from Q3
items.quote: this quarter, there are multiple reasons, because election is going on and due to the limited wedding dates, that’s why the season was little low in the 1st Quarter. I think in a normal case, they are like 45 days to 60 days where the marriage dates, but in this quarter there is like 25 to 27 dates are available thoroughly. Vikrant Kashyap: Okay. So, how do you see quarter two onwards? Vikas Katar

items.statement: Old gold exchange 20-25% of procurement, monthly saving schemes 3-5% of sales
items.quote: So, our old gold exchange program is like somewhere around 20% to 25% we are like procuring from the old gold. And the monthly saving scheme is somewhere around 3% to 5%, the total entire sale.

items.statement: Follows natural hedging - buys gold same day as sales, no MCX hedging
items.quote: So, we maintain the natural hedging policy. So, we do not hedge anything on MCX or like that. We maintain a natural hedging policy, like whatever gold we sell on the particular day, we buy it on the same day at the same price.

items.statement: Weighted average inventory cost below market due to legacy stock (Rs 100 to Rs 70,000 per 10g)
items.quote: And how it has impacted our margin is like because we are following the weighted average cost of method, and we have been in this business since 1940. So, in our inventory there is a gold which is like Rs. 100 per 10 grams ranging from Rs. 70,000 per 10 grams. So, our weighted average cost is always lesser than the current market price.

items.statement: Focus on Tier-2/3 cities with less competition and high purchasing power; metro entry after 2 years
items.quote: So, Maharashtra and Mumbai we have in our plan, but after like two years maybe we are focusing on Mumbai and big metro cities. Because right now we think there is a lot of scope in the Tier-2, Tier-3 cities where the competition is less, but the purchasing power is very high. So, we are more focusing on particular those areas first.

items.statement: Gold price spikes cause customer pullback; volumes recover when prices stabilize
items.quote: Because there was a sudden spike in the gold prices, so that's why we have seen in the recent past trend that whenever there is a sudden spike in the gold prices, the customer takes a back foot. And once the gold prices get stabilized, the sales gets on increasing.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of ~30% YoY with potential 10% upside from large deals
items.quote: We are expecting a growth of about 30% in this FY25 from last year. We are expecting EBITDA margin of around 15%. Further, there is a potential upside of another 10% growth if we manage to get few of the large deals , which we

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target of around 15%
items.quote: We are expecting EBITDA margin of around 15%.

items.statement: Order book at INR 810 million at end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: Frog Cellsat Ltd's order book stands at impressive INR 810 million at closing of Q1 FY25, reflecting strong client confidence in our capabilities and in our ability to deliver high quality innovative telecom infrastructure solutions.

items.statement: Growth driven by in-building coverage, DAS, greenfield airports, metros, 4G-5G upgrades, third operator spending, railway EHS coverage, interference mitigation
items.quote: Looking ahead, our growth is driven by rising demands for in building coverage and expanding opportunities in mobile coverage solution s, particularly DAS, greenfield airports and metros alongside 4G to 5G upgrades

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin compressed to 7.88% from 10.89% due to hiring for upcoming services
items.quote: Margins stood at 7.88% compared to 10.89% over the same period. The compression in EBITDA margin is attributed to increased hiring to meet the demand for our upcoming services.

items.statement: Product margins intact; employee cost increase is buildup for new services and products
items.quote: The product margins are intact, the cost of employees have gone up, and that is basically a buildup to deliver new services and products for the business which we have in hand and which is an

items.statement: Planning SMT line investment; may include in enhanced PLI investment bucket for higher incentives
items.quote: We are expecting that we'll get an opportunity to increase our investment limits in as per PLI. And if that opportunity is coming to us, we would like to include this SMT line investment in that investment bucket that we'll have for PLI, so that we'll have increased incentives under PLI.

items.statement: SMT line not yet installed; delayed to align with potential PLI investment enhancement
items.quote: Firstly we have not put up the PCB line, SMT line right now, It's in the plan. We have delayed the plan of putting it.

items.statement: Revenue mix for FY25 guided at ~INR 30 cr services, INR 40-50 cr DAS projects, remainder IBS/network accessories/antenna
items.quote: Broadly, if you look at it, then in INR 205 crores, we will be doing about INR 30 crores of services, about INR 40-50 crores of projects, DAS projects. And the remaining is going to be our normal business which is IBS accessories and network accessories and antenna.

items.statement: Jio, Indus, Crest Digital, ACES added as new customers; Airtel remains largest at ~70%+ of FY24 revenue
items.quote: Yes. So last year, it was around 70% plus from them.

items.statement: Top 10 customers account for ~99% of revenue given small customer base of 10-12
items.quote: Look, we don't have too many customers, Tushar. Probably if you look at our total customers, they will be 10, 12 customers only, right? So, our revenues from top 10 customers, if you ask, maybe it's 99%.

items.statement: Unique Indian manufacturer of DAS/repeater products; competitors are Chinese/European/US brands facing national security certification headwinds
items.quote: The products that we manufacture are not manufactured by any other Indian manufacturer, whether it is HFCL or Tejas or any other business that you see or any Indian manufacturer that you see telecom manufacturer.

items.statement: Key global DAS competitors: CommScope (US), Solid (Korea), PROS Technologies; Frog now displacing them in projects
items.quote: Look, there are global companies like CommScope is from US, then there is a Korean company called Solid, whose equipment is deployed in Delhi Airport. There is a company called PROS Technologies whose equipment is deployed in, Bangalore Airport. So, these are the companies whose equipment has been going in the projects so far. And now we are taking over them.

items.statement: National Security Directive mandating certified equipment favors Frog as certified local manufacturer
items.quote: Today there is what you say regulation which is put by government on all the operators that any equipment that they are going to put in their network has to be National Security certified and that has changed a bit how the competition works. And that is helping a bit because we are national security certified as a company and our products as well.

items.statement: VHF repeater/DAS for railways in RDSO approval process; revenue contribution expected later in FY25 or FY26
items.quote: VHF product is there, but it will take it is in the approval process. And railway's RDSO approval process takes bit of lengthy process. So, we expect that to start adding to our revenues from later this financial year or maybe next financial year.

items.statement: Interference mitigation solution developed indigenously; awaiting operator deal conclusion, no order yet
items.quote: We are waiting for operator to conclude a deal. It is getting included in part of some other bigger network deal, which they are currently negotiating. So we are waiting and watching. So far there is no order to answer you, but it is expected sometime soon.

items.statement: H2 FY25 expected significantly better than H1; quarter-on-quarter growth from Q2 onward
items.quote: We expect ramp up to start from Q2 itself, but the H2 is going to be definitely much more significantly better than Q1 and Q2.

items.statement: Current order book of INR 81 crore to be fully executed within FY25; BMRCL and Noida Airport projects likely closed by Q3
items.quote: All of it will be completed within this financial year for sure. As I said that this order book also includes the 2 projects BMRCL and Noida Airport. So, these projects will be most likely closed within Q3.

items.statement: UK subsidiary GoRF formed; taking baby steps to explore Europe/US export opportunities for locally developed products
items.quote: For Go RF UK, the company is there the company is formed and we are looking for opportunities there. Not very proactively right now, we are taking some baby steps there. It is part of our larger plan whereby all these products that we have developed here, you plan to take them to Europe market as well as US market.

items.statement: Previous FY24 guidance of 40% growth cut to 20% due to project delays (BMRCL, Noida Airport) that have now materialized in Q1 FY25
items.quote: we initially had given guidance of 40%, which curtailed down to 20% later, and we managed around t hat. So why that has happened, w e were expecting these projects which we have secured now in Q1 this year, BMRCL and Noida airport. These projects we were expecting in the last financial year, which for some reasons got delayed and f inally came in Q1

items.statement: Increased hiring in Q4 FY24 and Q1 FY25 to build team for services and production for upcoming order requirements
items.quote: We are building up really our team for the services as well as production to cater to the new upcoming requirements that we have and we are seeing that the orders are already there and we are expecting few other large orders to cater to those requirements, we are building the team.

items.statement: DAS product deployed at Lucknow airport for 5 operators; reference site enabling Noida Airport win and future airport pipeline
items.quote: Our DAS product which is from Cellular, has been deployed in last quarter at Lucknow airport. 5 operators have been deployed and everything is running absolutely fine. As a follow-up of that, we have received this Noida Airport project also.

items.statement: TETRA coverage deployed at Chennai airport creating reference for public safety market
items.quote: Similarly in TETRA domain, we have deployed at Chennai airport, that opens up a significant market for us for TETRA.

items.statement: PLI recipient; government checking if PLI recipients want to enhance investment commitments for higher incentives
items.quote: we are al ready PLI recipients and now government is checking with all the PLI recipients if they are interested to enhance their investment payments, which will obviously enhance the incentives also

items.statement: Patent applications filed for proprietary technology where opportunities exist
items.quote: Yes, wherever we are getting that opportunity, we are patenting it. So, few patents we have already applied and so that work is on here.

items.statement: Domestic demand recovering driven by favorable monsoon and kharif sowing up ~10% YoY; export demand soft with oversupply from China keeping prices depressed
items.quote: In domestic markets, there is a positive sentiment primarily driven by monsoon prediction of IMD. There was a deficient rainfall till June '24 , that did impact first quarter in fiscal year '25 sales. But of late, monsoon has started really picking up well and the kharif sowing is registering significant growth of about 10% as compared to last year.

items.statement: Key crop acreages up significantly: Paddy +21%, Soyabean +30%, Maize +34%, Pigeon pea +191% YoY; cotton acreages down significantly in North due to pink bollworm
items.quote: If you look at key crops, Paddy is about 21% up, Soyabean about 30%, Maize 34% and pigeon pea about 191%. This is one crop that has seen a significant increase in acres driven by commodity prices. From field reports, what we are hearing, cotton acreages have reduced significantly in northern part of India, there's one particular pest called pink bollworm that has been bothering the farmers.

items.statement: Near-term outlook challenging for international business for next three months; domestic business positive with good rains and commodity prices; confident on medium-to-long-term growth
items.quote: In conclusion, I think near -term outlook for the business particularly international remains challenging at least for the next three months; however domestic business with the rain and the commodity prices being good is looking positive, we are very confident and optimistic about the overall growth prospect in the medium- to-long- term.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.96 crore (-13% YoY), gross contribution margin 30%, PAT Rs.48 crore vs Rs.63 crore YoY; margin compression from adverse mix (seeds down) and lower domestic/international margins vs history
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.96 crore; it is lower by about 13% compared to the same quarter last year with a gross contribution margin of 30% and PAT for the quarter stood at Rs.48 crore compared to the Rs.63crore reported during Q1 of fiscal year '24.

items.statement: International business not making negative margin; spreads compressed, margins lower than historical; Q1 EBITDA drop Rs.14 crore YoY, Rs.4 crore from seeds, Rs.10 crore from crop care largely international gross contribution drop
items.quote: See, gross margin has come down not because of international business making any negative margin. So, we did not make negative margin in the international business. We have mentioned in the earlier calls that we were taking swift actions in terms of liquidating old inventory. Overall, spreads has indeed compressed and hence the margins are lower than what we have made historically, but we have not

items.statement: Domestic price decline upwards of 10% YoY (14% in Q1); volume growth 13% led by herbicides and new launches; price declines in undifferentiated portfolio where brand share weak
items.quote: In domestic business, price decline was upwards of 10% and this is YoY decline, the QoQ decline has come down, but obviously because Q1 was on a higher price last year; it's 14%.

items.statement: International revenue Rs.133 crore (-5% YoY) with volume growth ~19% but price challenges impacting revenue; Acephate, Hexaconazole, Pendimethalin, Metribuzin prices muted, Metribuzin ~half of two years ago
items.quote: Coming back to International business, Revenues stood at Rs.133 crore, which is lower by 5% compared to the similar period last year, though we had a decent volume growth of about 19%, but the price challenge s are really impacting overall growth from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Capex envisaged in range of Rs.100 crore for the year; commissioned Water-Soluble Fertiliser Plant during the year; integrated R&D facility in Bangalore expected ready in two years
items.quote: We are also very prudent in CAPEX investment and envisage our expense would be in the range of Rs.100 crore.

items.statement: Seed supply constraints in hybrid maize and hybrid paddy (significant revenue contributors); North cotton hybrid Diggaz good volume growth despite lower acreage; South/West cotton liquidation to be watched
items.quote: So, if you see our business, the two areas where we had supply challenges primarily were hybrid maize as well as hybrid paddy. Subhra Gourisaria: So, North cotton actually we said we had very good momentum. South and West cotton we will have to yet see how the liquidation progresses, but it's not a big part of our portfolio. So, paddy and maize were the bigger dip for us

items.statement: Improving front-end capabilities on customer centricity theme; building connected organization leveraging digital for scale and closer customer access; 'Anubandh' program for channel visibility beyond distributor to retailer; expanding reta
items.quote: We are improving our front-end capabilities based on the theme of customer centricity . And as we work more on this, you will start hearing more about this as we move forward. Our endeavor will be to build a more connected organization leveraging digital. I think digital will give us a scale and that's where we will get closer to the customer.

items.statement: Healthy cash balance as of 30th June with no external borrowings
items.quote: We do have a very healthy cash balance as of 30th June as well, and with no external borrowings.

items.statement: Leadership changes underway to bring fresh thinking; rightsizing organization; investing in people as key pillar alongside R&D
items.quote: And the last but not the least is investment in people. I think we are moving; we are looking at some significant leadership changes wherever required to bring some fresh thinking and also looking at not only from the perspective of rightsizing the organization.

items.statement: Innovation Turnover Index (ITI) ambition to move to high teens; uptick seen in Q1; last 4 years contribution vs overall portfolio
items.quote: ITI is difficult to say because it's last four years contribution of it versus the overall portfolio and we do expect the overall portfolio to grow as well. Having said that, our ambition is certainly as we said earlier as well, that ITI should start moving to the high teens and which is where we are seeing an uptick happening in 1st Quarter as well.

items.statement: International pricing volatile, no visibility 10-11 months out; Acephate faces regulatory review risk; China oversupply continues capping prices; domestic technical prices creeping up MoM/QoQ may compress margins where brand strength weak
items.quote: What we see is, if you start splitting our business in segments, as I said, domestic formulation demand is looking good for the various factors I mentioned. Seed, the majority of our season is over. P rimarily the bulk of the business happens in kharif, and the only adjustment would be related to how much return comes versus what we have estimated. So, that adjustment you will see probably in the

items.statement: Strategy shifting to make-vs-buy decisions; partnerships and collaborations with global and domestic companies key for portfolio refresh; 'Mark Plus' 9(3) product launched in collaboration with a major; not pursuing everything in-house
items.quote: I think we are moving to a mindset to say we have to make a smart decision , make versus buy, in a world where so many supply chain and product partnerships are available. We have to be very prudent in making a decision. So, whatever is financially better, that's a decision we should make a nd obviously there's a point on supply chain certainty. So, our decisions are more going to be based on make

items.statement: Export pricing pressure: Metribuzin prices ~half of two years ago; Acephate, Hexaconazole, Pendimethalin prices muted; Baltic Dry Index doubled YoY increasing sea freight; domestic pricing product-specific, most products down YoY
items.quote: We have some old products like Acephate, Hexaconazole and Pendimethalin where prices continue to remain muted. Metri buzine prices actually are almost at the level of half compared to what they were two years ago. On top of that, sea freight has also seen steep hike as the Baltic Dry Index has doubled over last year, impacting margins.

items.statement: Export recovery soft in key markets (Brazil, US, SEA); volumes picking up but prices depressed due to China oversupply; Northern Hemisphere season may balance inventory; sequential price drops stabilized
items.quote: On the export front, recovery remains soft with the key markets like Brazil, US, SEA. So, while volumes have started picking up, prices continue to depress due to oversupply from China. We think with the ongoing season in the Northern Hemisphere including US, should lead to some balancing of the inventory and hopefully things will move start looking positively from there.

items.statement: Digital investments across 5-6 initiatives: SAP S/4 HANA ERP changeover, 'Drishti' AI/ML tool for farmer advisories, 'Anubandh' channel visibility, 'Seed-Say' AI/ML forecasting, customer-connect, manufacturing automation evaluation; digital
items.quote: So, if you look at all our digital spend actually you can categorize into five categories. One is obviously the back end is very, very important, which is SAP S4 HANA where we are going through complete changeover of our ERP system. That obviously takes time and money. On our other efficiency related, we are building a tool called “Drishti” and I think it has been talked about in the past and that

items.statement: Cooling products drove Q1 growth on favourable summer; consumer demand improvement uncertain, may be one-off
items.quote: Q1 posted good growth as cooling products capitalized on a favourable summer. Categories like air conditioners, fans and air coolers performed well as we leveraged our manufacturing capacities, brand strength and omni-channel presence to tap into the market opportunity.

items.statement: Consumer demand pickup seen but sustainability unclear; construction activity impacted by heat and elections
items.quote: So, some pickup is definitely there. And that's why this growth. For example, fans, yes summers was high, but fans is also a penetrated category. So, we believe something was there.

items.statement: Lloyd EBIT margin improved to 3.5% in Q1 from 2.8% in Q4; driven by premiumization, cost efficiencies, operating leverage
items.quote: Now what we are observing is for two quarters now, you have delivered, you're broken even. I think fourth quarter, you did almost 2.8% margins. In this quarter, you did around 3.5% margins.

items.statement: Switchgear contribution margin range 38-41% long-term; segment EBIT margin band 24-30%
items.quote: We have been in the range of between 40% -41% to around 37% -38%. So I think sometime in the quarter, this thing will happen. And look, we have investing in the business, there will always be some dilution in that, which is possible. We believe that the long -term range, which one should assume for this business is between 38% to sort of 41%.

items.statement: Overall A&P spend 3-3.5% of sales; Lloyd 4-4.5%, Havells 2.5%
items.quote: Overall, I think generally, Lloyd is between 4% and 4.5% and Havells is about 2.5%. So overall, it's about 3% to 3.5%.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR 800-900 crore on cash basis; FY26-27 INR 1,000-1,100 crore including new cable announcement; 30-40% for Cables & Wires
items.quote: I think we have already announced it last time . It's around INR800 -odd crores. So I think we continue to maintain that.

items.statement: FY26-27 capex INR 1,000-1,100 crore including INR 300 crore cable announcement; 30-40% for Cables & Wires
items.quote: Yes, and if we include about INR300 crores what we announced, INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores will be the overall capex if you include that. And yes, 30%-35% of that will be cable, maybe almost 40%.

items.statement: Tumkur cable facility awaiting final approvals, sales to start within Q2 FY25; expanding power cables for domestic and export
items.quote: We are just awaiting the final approvals for our sales to start happening from the new facility in Tumkur. So it should start within this quarter. And so that first phase of expansion is over. But we are continuing to add capacity, both for exports and for domestic segments and for a larger range of underground cables.

items.statement: Lloyd US UL approvals for full HVAC range expected in 12 months; cable approvals in 9-12 months
items.quote: Typically for the entire range, like we have already got one of the range approved, but I think the full range, which is required to tap the opportunity, I think we should set our target around 12 months from now.

items.statement: Cables & Wires: June saw heavy destocking due to commodity price decline; July returning to normal levels
items.quote: June was a particular month where suddenly there was a huge destocking because we had seen stocking in March-April-May period. In June, heavy destocking happened because of the raw material fluctuations. We are seeing July to be coming back to normal levels.

items.statement: Price hikes taken across categories in Q1 due to commodity inflation; no further hikes if raw material stays at current levels
items.quote: So as far as price increases are concerned, most of that has been done in many product categories, including Consumer Durables in the first quarter. So as long as this raw materials remain at this level, we've taken all the pricing actions as of now.

items.statement: Crabtree merged into Havells Crabtree brand; Standard, REO, Lloyd to remain independent brands
items.quote: So all switching solutions from the Havells brand are now termed as Havells Crabtree. And Crabtree because of the legacy brand of the switches, so we'll continue with that brand for all switching solutions from us. But whether it is Standard, REO and Lloyd, they will continue to remain as independent brands even in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Export aspiration ~10% of revenue over time; US JVs initiated, also targeting SAARC, AMESA, Europe, Australia
items.quote: Over a period time, may be around 10% of our business should come from international. But that's an aspiration. I mean we are not holding out any medium -term targets for that. But our opportunity is definitely there, and I think it's something which can be leveraged by us.

items.statement: Inventory at 63 days; scope for improvement but seasonality and unpredictability require buffer
items.quote: Everybody wants to improve on that, but you have to balance the growth and the inventory. Also, a lot of this has been increased over a period of time because of addition of Lloyd as a business which has a lot of seasonality.

items.statement: Lloyd AC contribution ~85-87% of Lloyd revenue in Q1; non-AC categories growing well
items.quote: So non-AC categories, you see in this quarter, obviously AC is dominating almost 85% -87%. And as we always maintained, and we mentioned earlier in the call also, that we see Lloyd is a journey, so I think the journey will cover the other product categories as well.

items.statement: Switchgear segment EBIT margin band 24-30%; contribution margin 38-41%
items.quote: I would say these are decent margins. And just looking at the nature of the industry investments, we made like somebody said, Havells Crabtree as a brand. I think we also need to invest behind the brand. So overall, I think, again, this has been between 24% to 28% - 30%. So I think that's the band we expect to maintain.

items.statement: Consumer demand recovery uncertain; prolonged weakness for 3-3.5 years across industries
items.quote: As you say, ECD is a portfolio. So there are multiple levers. Fan has gone through its own journey of transition to BEE rating and things like that. The underlying trend also has been the weak consumer demand. And I think this is not just playing out in ECD. It 's also playing out if you look at related categories across industries as well.

items.statement: No specific margin or growth guidance given; Lloyd profitability journey long-term with continued investments
items.quote: I would not give any number associated, as you are probably asking me on this call. But I would say that one, there will be improved price realization and reduced costs over a longer period of time as well as growth will be a major driver for Lloyd for us.

items.statement: Open to inorganic opportunities but will evaluate on pricing, capital deployment, returns; no rush
items.quote: I think, look, there is no best or worst time for these kind of opportunities. We will have to evaluate them as they come. And it's not that we have not evaluated in the past. But frankly, they have to make sense on the pricing, on the capital deployment and that returns thereon. So we'll always be open to this.

items.statement: Investing in talent pool for Lloyd; brand building and R&D investments continuing
items.quote: we continue to strengthen our market position with investments into brand building, di fferentiated offerings and talent pool

items.statement: Switchgear competitive intensity stable long-term; national players like Gold Medal, Norisys, Schneider, Legrand are premium priced
items.quote: Well, I think the increased competitive intensity or similar competitive intensity has been there for quite some time. And when you say local players, I don't know how you calculate, how you're taking national players like even Gold Medal or Norisys or Schneider and Legrand as regional players. They're not regional players. They are national players. And I believe that they are also premium priced

items.statement: Raw material prices increased over last few months; corrective pricing actions taken
items.quote: We've already said that there have been some increases in raw material prices over the last few months and corrective pricing actions have already been taken.

items.statement: Channel inventory for ACs low; stock-out situation in industry this summer
items.quote: Channel inventory is not there. Actually, you are aware there are a lot of manufacturers and the channels that were running out of the inventory. So there's not much inventory at the channel.

items.statement: Fans performed very well in Q1; kitchen appliances gaining traction; outreach to smaller towns and villages
items.quote: Fans have done very well in this quarter.

items.statement: Lloyd capex ~INR 100 crore out of total INR 1,100 crore; most capacity already in place
items.quote: Out of which, Lloyd is lower because most of the capacity is there and only about INR100 crores are for Lloyd.

items.statement: Management targets operating EBITDA margin of 16.5%-17% in H2 FY25 and aims to exit FY25 at that level.
items.quote: we definitely want to operate closer to that 16.5%, 17% type of margin in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain the Q1 top-line revenue momentum in the remaining quarters of FY25.
items.quote: We feel that the healthy kind of top line revenue momentum will continue.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operating EBITDA margin was 15.2%, down 80 bps QoQ due to one-time hits including US project ramp delays and Middle East PDD.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter was at 15.2%, a decline of 80 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: US geography EBIT margin dropped to 3% in Q1 from 9% in Q4 due to holding resources for delayed project starts; management targets double-digit US margins in H2 FY25.
items.quote: we believe we'll come back to a double-digit margin profile in the current year.

items.statement: 12-month order book backlog flat QoQ but up 23% YoY; Q1 typically slower for order book but pipeline building is strong.
items.quote: Our 12 months order book backlog, while it was flat quarter-on-quarter, increased 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Capacity utilization ~80%, Chennai TBR capacity coming online end of Q2

items.statement: International order base strong, double-digit export growth expected for FY25
items.quote: Our order base looks strong and the growth is coming from desired focused markets of Latin America, Europe and progressively, it will also come from US.
