items.statement: FY25 net screen addition target of 50 screens (120 gross additions, 70 exits)
items.quote: For FY '25, the company expects to open 120 new screens and exit 70 screens resulting in a net addition of 50 new screens.

items.statement: Implementing capital-light growth model by partnering with developers for joint capex investment
items.quote: As guided last quarter, we are been selective in new screen additions and gradually implementing a capital-light growth model by partnering with developers and jointly investing in new screen capex.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by 13% fewer releases and only 3 blockbusters vs 7 last year due to general elections
items.quote: This prompted many producers to postpone film releases, resulting in a 13% drop in the number of releases in the quarter as compared to the first quarter of last year.

items.statement: Strong content pipeline visible for Q2 onwards with major releases across languages including Pushpa 2 in December
items.quote: With Kalki's spill over and the visibility of a great lineup ahead across the languages, Q2 has started off on a great note.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA loss of INR20 crore and PAT loss of INR137 crore vs EBITDA of INR100 crore and PAT loss of INR44 crore last year
items.quote: Total revenues for the quarter was INR1,209 crores. EBITDA loss was INR20 crores and PAT loss of INR137 crores as compared to revenues of INR1,324 crores, EBITDA of INR100 crores and PAT loss of INR44 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: Ticket prices increased ~4% but ATP declined 5% due to lack of blockbuster films
items.quote: We did pass on the inflation-led increase in ticket prices to the customers. So in fact, the ticket prices were increased by about 4%.

items.statement: Opened 50 new screens, exited 14, net addition of 36 screens in Q1; portfolio at 1,754 screens across 361 cinemas
items.quote: the company opened 50 new screens and exited 14 underperforming screens resulting in a net addition of 36 screens during the quarter.

items.statement: Premium formats at 15% of screens; new additions to have 15-20% premium/special format screens
items.quote: Almost 15% of our screens are premium and special format screens, which includes premium large formats, including IMAX, 4DX, et cetera.

items.statement: Re-releases contributed ~12 lakh admissions in Q1; building dedicated team for curated film festivals
items.quote: this quarter, we contributed close to about 12 lakh admissions coming in from the re-releases itself.

items.statement: PVR INOX Passport 2.0 sold 2.5 lakh passports in Q1 despite weak content
items.quote: We launched the PVR INOX Passport 2.0 on March 18th and have seen a tremendous response to the revised program. Even in a quarter as impacted as Q1, we sold 2.5 lakh passports.

items.statement: Karnataka 1-2% cess media report not confirmed as government order; industry engaging with authorities
items.quote: this is a media report. We've been in touch with the government officers. We reached out to the relevant mini stry. And so far, there is no confirmation that this is a definitive government

items.statement: South India regional movie share lower due to higher single screen penetration; 35-40% of new screens planned in South
items.quote: The answer is yes. The penetration of single screens is more in South.

items.statement: Monetizing non-core office assets for deleveraging; first bids received, expect INR300-350 crore from two assets in 3-4 months
items.quote: So about 300 to 350 is what we believe it shall be the capital values of the two assets.

items.statement: JV with Devyani International registered as Devyani PVR INOX Food Court Ltd; brand 'Treat Junction'; 2 food courts operational in 2-3 months, 4-5 by FY25 end
items.quote: We've also finalized a brand name for the food court that will be set up in the shopping malls. We will be calling it Treat Junction as a brand for all the food courts.

items.statement: Advertising revenue grew ~5% YoY driven by Kalki and off-screen sponsorships; expect growth in Q2/Q3 with bigger releases
items.quote: Overall, as well, we looked at not only on-screen, but offscreen sponsorship deals with certain clients where we were playing classics and rereleases. So because of all of that effort, the team was able to deliver this 5% growth.

items.statement: Fixed cost up 7% YoY; same-store fixed cost up 2.5%; rental escalation 3.7% on same cinemas
items.quote: if you look at our total fixed cost, it has gone up by 7% compared to last year quarter 1. And if we further break that down into like-for-like same-store basis, the same-store growth is only about 2.5%.

items.statement: Content pipeline fully back to pre-COVID levels expected by next financial year; Q2-Q4 strong due to Q1 spillovers
items.quote: we believe that we have scope to get better. Fortunately, Q2, Q3 and Q4 is looking fairly strong also partly because a lot of films, which were coming in Q1 were pushed to Q2 or Q3.

items.statement: Theatrical window harmonization discussions ongoing with producers; consensus for consistency but no timeline; 8-week window for Hindi/English, 4-week for South
items.quote: On windows for Hindi, English and a few other languages, including Punjabi, we follow 8-week window. For the South region, it varies, but it typically tends to be a minimum 4 weeks.

items.statement: New screens typically reach cinema-level EBITDA breakeven within 6-9 months; majority of year-old screens profitable
items.quote: Typically, they start becoming profitable at EBITDA level -- at cinema EBITDA level within 6 to 9 months of opening.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue guidance of INR1,400-1,500 crores, EBITDA of INR230-260 crores, and exit Q4 EBITDA of INR80-90 crores (20-22% margin).
items.value: Revenue INR1,400-1,500 cr; EBITDA INR230-260 cr; Exit Q4 EBITDA INR80-90 cr
items.quote: We continue to reaffirm our guidance for our outlook for our full year. We expect revenues to be in the range of INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores, with our EBITDA in the range of INR230 crores to INR260 crores and with an exit Q4 EBITDA expected to be in the INR80 crores to INR90 crores level, approximately 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped due to inventory reduction but expected to return to 48% in H2 FY25.
items.quote: So, we said you should estimate that our gross margins will get back to 48% in H2.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR160 crores in Q1 (INR40 crores from free cash); target year-end net debt under INR500 crores and debt/EBITDA under 2x.
items.value: Debt reduction INR160 cr; Target net debt <INR500 cr; Debt/EBITDA <2x
items.quote: We have reduced debt by about INR160 crores, almost INR40 crores of that coming from free cash generation through the quarter. With a targeted further cash debt reduction from cash flows, we expect end of the year debt adjusted for the uncalled money of the rights to be under INR500 crores and significantly better than our Debt to EBITDA guidance of under 3 times, we should be now comfortably guid

items.statement: Vizag facility retrofit capex amount not finalized; will be funded internally without additional borrowing; update expected next quarter.
items.quote: We don't have the exact numbers as the work is being conducted by consultants. So, we will probably be able to update that in the next quarter. But we would not need to borrow any additional monies to achieve this.

items.statement: Regulated markets revenue share back to 75%+; CRAMS currently 5-8% of revenue, targeting ~10% next year.
items.quote: Well, at this time, we are still in the 5% to 8% range. But based on our confidence and RFP that we expect this to be to grow to about 10% in the next year.

items.statement: Ibuprofen pricing has come down but inventory normalized; Pondicherry facility fully utilized at ~5,000 tons; Vizag retains 3,000-ton ibuprofen block.
items.quote: To answer your specific point on pricing, the pricing has come down, but we do not operate in that market where there is intense competition. And the urge for us to do that earlier and which also caused a lot of trouble for us has been removed by the fact that we have shut the tap from the Vizag facility.

items.statement: Biosecure Act relevant only to biologics, not small molecules; sustained low crude prices expected to improve margins.
items.quote: As the law correctly calls itself The Biosecurity Act, this is only relevant to biologics, and it is not so relevant to

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA INR50 crores (14% margin) vs reported INR42 crores; difference due to non-recurring Vizag/R&D costs.
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA reported is INR50 crores against a reported EBITDA of INR42 crores. And the reason for this is mainly because part of our network optimization, you would have probably seen in our deck that was released today, we have mothballed our vizag facility.

items.statement: Significant number of CRAMS RFPs issued; expecting conversion of some major programs during the year.
items.quote: We are seeing now with a renewed focus on our CRAMS operations, a significant number of RFPs that we have issued. And we hope that during the year, we would have achieved success with some of these major programs.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 target of ₹20,000 crore revenue; new mid-term guidance to be released this fiscal year
items.quote: We had this target of reaching ₹20,000 crores of top-line by FY26. We exited the previous year at a top-line of about ₹18,000 crores. And that is where we believe that we should be either able to achieve or beat the guidance ahead of its time.

items.statement: International business target of 10% revenue contribution by FY26 maintained
items.quote: As part of the Project Leap, we target to reach 10% of contribution from international business for FY26.

items.statement: Capex guidance of ₹1,000-1,100 crore for FY25 maintained, likely towards higher end
items.quote: We are on track to do the capex on our guided range of ₹1,000 crores to ₹1,100 crores for the year. We believe it should be more towards the higher end of that range.

items.statement: FMEG advertising spend guided at 3-5% of B2C top-line annually
items.quote: At an annual level, our advertising and promotion spends will continue to be within our guided range of 3% to 5% of the B2C top-line.

items.statement: EPC business long-term margin guided at high single digits; contribution at mid-to-high single digits of consolidated revenue
items.quote: We've always guided that within the EPC business, the margin profile in the long term will be in high single digits. And that is something that we'll continue to guide the market. As far as the contribution to the company's top line is concerned, we believe that the contribution will range somewhere between mid to high single digits going ahead.

items.statement: Wires & Cables long-term EBITDA margin guided at 11-13%, currently achieving 12-14%
items.quote: See, our guided range on cables & wires for the long term is 11% to 13%. But we also think that because as of now, we are realizing better operating leverage, we should be able to generate somewhere between 12% to 14% at EBITDA level.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to normalize to 50-55 days; inventory days around 100 days
items.quote: Generally at a working capital day view, we believe 50 days to 55 days of working capital days is what is an optimum working capital cycle for us. Within that, the inventory days will be somewhere closer to about 100 days.

items.statement: Domestic Wires & Cables volume grew ~10% YoY in Q1 FY25 on high base
items.quote: The domestic Wires & Cables business registered a volume growth of about 10% while the value growth, because of the increased commodity prices, was there but to a large extent, it was negated because of the effect it had on sales.

items.statement: FMEG grew 21% YoY driven by fan demand from heatwave; fans hit highest quarterly sales in years
items.quote: FMEG business recorded solid growth of 21% this quarter, driven by strong demand for fans due to heatwave across several parts of the country. The fan business achieved its highest quarterly sales in the past couple of years.

items.statement: International business declined 28% YoY due to demand softness in largest geography and model transition
items.quote: Meanwhile, our international business registered a 28% year on year decline, resulting into a contraction in its contribution to the Company's top-line. Further, elevated freight costs compressed the margins in this business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 12.4% in Q1 FY25, down from prior year due to mix shift to lower-margin EPC and institutional sales, and lower international contribution
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 6% year on year, with EBITDA margins at 12.4%. The notable decline in EBITDA margins was influenced by a shift in our business mix towards segments with lower margins.

items.statement: Wires & Cables domestic EBITDA margin normally 9-11%; international higher; Q1 impacted by commodity volatility and channel destocking
items.quote: On our domestic business, generally, we make EBITDA margins somewhere between 9% to 11%. And on our international business, the margin profile is a bit better. But this is what plays out in a normal scenario.

items.statement: FMEG losses narrowing due to lower ad spend and better mix from switchgear and conduit pipes; targeting EBITDA breakeven near term
items.quote: In terms of profitability, we've seen a decline in losses, attributed to lower advertising costs, and boosted by higher contributions from switchgears and conduit pipes & fittings product segments.

items.statement: Wires business EBITDA margin 15-16% when commodity stable; domestic cables 9-11%; international higher than wires
items.quote: Within B2C, the wires business is a better margin business. So generally, when the commodity prices are stable, we make somewhere between 15% to 16% at EBITDA level on the wires business, whereas on domestic cables, we generally make between 9% to 11%. International businesses is again much higher margin business.

items.statement: EPC order book robust driven by government RDSS scheme; execution driving 292% revenue growth
items.quote: Going ahead, we have a pretty good order book. And that's largely because of the RDSS scheme of the government.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex ₹280 crore; on track for full-year guidance of ₹1,000-1,100 crore
items.quote: During the first quarter, we've done capex of about ₹280 crores. So, we are on track to do the capex on our guided range of ₹1,000 crores to ₹1,100 crores for the year.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility in Q1: copper up 15% mid-Mar to mid-Apr, up 11% mid-Apr to mid-May, down 12% mid-May to mid-Jun
items.quote: From mid-March to mid-April, it went up by almost 15%, mid-April to mid-May up by almost 11% and from mid-May to mid-June went down by almost 12%.

items.statement: Wires & Cables revenue mix ~75% cables, 25% wires in Q1 FY25; similar to FY24; cables outgrowing wires
items.quote: cables would have contributed closer to 75% whereas wires would have contributed closer to 25%. Ashish Jain: And what is this number for FY24? Chirayu Upadhyaya: Again, similar, just a few bps lower. So again, as we mentioned, even in this quarter the cables have outgrown wires

items.statement: FMEG mix: fans and lights 50-55%; switches & switchgears high-teens; conduit pipes & fittings high-teens; others single digits
items.quote: As far as the mix is concerned, the fans and lights both of them are the larger contributors within the FMEG segment contributing somewhere between 50% and 55% of the FMEG top-line. Switches and switchgears would contribute in high-teens. A similar contribution will be from conduit pipes and fittings.

items.statement: Institutional sales outpaced channel in Wires & Cables due to back-to-back pricing insulating from commodity volatility
items.quote: In institutional orders, we have back-to-back pricing, so we don't get largely affected because of this volatility in commodity prices. And that is why the orders that we have taken in the past 3 to 6 months and where we had to supply cables, those are something that we continued to supply.

items.statement: No material change in country preference for non-Indian players in US market; slowdown due to distribution model transition
items.quote: There has been no material change as far as any preference for particular country players are concerned. We don't believe there is any such sentiment that the country is preferring players from other countries.

items.statement: Income tax matter: no tax demand notice or orders received; cooperating with authorities
items.quote: Even as on the present date, we have not received any tax demand notice or any other orders from the income tax authorities. Having said that, it goes without saying, that we are fully committed and we will cooperate with the income tax authorities as far as their procedure is concerned.

items.statement: Board reconstituted Audit and NRC committees to comprise only independent directors, exceeding legal requirements
items.quote: Both these committees will now fully comprise of Independent Directors, in-line with globally accepted best governance practices. This change underscores our commitment to maintaining transparency, accountability, and integrity in our corporate governance framework.

items.statement: International business model transition in US will take few more quarters to stabilize; freight costs elevated but expected to ease
items.quote: It will still take us a bit of time as far as the geography that we're discussing is concerned, will take us a few more quarters. It's a large geography. And we'll have to have enough distribution in place.

items.statement: India Ratings improved credit rating outlook to 'positive' from 'on watch with negative implication'
items.quote: India Ratings has improved the outlook on our credit rating to 'positive' from the earlier 'on watch with negative implication'.

items.statement: Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin of 13%-13.5% for FY25
items.quote: as Mr. Chari said this is what at least for the current year, this is what we are seeing, 13%-13.5% will play between these two numbers.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning business targeting Rs. 250 crore revenue in FY25
items.quote: Institutional cleaning chemical this year, we are expecting it to be Rs. 250 crore, the 1st Quarter was about Rs. 60 crore.

items.statement: Export revenue target of 25%-30% of total revenue over next 2 years
items.quote: I think we would be happy if the exports absolute number keeps growing and if it's within this 25%-30% kind of range I think for the next 2 years, that's what is our target number.

items.statement: Cash CAPEX outflow of ~Rs. 100 crore planned for FY25
items.quote: Overall, we will have an outflow of close to about Rs. 100 crore.

items.statement: Dahej expansion adding 20,000 tons HPPC capacity and 30,000 MT ethoxylation capacity by year-end
items.quote: The expansion includes adding 20,000 tons of capacity for products related to HP PC in the specialty chemicals space, as well as producing ingredients for our subsidiary companies. Additionally, to cater to the growing demand in the a gro, home and personal care, oil and gas and pharma sector, we are adding Ethoxylation capacities of 30,000 MT at Dahej facility of Unitop.

items.statement: Ethoxylation utilization at 90%+ at Tristar and Unitop; overall average utilization 55%-60%
items.quote: On the ethoxylation which is our core activity, our plants are working at almost 90%, and overall if we take an average, we are at about 55%-60%.

items.statement: Home textile orders from US market are full for current financial year
items.quote: the home textile business is now on upswing in India, orders are good with our home textile exporters especially for the US A market. So, we are confident of better sales i n the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 13.3% vs 14.1% YoY due to higher other expenses
items.quote: Our EBITDA has improved by 12.5% to Rs. 64.9 crore from Rs. 57.7 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 13.3% compared to 14.1% in the previous year. The drop in EBITDA margin was primarily due to increase in other expenses, mainly driven by higher freight, travel, maintenance and selling and distribution costs.

items.statement: Institutional cleaning business margins slightly below company average; operating leverage expected at Rs. 500-600 crore revenue
items.quote: maybe closer to Rs. 500-600 crore kind of top line is when this business will really start showing some positive traction and post that I think it will really bump up our margin.

items.statement: Healthy demand in both domestic and export markets for HPPC and Textile segments
items.quote: Both the markets we see healthy demand both domestic and in exports. As I said earlier, the home textile markets especially from the US, the orders are full with our current customers in India and also in Bangladesh. W e should see higher sales in both these countries with other countries also. In the HPPC segment, again, we see exports and the domestic market b oth having good demand.

items.statement: Prices stable overall; slight price cuts taken to drive volumes
items.quote: Prices are more or less stable now. There are some places where we have taken slight price cuts just to get into the volume game, but overall prices seem to be stable now.

items.statement: Freight costs up 35-40% YoY in Q1; stabilizing recently
items.quote: if you see YoY it would have definitely increased about 35%-40% of what it was in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Exports at 24-25% of revenue in Q1 FY25, up from 20% YoY; absolute export revenue grew ~50% YoY
items.quote: if you see overall the business itself is growing, so it's growing both on the domestic as well as on the exports. But if you see, I think, last year Q1 our exports would have been 20% of our revenue. Today, this quarter it's almost 24%-25%. But if you see in value terms, at least 50% growth.

items.statement: New distributor appointed in Bangladesh; 6-person sales team on ground
items.quote: We have a team of people present there, we have now a new distributor and we think that progressively we should see better traction in sales from Bangladesh than in the previous quarters.

items.statement: Dubai subsidiary incorporated for global expansion; may set up marketing and manufacturing facilities
items.quote: We incorporated the subsidiary in Dubai primarily for any global expansion that we may plan going forward. So, rather than holding it through India, we currently incorporated this subsidiary. Any new set up which we may plan to do in any other country, we would like to do it through this Dubai subsidiary.

items.statement: Working capital unchanged from March; expecting release of funds by September
items.quote: Working capital is pretty much the same as what it was in March. We have taken some steps. Hopefully by September we should see some release of funds coming out of working capital.

items.statement: 90-100 days working capital cycle is new normal post acquisitions
items.quote: And as we said in the last 2 earnings call, between 90-100 days is a new normal which we should consider.

items.statement: Launched esters, cocoamidopropyl betaines, CDEA, biosurfactants, silicone block polymers in-house
items.quote: In the HPPC segment, we have introduced a lot of esters in the last couple of quarters. So, all these products which were in the R&D stage, they have been launched both in the market as well as raw materials for Unitop. So, most of these esters were being outsourced by Unitop. Now, they are being manufactured in-house at our Rossari Dahej plant so that project has taken off very well, like the SMO

items.statement: HPPC segment revenue grew 21% YoY to Rs. 365 crore (75% of total); TSC grew 21% to Rs. 98 crore (20%); AHN flat at Rs. 27 crore (5%)
items.quote: Our HPPC division saw robust growth of 21% YoY during the quarter, reaching Rs. 365 crore compared to Rs. 301 crore. The Textile Specialty Chemicals division also grew by 21%, up to Rs. 98 crore from Rs. 81 crore. AHN division experienced muted performance, with the revenues at Rs. 27 crore in Q1 FY25 compared to Rs. 29 crore last year. In terms of revenue contribution this quarter, HPPC leads wit

items.statement: GST penalty notice of Rs. 25 crore appealed; no provision made as management expects favorable outcome
items.quote: No, there will not be any provision. That's an order which has been passed, as per the department it's an IGST refund, which they claim to be erroneous. We have taken proper legal views on the order which has come, and we are now going to appeal against this order with the higher authority of commissioner appeal, and we are quite hopeful of getting a favorable order on this.

items.statement: Container shortage and shipping delays due to China diverting containers to EV shipments; freight rates 2-3x higher
items.quote: There are also delays because vessels are not available, containers are not available. So, normal shipping times have increased. Now, what is happening is when containers reach late to the customers, they consume late and then the next orders get delayed, and the customers want to try out some other suppliers from where they can get the container early. Overall, I think the whole world is grapplin

items.statement: Employee expenses up 17% YoY, 14% QoQ due to hiring and increments; not one-off
items.quote: s not a one-off increase. T here we have gotten people through between last year and current year and of course there has been general increments that had happened

items.statement: Cross-selling between Rossari, Unitop and Tristar increasing; new capacities will manufacture inputs for subsidiaries
items.quote: As it is, having a lot of cross-selling, this is only going to go up now over the year. So, it would be ideal to look at the EBITDA margin at a consolidated level, and as Mr. Chari said this is what at least for the current year, this is what we are seeing, 13%-13.5% will play between these two numbers.

items.statement: Other expenses up due to Rs. 3-4 crore one-offs: Tristar plant shutdown (12-15 days), HR consulting, higher freight, exhibitions, travel
items.quote: Yes, this quarter we have about Rs. 3-4-ish crore of one-off expenses that has got booked. One of it is on the maintenance side, in Tristar, we had a plant shut down for about 12 to 15 days. So, that's where the maintenance costs have gone up. We had a shutdown at the T ristar facility. So, we have some expenses booked on the maintenance side during this quarter. And we have also initiated in the

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 18-22% with ~13% EBITDA margin and 50-75% cash conversion from EBITDA
items.quote: In terms of FY '25 guidance, we expect our revenue growth to be in the 18% to 22% band with approximately 13% EBITDA margin. The free cash generation for the business should improve meaningfully during the year and we expect the cash conversion from EBITDA to be within the 50% to 75% band.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio maintained at up to 20% of consolidated PAT for FY25
items.quote: Some of these proposed acquisitions may not warrant significant capital to be deployed, hence shall continue to maintain a similar dividend payout ratio of up to 20% of our consolidated PAT for FY'25.

items.statement: Proximus Opal completed 83.1% stake acquisition; synergies with TeleSign and Microsoft partnership underway
items.quote: During the quarter gone by, Proximus Opal completed the acquisition of 83.1% stake in Route Mobile. This acquisition will help Route Mobile in entering mature markets like USA and Europe, expand its product portfolio, and unlock synergies with TeleSign.

items.statement: Vodafone Idea firewall deal went live in April 2024; targeting Rs 500 crore incremental revenue in FY25
items.quote: Route Mobile's largest firewall deal with Vodafone Idea went live in April '24. There were a few teet hing issues during the month of April, which was resolved during that month

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross profit margin expanded to 22.1% vs 21.4% YoY; EBITDA margin 12.5% vs 11.8% QoQ
items.quote: In terms of direct margin, after adjusting for non -cash impact of Rs. 38.8 million related to refundable security deposit provided to an MNO, which has been amortized and booked under purchase account under I ndAS 109, g ross profit margin expanded to 22.1% as compared to 21.4% in Q1 '24 and 21.8% in Q4 '24

items.statement: Direct margin growth expected to be slightly better than revenue growth due to new products; RPT may be dilutive to direct margin but accretive at EBIT level
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be able to maintain this. And because of the new products, as Rajdip said, we will be able to also expand it. The only thing that, Ronak, I will just call out here is, it also is a function of the related party transactions. Some of these related part y transactions may be a little dilutive, I mean, from a direct margin and EBITDA standpoint. But it would be, I mean, accreti

items.statement: Stopped capitalizing TruSense digital identity project at Masivian; expensed Rs 14.5 million employee cost; remaining intangible capex ~USD 1 million/year for 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We also stopped capitalizing the digital identity project, TruSense, at Masivian. The employee cost amounting to Rs. 14.5 million with respect to such capitalization was expensed out during the quarter.

items.statement: Normalized cash flow conversion from EBITDA stood at 110% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The normalized cash flow conversion from EBITDA stood at 110%, you may refer to Slide 17 of the earnings presentation.

items.statement: Refundable security deposit of Rs 38.8 million amortized under IndAS 109 for firewall deal; advance to supplier to be consumed by Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: This is for the security deposit that we have given for our firewall deal, and that security deposit essentially is being treated under IndAS 109 accounting standards, and hence there is a non-cash charge to the purchase account.

items.statement: Average realization per billable transaction declined to Rs 0.30 from Rs 0.33 YoY due to higher domestic India volumes; sequentially stable at Rs 0.30
items.quote: Average realization per billable transaction declined to Rs. 0.30 compared to Rs. 0.33 in Q1 FY '24 due to increase in domestic volumes in India. Sequentially, it remained stable at Rs. 0.30.

items.statement: Global CPaaS market growing at low single-digits; Route Mobile guiding 18-22% growth; ILD volumes face headwinds in high-price markets but domestic use cases growing multi-fold
items.quote: Amit, I think see, at least when the entire CPaaS market is growing at lower single-digit, like, we as a company giving 18% to 22% still is one of the best guidance we are giving based on certain clear ideas we have about pipeline.

items.statement: Promoter holding at 83%+ post open offer; one year to reduce to 75% minimum public shareholding via block deals or OFS
items.quote: Pursuant to the open offer, the promoter's shareholding actually increased to 83+% and we have a stipulated timeframe of one year to bring it back to the minimum public shareholding of 75%.

items.statement: Non-cash FOREX translation loss of Rs 119 million in Q1 FY25; UK taxed at 25%, UAE tax implementation increased effective tax rate to 21%
items.quote: In terms of the other operating overheads, there were non-operating non-cash FOREX translation loss of Rs. 119 million and one-time cost of Rs. 8.6 million incurred for seeking expert opinions on transfer pricing for the related-party transactions with the Proximus Group and for the mandatory tender offer.

items.statement: Employee benefit expenses up 27% QoQ due to annual increments, one-off retention incentives, and TruSense capitalization stop; net headcount +1 (61 joined, 60 left); monthly run rate ~Rs 20-21 crore
items.quote: In terms of the operating overheads, there were significant increases in workforce cost, that is the employee benefit expenses increased by around 27% on a sequential basis. It includes the annual increments and certain one-off incentives paid to employees for retention, and to reward them for the exhaustive integration work done by the team to reap the synergies from the group.

items.quote: And with that perspective in our margins, we would like to, we still keep an outlook of decently between 7% to 8% margin percentage.

items.statement: Optimistic demand outlook driven by GDP growth, e-commerce and infrastructure improvement
items.quote: We are optimistic. We see as the GDP growth rates improve, the e-commerce, the infrastructure improves, we see healthy prospects.

items.statement: General price increase of 3.9-4% implemented across products selectively based on contracts
items.quote: We have had our general price increases. Of course, it is not to the expected budgeted level what we had, but roughly be tween 3.9% to 4% is the additional revenue that comes from

items.statement: Fuel cost neutralized via variable surcharge linked to Brent crude in customer contracts
items.quote: So, typically, our customers, our customer contracts have a fuel surcharge clause, which percentage increases or decreases based on the global Brent oil prices.

items.statement: No one-off costs in Q1; current costs expected to generate revenue or efficiencies in upcoming quarters
items.quote: It's a normal quarter a nd we expect those, against those costs, the additional revenue or efficiencies to be generated

items.statement: Merit increases of ~4% YoY and ~4.5-4.6% QoQ impacted margins
items.quote: So, normal merit increase roughly would be, we will have to, you know, it is roughly, you know, 4% Y-o-Y, you know, quarter-on-quarter increase, ma'am.

items.statement: Shipments grew 7.4% QoQ to 90.15 million; weight grew 9.6% QoQ to 313,089 tons
items.quote: Overall in terms of shipments, last quarter , it was 83.94 million shipments. This quarter, it is 90.15 million. In terms of weight, it is 285,643 tons in June 23 quarter. And it is 313,089 weight in tons in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Facing tough competition in surface express; aim for profitable growth with pricing flexibility for key customers
items.quote: On the surface part, we are growing more on the surface and on the surface, we are facing a very tough competition.

items.statement: Rate per shipment up 2.1% YoY; revenue per kg down 0.7% YoY
items.quote: Overall, at RPS, RPK level versus the previous year quarter, we are seeing a marginal growth on the RPS part and RPK slightly down. However, rate for shipment has increased by 2.1%, whereas RPK is 0.7% down.

items.statement: Margin expansion dependent on optimum aircraft utilization and domestic demand; no forward-looking statements provided
items.quote: We had said that, provided, we are able to generate that m uch level of, provided we go for an optimum utilization. I think that's the one. A is that, we do not make any forward -looking statement.

items.statement: FY25 revenue and PAT growth target of 30% each
items.quote: Yes, our growth is same pattern as always communicated we will achieve 30% top line and 30% bottom line we will achieve this year too.

items.statement: FY25 content investment budget of Rs 80 crore
items.quote: Around 80 crore you can assume will be a content investment.

items.statement: FY25 target of 300 song releases with focus on quality
items.quote: we have already released 100 songs approximately and our target is, this year it will be 300, but our target is to go for a quality

items.statement: Content cost to remain 28-30% of revenue
items.quote: We have changed our content acquisition strategy. And accordingly, you will see fewer releases from Tips our content expense will remain approximately 28% to 30% of revenues.

items.statement: Net profit margin expected to be similar to last year's range
items.quote: Ravi it would be similar range of the last year.

items.statement: 97 new songs added in Q1 FY25 (79 non-film, 18 film)
items.quote: We have added 97 new songs to our music library as of Q1 FY25. Among these 79 belong to non- film music, and 18 belong to film music.

items.statement: FY25 film release target of 15-20 movies including regional
items.quote: we target that we want to release music first to release at least 15, 20 movies including regional so that is our target to release every year.

items.statement: FY25 pipeline: 3-4 Hindi films and 10-12 regional films
items.quote: Three to four Hindi and around 10 to 12 films regional.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operating EBITDA Rs 54.4 crore, up 55% YoY; PAT Rs 43.6 crore, up 61% YoY; PAT margin 58.9%
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA for the quarter reached Rs.54.4 crores showing a year-on-year growth of 55%. Furthermore, our PAT for the quarter was at Rs.43.6 crores reflecting a notable increase of 61%. The PAT margin for the quarter is 58.9%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 content cost Rs 12.7 crore vs Rs 12.2 crore YoY
items.quote: Our content cost for the quarter stood at Rs.12.7 crores as compared to Rs.12.2 crores in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue Rs 73.9 crore, up 40% YoY driven by YouTube, Spotify, JioSaavn
items.quote: The Company has reported revenues of Rs.73.9 crores in Q1 FY25. A significant increase by 40% year-on-year. YouTube, Spotify, JioSaavn remained the key growth drivers for our digital content, be it new releases or our catalogue.

items.statement: YouTube contributes 45-50% of total revenue
items.quote: We can't tell you the exact number, but you can, as always mentioned that between 45% and 50% is always YouTube.

items.statement: Wynk settlement: Rs 5 crore booked in Q1, Rs 7 crore expected in Q2
items.quote: As we have already declared that Rs. 12 crores was the settlement, Rs. 5 crores we have taken in this quarter and Rs. 7 crores we will get in second quarter so we will take that as well.

items.statement: New content contributes 10-15% of revenue, catalogue 85-90%
items.quote: But as we said earlier, the new content at any time would contribute around 10% to 15% of the revenue and the catalogue would be the remaining.

items.statement: Non-film music not a substantial revenue or cost contributor
items.quote: overall non-film won't be a substantial contributor except let say one or two –But overall both on the revenue and cost front, it won't be a substantial contributor.

items.statement: Future acquisitions primarily film music
items.quote: It would be both and let say primarily more towards film's music

items.statement: In-house ERP system Pulse launched for content management, reporting, analytics; minimal cost
items.quote: Pulse basically takes care of content management and delivery, and also reporting analytics. So, it's basically having more processes in place so that our teams are geared up for the next level of growth that we want to achieve in the Company.

items.statement: Completed share buyback of Rs 46.62 crore inclusive of taxes; will continue returning surplus cash
items.quote: As you all know the Company has recently completed a share buyback for non-promoter shareholders, amounting to Rs.46.62 crores inclusive of all taxes. We will continue to pay out surplus cash to shareholders.

items.statement: Warner deal renewal: revenue booked on actuals; overflow expected after 3-4 years; content now on Wynk, Instagram via Warner
items.quote: whatever money we got from Warner's, we have kept it as advanced and whatever business actual they are doing. And they are reporting us, and we are taking that business in quarter wise.

items.statement: Instagram monetization started via Warner license
items.quote: Yes. We have also given Instagram license also to Warner and we are quite positive we will get money's from there as well.

items.statement: Content cost per song varies widely (spiritual ~Rs 2 lakh, big film song ~Rs 4-5 crore); film songs cost more than non-film
items.quote: If there is a one big film maybe it will cost 20 crores and I have only four songs or five songs in the film per song will be 4 to 5 crores and sometime one spiritual song we can make in 2 lakhs also.

items.statement: Film release delays depend on producers/directors; may push some FY25 films to FY26
items.quote: at time in our business few movies shift to next year or if there is any delay so we can't say anything on such delays because it is in the hands of the Producer and Directors all those people we are depending on them.

items.statement: Subscription revenue growth in India to take 2-3 years; ad-led model persists on YouTube
items.quote: it will take another two, three years and the platforms are doing all the right things to limit the free usage and motivating the users to go to the paid, but it will take time, it's not going to be six months or one year, it's going to take at least two, three years more.

items.statement: Content cost recovery targeted in 4-5 years; full cost written off in year of acquisition
items.quote: In my mind I want to recover my cost in three years' time maybe more earlier than that. But to investor, I always maintain that you please consider that we will recover the cost in four to five years' time.

items.statement: 7-8 experienced team members evaluate song quality and hit potential
items.quote: See deciding of a hit song comes with experience and we have seven to eight people working in the Company and everybody is experienced person and they have seen our growth, they have seen our hit numbers songs.

items.statement: Aspirational ROA for FY25 recalibrated to 2.2% from earlier 2.5% target
items.quote: I would just like to get back everyone's memory to the call we had in Q4, wherein we did mention that the aspirational ROA that we are chasing for the year is not 2.5%, but more like a 2.2

items.statement: Targeting PPOP growth in high teens to 20% for FY25
items.quote: On the question of PPOP, yes, our PPOP numbers are subdued, but we are looking at taking PPOP levels closer to the high teens to 20% type of levels for the year.

items.statement: Medium-term NIM aspiration is to return to 7% corridor
items.quote: The aspiration level is to get back to 7%. It is tough. I'm acknowledging that it's a stiff ask, but our business models should basically predicate on getting to that 7% territory in the near to medium term.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing expected to remain in 7.8%-8% corridor
items.quote: Yes, because at least today, we do not see any let-up. So yes, that would be my guidance, yes.

items.statement: Opex to assets target closer to 2.65% for full year FY25
items.quote: So that number is closer to 2.65% types of aspiration for a full year basis.

items.statement: Credit cost aspiration for FY25 around 1.4% and 1.2%-1.3% for longer term 2.5% ROA target
items.quote: So, 1.4%. So -- and over a longer period, our aspiration is also to reach 2.5% post-tax ROA, which would then mean that we will need to operate in the corridor of 1.2% to 1.3% of credit cost.

items.statement: Q1 disbursement growth moderate at 5% YoY due to election disruptions, heat waves, and flooding
items.quote: We did mention in our monthly updates about some of the disruptions, which were specific in April a nd May, considering election disruptions, heat waves in the north belt of the country. And in June, we did witness some flooding in Northeast

items.statement: CV and construction equipment disbursements grew 11% YoY
items.quote: When you look at CV business and construction equipment, we are not a very, very large player in huge CV, but in especially LCV, SCV where we have a good share as well as some of the bus segment that we've been participating on late, we have seen incremental growth, and that's grown we're at 11% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Tractor segment saw degrowth in Q1; industry cooling off for last 2 years
items.quote: Tractor, the industry has seen actually some amount of cooling off last 2 years, but Q1 has seen -- what numbers you see are a mix of wholesale and retail numbers. These are, of course, retail numbers. Our growth has -- we've had a degrowth in practice

items.statement: NIMs slightly lower QoQ and YoY due to elevated cost of funds; income to average assets at 12.9%
items.quote: However, all the levers which we have at our end, we've, in fact, even in Q1, most of the incremental COF come in in our internal budgets. And we are looking at all levers to make sure that cost moderation happens in the year going forward, which has also resulted in NIMs being slightly lower than last quarter and lower than last year's same time.

items.statement: Rate transmission from last 2 quarters to start showing delta in income to average assets going forward
items.quote: We have transmitted rates in the last 2 quarters now, which will start showing some delta in the going forward income to average assets, as well as our focus on what we call as penal interest charges and other charges.

items.statement: Used vehicle segment target 20% of incremental sourcing (currently 17-18%) to improve NIMs
items.quote: For specific NIM attractiveness, we have cited that the used vehicle segment, which is anywhere between 17% to 18% of our incremental sourcing needs to go up to 20%.

items.statement: Prime/affluent customer segment thresholds hit; no further negative drag on yields from mix shift
items.quote: On the prime vehicle side and on the more affluent customer segment side, we've already hit our threshold. So, our incremental growth is not going to come in from swapping out higher NIM products and swapping in lower NIM kind of capable products.

items.statement: AUM grew 23% YoY; book growth expected in high teens to 20% for FY25
items.quote: Just considering the last 2 years of good disbursements, we don't see too much of a challenge on book growth being in high teens to maybe 20%.

items.statement: GS3 at 3.56% vs 3.4% QoQ; contained seasonal Q1 increase; aspiration to keep below 3.4%
items.quote: Our GS3 numbers from closing of Q4 last year at 3.4% has climbed up to 3.56%. Historically, we've always seen Q1 significantly go up versus Q4. That number has been moderate in specifics of Q1.

items.statement: GS2 increased to 6.1% from 5% QoQ; seen as temporary delays in tractor segments
items.quote: When we look at GS2 numbers, yes, this GS2 numbers are much lower than last year same time. And there has been a bump up from Q4 from 5 to 6.1. We do see some specific bumps with certain customer segments and product segments like tractor in certain

items.statement: Credit cost improved to 1.5% from 2.1% YoY; write-offs at 1.1% of assets
items.quote: Credit cost, this has been a major benefit for the quarter. And you know that credit cost is a summation of provisions, write-offs, and settlement losses. On all 3 fronts, we are seeing ourselves moving in positive territory.

items.statement: Stage 3 coverage ratio at 59-60%; expected to decline further as LGDs improve
items.quote: Coverage ratio has come down to 59%, close to 60%. As I mentioned, this was bound to happen as the LGDs are improving with last 7, 8 quarters, collections overall throughput improving, which reflects directly in the LGD.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 94% YoY despite GS2/GS3 increase; overdue collections support ratio
items.quote: Collection efficiency, Viral is a function of due collections as well as overdue collections, right? And hence, that number will not be exactly mathematically equal to the due collections only because there are different buckets of overdue collection.

items.statement: Received corporate agency license from IRDAI; six tie-ups live (2 life, 2 general, 2 health)
items.quote: We have received the approval from IRDAI. And we are pleased to announce that six tie-ups have already gone live in the last month active tie-ups, two in life, two in general and two in health.

items.statement: Tier 1 capital at 16.4%, overall CAR at 18.5%; no capital raise needed in FY25, may raise in Q1/Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our Tier 1 is still very strong at 16.4%, overall, at 18.5%. With our current growth trajectory for the rest of the fiscal, we don't see a need to raise capital maybe sometime next year, Q1, Q2 when our Tier 1 levels are lower, we will look at augmenting our overall cost.

items.statement: Borrowing book near INR 1 lakh crore; shifting to offshore borrowings for quantum and 3-year ALM stability
items.quote: One must appreciate the fact that we are now close to a INR1 lakh crore borrowing book as well. And therefore, we need to take a balanced view on the instruments that we use. So, the offshore borrowings will bring in quantum, they come in at a slightly higher cost, but they bring in quantum and they come in at a 3-year door-to-door maturity.

items.statement: Opex reduced YoY and QoQ; frugality exercised; tech/digital investments yielding efficiency benefits
items.quote: We have reduced opex on a Y-o-Y as well as Q-o-Q basis, frugality on various projects has been exercised and going forward to -- with some of the benefits we're seeing in the efficiency levels of the investments made in tech, etcetera.

items.statement: PSU banks aggressive on PV pricing; NBFC share in CV declining; used CV remains NBFC fortress
items.quote: If you ask -- if we see where the competition intensity is, it is PSU banks who we see basically with the rate beneficial, we see a lot of aggression from the PSU banks. On the CV side, yes, the CV fleet operators, again, are moving towards banks and we see NBFC's overall share in CV come down a little bit.

items.statement: Northeast flood losses fully provided in Q1; no further provisions required
items.quote: Nothing, nothing. We have fully provided for that, and there would be no more provisions required.

items.statement: Income to average assets at 12.9%; targeting expansion to ~13% via fee income and rate transmission
items.quote: We are looking at augmenting the income. We are not happy at a 12.9% level; we are looking at going up. And I did mention the levers that we're working on including fee-based income to augment this line item.

items.statement: Annual double-digit sales growth primarily volume-led; EBITDA margin target 16-17% annually
items.quote: On an annual basis will aim to have double digit sales growth primarily led by volume. Also on the margin front, we should be able to hold on or do better than our historical EBITDA margin of 16% to 17% on an annual basis.

items.statement: Revenue grew 8% value and 10.8% volume in Q1 FY25; 2-year CAGR 11.5%, 3-year CAGR 12.2%
items.quote: The year has started on a positive note with revenues growing by 8% in value terms and 10.8% in volume. On a two -year and three-year CAGR basis, it works out to 11.5% and 12.2%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 18% vs 17.1% YoY; gross margin comfortable at 49-50% at current RM prices
items.quote: On EBITDA margin for the quarter, we stood at 18% versus 17.1% for the same period last year, an increase by 13.7%

items.statement: Gross margin range 49-50% at current raw material prices
items.quote: at these level of RMPM prices, we'll be comfortable with the gross margin range of 49% to 50%.

items.statement: Price cuts of ~3% taken in dishwash, fabric care and personal care; will remain for rest of year
items.quote: These cuts prices which are taken will remain there for the balance year as well. So there would be a decline to that extent.

items.statement: Liquid detergent growing faster on small base; Morelight 5L pack launched at INR70/litre; powder stable
items.quote: liquid is on a smaller base and it's growing faster. So the growth rates are going to be much faster while powder category is much stable category.

items.statement: Modern trade & e-commerce now ~15% of revenue vs ~10% 2-3 years ago; growing faster
items.quote: modern trade and e -commerce business is around 15% of our top line. So that's what it contributes now and it's been growing at a much faster clip.

items.statement: Full-year capex guided at INR 50-60 crores; depreciation in line
items.quote: Overall capex we believe should be in the range around INR50 crores to INR60 crores for the full year and depreciation also has been in line with that.

items.statement: Other expenses up 22% YoY, in line with sales growth; no one-offs
items.quote: it's very much in line with the overall sales increase and overall expense increases. It varies I mean again it can move between one quarter here and there but very much in line there are no one offs in the other expenses.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet with cash ~INR 650+ crores
items.quote: the cash balance now is in the range of around INR650-plus crores.

items.statement: Dividend payout reduced to 35% in FY24 from 60% average; conserving cash for future opportunities
items.quote: currently we have been conserving cash for any future opportunity which we may consider. So right now we are in the conservation mode for any future opportunities.

items.statement: Gained 300 bps market share in household insecticides vs last quarter; confident in LV differentiation
items.quote: we have gained 300 bps compared to last quarter and that's good enough and a good direction for us to show that our efforts are working

items.statement: Personal care margins impacted by volatile palm oil prices and freight costs
items.quote: the key raw material is palm oil and you know how the palm oil prices have been so volati le and it's an imported product. S o therefore the freight cost going up and down

items.statement: No specific outlet target for distribution expansion; focus on both direct and indirect
items.quote: We wouldn't want to say that right now.

items.statement: Personal care target 15% revenue mix from 12% via organic and inorganic routes; no timeline
items.quote: See, that's the wish that we want to be . To take from existing 12 to 15 and we'll see all possibilities both organic and inorganic.

items.statement: FY25 group operating revenue guidance of Rs 4,250 crore (PGEL Rs 3,650 crore + JV Goodworth Rs 600 crore), 55% growth over FY24
items.quote: For FY '25, our revised operating revenue guidance stands at, at least Rs. 3,650 crores in PGEL and another Rs. 600 crore in our JV Company Goodworth Electronics implying Rs. 4,250 crore of group operating revenue, which is a growth of 55% over FY '25 numbers.

items.statement: FY25 net profit guidance of at least Rs 216 crore for standalone PGEL, 58% growth over FY24
items.quote: We are also revising our guidance of net profit of at least Rs. 216 crore in FY '25 which is a growth of 58% over FY '24 net profit of Rs. 137 crore.

items.statement: FY25 product business revenue expected to grow ~60% from Rs 1,668 crore to Rs 2,650 crore
items.quote: The growth in product business that is washing machine, room air conditioners and air coolers is expected to be around 60% from Rs. 1,668 crore in FY '24 to around Rs. 2,650 crore in this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of Rs 370-380 crore, funded largely by internal accruals
items.quote: CAPEX guidance stands at Rs. 370 crore to Rs. 380 crore. The Company has planned to further expand room AC capacity by setting up a new integrated unit in Rajasthan and also a new greenfield capacity is being set up in Greater Noida for washing machine.

items.statement: Capex breakdown: Rs 125-130 crore for RAC plant & machinery, Rs 35-40 crore for washing machines, Rs 3 crore for coolers, Rs 20 crore for maintenance/sanitary/other, Rs 180 crore for land & building across Supa, Bhiwadi, Noida
items.quote: So, there will be about 125 to 130 crores will go for the plant and machinery in the RAC business, about 35 to 40 crores in the washing machines, about Rs. 3 crore for the coolers, and rest about 20 crores for, I will say, the maintenance CAPEX, and sanitary wear, and other businesses.

items.statement: RAC capacity expansion: indoor units from 250k to 350k/month, outdoor from 200k to 300k/month, window AC from 25k to 50k/month by year-end
items.quote: On a monthly basis, we can do currently about 250,000 indoor units and about 200,000 outdoor units and 25,000 window AC currently. This capacity we want to take to about 350,000 indoor units and 300,000 outdoor units by this year and maybe about 50,000 window AC.

items.statement: Washing machine capacity expansion from 115k to 200k units/month by year-end
items.quote: In the washing machine, our current capacity is about 115,000 per month, both semi-automatic and fully automatic put together. This we want to take to 200,000 per month by yearend.

items.statement: Seasonal capacity utilisation 80-90% in peak season, below 20% off-season for AC; washing machine 80-90% in season, ~40% off-season
items.quote: Typically, in the season, the capacity utilization remains in the range of about 80 % to 90%. In AC, the season starts somewhere from January, February, and it lasts till May, June. In the washing machine, typically, and in the off-season, this capacity utilization comes down to below 20%.

items.statement: Order book for product business remains robust; on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in FY25
items.quote: Orderbook and visibility for product business remains robust and the Company is on track to accelerate product business growth significantly in this financial year.

items.statement: Room AC revenue Rs 882 crore (130% YoY), washing machine 72% YoY, coolers 287% YoY
items.quote: The room AC business contributed Rs. 882 crore, which is a 130% growth on a Y-o-Y basis. The washing machine business had a growth of 72% on Y-o-Y basis and cooler operating revenues also grew by 287%.

items.statement: Gross margin 18.1% in Q1 FY25 (same as Q1 FY24); lower due to higher AC mix with bought-out parts; conversion price fixed per unit for season, BOM pass-through
items.quote: If you look at our product business, the AC business has lower contribution margins because the bought-out parts, especially the compressor, the controller chip set and even motors et cetera are being bought from the vendors directly. So, that is why the gross contribution is lower.

items.statement: Conversion prices fixed per unit for the season; cannot renegotiate mid-season regardless of demand strength; margin improvement only from operating leverage
items.quote: Once the prices are settled with a customer for conversion or a season, they don't change in the mid-season irrespective of the season being strong or weak. So, it is not that we can actually renegotiate in the season, go back to the customers.

items.statement: High dependence on Chinese imports for key components (compressor, controller chips, motors); domestic value addition improved from 20-25% to 40-45%, targeting 70-75% in 2-3 years
items.quote: If you see, largely if you see 4 , 5 years back, if we say that domestic value addition was around 20%, 25%, today we can very easily say that we have reached a level of around 40%-45%. But with these capacities coming up and in next 2, 3 years, I think we will be very easily touching around 70%, 75% domestic value addition in India.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expands at year-end due to peak production coinciding with Chinese New Year inventory build; expects gradual improvement over next couple of years as local component capacity ramps up
items.quote: These things are likely to change in coming years as the capacity for components and raw materials ramp up in India, and we are hopeful that going forward in a couple of years, the working capital cycle will shrink from what it is today.

items.statement: Capex to be funded largely by internal accruals
items.quote: As stated by Vishalji, we have guided for 370 crores to 380 crores of CAPEX in FY '25. This will be funded largely by internal accruals.

items.statement: New RAC PLI scheme announced; company will apply through one of its entities
items.quote: Laptop and IT, we are still a work in progress. This new PLI which has come for RAC, we will be applying in that through one of our companies.

items.statement: Differentiation through delivery performance; quality and cost are hygiene factors; gaining share due to superior delivery in season
items.quote: The differentiation comes mainly from delivery, and we take pride in that and we have been able to add new customers, also increase our share of business in most of the existing customers because our delivery has been allowing us to differentiate from the competition.

items.statement: AC industry volume growth expected at 15-20% annually driven by climate change and affordability; AC penetration ~7-8%, washing machine ~12-14%
items.quote: Basically, we think industry should grow at about 15% to 20% in the coming years, given the climate change and also the increased affordability of AC and that will help us to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: TV business fully shifted to JV Goodworth; PGEL electronics revenue Q1 Rs 100.8 crore (incl Rs 17 cr TV sales to third parties, Rs 13-14 cr AC controllers); full-year electronics revenue ~Rs 200 crore
items.quote: Now, I want to highlight that the total revenues assumed from the electronics business for the full year is about 200 crores, out of which 100 crores has already come in the first quarter. And TV business has shifted fully to the Goodworth, and now there will be no more TV sales from the main Company, PG Electroplast.

items.statement: Refrigerator contract manufacturing evaluated but not meeting internal ROC guidelines; waiting for industry dynamics to improve before entry
items.quote: We were not convinced that we were able to, at least on the exercise that we did, we were not hitting the internal ROC guidance guidelines that we have for ourselves in the refrigerator business, given the current conversion margins, which we are seeing in the industry.

items.statement: IT PLI progress slow; customers delayed decisions awaiting elections; no significant activity yet; sales target of Rs 750 crore year-1 uncertain
items.quote: Most of the customers were waiting for the elections to get over. Now, I think we have still not seen much movement on the IT PLI side yet. Most of the customers are still slow in decision making.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration of 25-30% revenue CAGR over next 4-5 years; existing product lines to deliver 20-25% growth, new opportunities for additional scale
items.quote: We believe that we can actually look at least 25% to 30% kind of CAGR growth for us for next four or five years. I don't see any challenges in that.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA improved 6.7x YoY to INR 12.05 cr; adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 4 cr from INR 11.77 cr
items.quote: EBITDA for quarter Q1 FY 2025 was INR 12.05 crores as compared to INR 1.80 crores in Q1 FY 2024 marking an improvement of 6.7x year -on-year.

items.statement: PBT improved ~2,000 bps YoY to negative INR 13.74 cr from negative INR 18.79 cr
items.quote: Profit Before Tax improved approximately 2,000 bps year -on-year, standing at negative INR 13.74 crores as compared to negative INR 18.79 crores in Q1 FY 2024.

items.statement: Targeting 45% YoY revenue growth for next 3 years; aim to reach INR 1,000 cr revenue
items.quote: we have targeted ourselves to grow at a 45% year-on-year revenue going in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Aim to retain current EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and PBT ratios for next 3 quarters to exceed internal expectations
items.quote: Our idea is that if we are able to retain the similar sort of ratios for the next 3 quarters, then we would have exceeded our internal expectations.

items.statement: Targeting 450 bps quarter-on-quarter EBITDA improvement
items.quote: we would like to keep an eye on profitability, ensuring that we are improving our EBITDA by 450 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Rental business manages 30,000 units across 17 cities; 6 lakh tenants searching, 90,000 under management, INR 70 cr rental payments managed
items.quote: The rental business comprising of student living, co -living and family rentals, manages 30,000 rental units across 17 cities in India.

items.statement: Target 50,000 units under management as first milestone, then 1 lakh units
items.quote: We are aiming to reach 50,000 units under management as our first pit stop, followed by 1 lakh units under management.

items.statement: Distribution: 80,000 active buyers on Aurum Analytica; 7,500+ SaaS licenses across 180 projects; INR 450 cr home sales facilitated via broker aggregation
items.quote: This quarter, we had 80,000 buyers actively looking for home purchase at Aurum Analytica. items.statement: Closed unbanked rural branches (UBRs), reducing outlets from 808 to 780; UBR share at 34.4% vs 25% regulatory norm.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 55.5% in Q1 FY25 from 58% in Q1 FY24; full-year FY24 was 57.4%; expecting further leverage.

So whe n we started the year at 58 .0%, ended the overall year at 57.4%. We have begun this year at 55%. So we are expecting more and more leverage to come through during this year.

items.quote: Our capital adequacy is at 19.3% with Tier 1 being at 18.2%. I must tell all of yo u that if I added the interim PAT , which is roughly about Rs. 171 crore, this capital adequacy would be at 20.2%.

items.statement: Home 360 anchor strategy: 3.6 products per housing customer; 99% CASA penetration with avg balance Rs 16,100; cross-sell includes 2W loan at 100% LTV, pre-approved business loan up to Rs 5 lakh.

items.statement: Cost of funds rose to 8.0% from 7.8% QoQ and 7.5% YoY; NIM maintained via asset mix shift and lower interest suspense.

items.quote: Our ROA is at 2.1% for the quarter and an ROE of 18.8 %. Now the ROE does include all the equity that has come in during the IPO, which is the first full quarter of the equity infusion for the quarter.

items.quote: For example, processing fee has been flat, insurance commission has increased from Rs. 29 crore to Rs. 39 crore. Recoveries have reduced from Rs. 40 crore to Rs. 20 crore. The core non-interest income is moving up, whereas the non-core non-interest income is moving down.

items.quote: we have witnessed an increase in raw material prices, like chana has increased by 17%, potato prices have increased by 13%, urad has increased by 24%.
