items.quote: And we have set up this facility which is all processing and packaging facilities. So we are expecting in this year USD40 million revenue.

items.statement: Jasmine rice sales volume approximately 70,000 tons annually; all manufacturing outsourced to Thailand millers
items.quote: So sales capacity we sell roughly 70,000 tons. As far as the manufacturing, that is all outsourced and we buy from the Thailand millers.

items.statement: Organic staples portfolio estimated at INR700-800 crores market size in India; launching soon
items.quote: Nielsen doesn't cover that, but estimate is roughly INR700 crores to INR800 crores organic the complete portfolio as a market.

items.statement: Appointed strong distributor in Saudi Arabia (1.2M ton Basmati market); Middle East currently 8% of revenue but key focus for next growth phase
items.quote: Middle East contribute roughly 8%. But as far as Saudi is concerned, we have appointed our partner there, distributor for that market.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced by 8 days to 202 days YoY through continued optimization focus
items.quote: Because of our continued focus on the working capital optimization, our net working capital days have also reduced by 8 days to 202 days versus 210 days in the last quarter, in the last quarter 1 financial year '24.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved to 0.2x from 0.4x; debt-to-EBITDA improved to 0.8x from 1.2x YoY; targeting further deleveraging in FY25
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio declined from 0.4x to 0.2x, and the debt-to-EBITDA ratio for quarter 1 financial '25 is 0.8 versus 1.2 in the previous corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Insurance claim of ~INR160 crores plus interest expected within 4 weeks per Supreme Court order; Golden Star earnout payment due June 2025
items.quote: Supreme Court has said that within 4 weeks we should get our money with Bank guarantee. So that's good news and we will get our money in 4 weeks' time.

items.statement: Kharif season sowing 10-15% higher than last year with good monsoon; expecting larger crop and lower commodity prices
items.quote: So whatever the forecast we are getting the crop is sowing is more 10% to 15% against last year and the monsoon is good. So everything so far is looking good and we are expecting more crop, lesser price.

items.statement: Premiumization expected to drive 0.5-0.7% margin expansion from higher gross margin products
items.quote: We have given the guidance also that where our margin expansion will come. We said 0.5% to 0.7% will come from premiumization.

items.statement: Commodity price decline impacted margins by 0.5-0.75% in Q1; 90% of crop now hedged for balance of year
items.quote: Overall I will say it may have impacted our margin by 0.5% or 0.75% down in this quarter.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat/ready-to-cook business in India expected to break even in FY26-27 at INR400 crores revenue base
items.quote: It will be breakeven in '26, '27. So on a revenue base of INR400 crores it will be and we are projecting that revenue to be in '26, '27.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in FY25-26 as commodity prices decline and freight costs stabilize
items.quote: We are very optimistic on year '25, '26 as the prices of commodity will also come down and there will be a stability in the freight cost also.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis freight impact not yet behind; worst expected to last 1-2 more quarters
items.quote: No, the worst is not yet behind. We have seen the Red Sea impact a little bit and that's why the growth in the margin has impacted. But we are positive that this is only a quarter or 2 -quarter thing.

items.statement: Lower MEP on rice exports benefits industry; limited direct impact on LT Foods as it exports higher-value Basmati
items.quote: As far as the lowering down the M EP, the industry will definitely gain. As far as LT is concerned LT has not much impact on this because we are exporting on a higher value.

items.statement: Basmati and non-Basmati markets don't cannibalize; different geographies and income segments
items.quote: So if you see the Basmati market, they don't cannibalize with non-Basmati to Basmati. Non-Basmati is more Africa and the country with a lower income. But as far as Ba smati is concerned, that's mainly consumed in Middle East, Europe and America.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 pre-sales were Rs 6,400 crore, driven by Privana West launch
items.quote: Our pre-sales number was in the range of 6,400 crores, predominantly headlined by the extremely successful launch of Privana West.

items.statement: Full-year pre-sales guidance maintained at Rs 17,000 crore with potential upside from LUX 5 launch
items.quote: So, right now, we are not officially re-guiding you to a higher number. But I think it's a logical conclusion that there should hopefully be some upward bias to that.

items.statement: Embedded margins for new launches remain in late 30s; LUX 5 expected to reach mid-40s margin
items.quote: Our embedded margins for new product launch continue in the late 30s and hopefully with the LUX 5 during the later part of this year we should be back to the mid-40s that we have charted ourselves for.

items.statement: DCCDL FY25 capex Rs 1,800 crore, growing 18-20% annually over next 2-3 years
items.quote: On DCCDL this year's CAPEX will be 1,800 crores and going forward in the next 2-3 years this will go up by about 18%-20% from this ballpark figure of 2,000 crores.

items.statement: DLF standalone residual capex ~Rs 700 crore each for three malls and Atrium Place JV
items.quote: So, the residual CAPEX on the three malls that DLF is constructing is about 700 crores. And the residual CAPEX on the Atrium Place which is a JV with Hines is again about 700 odd crores.

items.statement: DT Gurgaon Block 4 OC by year-end, full completion by Feb-Mar 2025; DT Chennai Block 3 OC by Sep 2024, completion by year-end
items.quote: Downtown 4 Gurgaon the OC is expected by the end of this year. However, after the OC comes there is a fair amount of other development, landscaping and other work to be done. We think this building will complete in all its ramifications by February-March next year. Downtown 3 in Chennai, we expect the OC to come in end August, early September, most likely September and by the time the landscaping

items.statement: DCCDL rental income exit run-rate guidance Rs 5,000 crore for FY25; FY26 expected Rs 5,800-6,000 crore
items.quote: The exit for this which we had given the guidance earlier is 5,000 crores. But next year the jump up will be rather significant because Downtown 4 in Gurgaon Downtown 3 in Chennai and the full rentals of Downtown 1 and 2 will come into play. And therefore, this will go up significantly in FY26.

items.statement: Office portfolio vacancy ~8%, target to reduce to 6-7% by year-end
items.quote: Our vacancy today in offices is about 8 odd%. We plan to take it down overall to between 6% and 7%.

items.statement: Strong demand across geographies; no slowdown seen; bookings backed by Rs 50 lakh booking amount and 35-40% collections within 9 months
items.quote: I don't see any slow down at this point in time. I am being very honest with you, and I don't see anything right now because right now as we play the whole world together. Any launch is a global launch for us whether it's the NRI, domestic or other cities in the country. We are seeing very robust demand.

items.statement: No price exhaustion; secondary market transactions at Rs 30,000-50,000/sq ft validate pricing
items.quote: I am happy to report two transactions in the second market in the last one week. One of Grove which is in the DLF 5 geography which is crossed Rs. 30,000 a square feet. And recently just today an hour back we closed a Crest 4,000 square feet unit at 49,500. It's touched Rs. 50,000 a square foot Crest.

items.statement: Quarterly collections ~Rs 2,900-3,000 crore for next two quarters; Arbour 45% collected in 15 months
items.quote: Ballpark this 2,900 to 3,000 crores is I think what a quarterly collection for the next two quarters at least should stay at.

items.statement: Receivables Rs 21,000 crore vs cost-to-complete Rs 10,500-11,000 crore; Rs 5,000 crore already in RERA accounts
items.quote: Ballpark our receivables of the projects that we have launched till the 30 th June is about 21,000 crores have to be collected. We have about 10,500-11,000 crores is our total cost to complete. Of that 11,000 crores, 5,000 crores is already residing in the RERA account today.

items.statement: Construction outflow on DevCo side to exceed Rs 800 crore/quarter from Q3 FY25
items.quote: I think our construction is on an ongoing basis. Yes, we believe that on a full total basis from Q3, the construction outflow on the DevCo side should be a number north of 800 crores.

items.statement: Launch pipeline: Goa by Sep 2024, LUX 5 in Q2, Mumbai by Dec 2024/Jan 2025, another Privana in Q4, plus Chandigarh and commercial launches
items.quote: So, our launch pipeline remains what we had indicated earlier which is that hopefully if all approvals come in time, we should have the Goa launch in this quarter before September end and we should have the LUX 5 launch in the next quarter. Mumbai, right now the approval process is on along with the requisite clearance, etc., The first slum rehab building of about 35 odd stories is ready now. And

items.statement: SEZ denotification process settling down; 1.6 msf denotified, 70-80% leased; leasing momentum to pick up in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: So, our SEZ portfolio before the denotification started was in the DLF system including DCCDL 16.5 million, out of which we de-notified about 10% about 1.6 million. This has been now I think 70%-80% leased out and I think as we go forward in the next three-four quarters the leasing momentum will pick up further because of two reasons.

items.statement: Ireo land parcels: 20-acre license transfer nearing completion; 7-acre conversion to group housing underway; launch planned early next year
items.quote: The 20 acres was already a group housing license. So, the transfer of license process is going on. I think that should really be completed in the next very short time. The balance 7 acres was a part of a plotted license and there's a migration of license exercise. There's a certain protocol process in the government. That's going on to convert it into a group housing license and the two of them wi

items.statement: Medium-term capital allocation: 50% growth, 50% shareholder returns; no fixed acquisition targets
items.quote: So, while we have broadly always indicated that we would like on a medium-term basis to allocate our free cash flow to growth and shareholder returns on broadly a half-half basis. But I think it will depend year to year. There is no set target that we have to acquire 10 million square feet of GAV or something because frankly we have enough GAV of our own.

items.statement: Speculator participation minimal; re-trade proportion minuscule; 20 cancellations in Privana West all reinstated at higher prices
items.quote: Actually, in the sales that Aakash and his team have done in the last 2.5-3 years, the proportion of re-trade that has come in the market is minuscule. So, it's not that people who are buying are exiting in a hurry by making that Rs. 50 lakhs profit or something. They're all here to stay for at least a medium term if not 100% case the long term.

items.statement: Free operating cash flow (DLF + Cyber City) exceeded Rs 2,500 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: really if you see between our DLF and Cyber City numbers together, we did in excess of 2,500 crores of free operating cash flow during the quarter.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 13-15% and EBITDA margin of 9-10% for FY25
items.quote: We do not give a guidance as such, but we always said that we should grow around 13% to 15% in revenues. And margins, we have largely come back. I think we should hover around between 9% to 10% EBITDA margins for the year.

items.statement: Strong Q1 driven by good summer; Electronics up 41%, Consumer Durables up 26%, Electricals up 7% YoY
items.quote: It has been a positive start to the fiscal year with a strong performance in the first quarter. We have reported a consolidated net revenue of INR1,477 crores in Q1, FY '25, higher by 21.6% on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 380 bps YoY to 36.3% due to pricing, softening inputs, better mix; recovery largely complete
items.quote: We reported a gross margin of 36.3% in this quarter, an improvement of 380 basis points Y -o-Y. This is due to a combination of pricing action, softening input prices and better product mix.

items.statement: Price hikes of ~2% in Q4 FY24 and ~2% in Q1 FY25 taken to offset commodity cost increases; more hikes ongoing
items.quote: We had improved our margins through the realization of input cost benefits towards the last quarter of last year and we had taken some price increase, I think, it was about 2-odd percent in quarter four of last year. We have also taken 2-odd percent in quarter one of this year.

items.statement: Capex of INR100-120 crore per year for next two years; fans plant building started, completion in ~18 months
items.quote: INR100-120 crores of capex. Basically what will happen is as we get into next year, there are also investments in moulds and dies that are going on. And they are also going to come up. So, there will be a normative capex of around INR100 crores to INR120 crores for the next two years also.

items.statement: Sunflame revenue declined 7% YoY, in line with forecasts; kitchen industry facing subdued demand
items.quote: Sunflame reported de-growth in the top line of 7% on a Y-o-Y basis. Also, the top line was soft. It was largely in line with our forecast s and plan

items.statement: Debtor days at 35 (below normative 60-62) due to strong season; creditor days at 75 due to high May-June buying
items.quote: So debtors have come down, they are lower than our normative levels because it was a strong season, so customers pay on time. Otherwise, similarly, even on the payable side, even May and June, both were big months.

items.statement: Fans category highly competitive with aggressive market leader and startup; price hikes mainly commodity pass-through
items.quote: Fans remains an extremely competitive category. We have a very, very aggressive market leader and we have a startup who's also very aggressive. So, most of the price hikes are in relation with the increasing commodity prices.

items.statement: BEE regulations caused 7-10% price increases in entry-level fans, 5% in premium; added to commodity cost pressure
items.quote: The second shock was given by BEE, which meant that there were almost 7% to 10% price increases in the entry level products and may be 5% increase in the premium level products.

items.statement: Stabilizer long-term CAGR 8-9%; digital UPS growth driven by summer power cuts and solar rooftop solutions
items.quote: See, for stabilizers, we are expecting, if you look at a very, very long term, that is about 10 years CAGR, It is somewhere around 8% to 9%. And that should be the growth that we also will be working with.

items.statement: Copper and aluminium prices firming up; crude derivatives also rising; pricing actions to preserve margins
items.quote: Of late, we are also seeing some firming up of commodity prices and will be taking pricing actions wherever necessary to preserve margins.

items.statement: Wires business 90-95% retail trade; limited project exposure; real estate activity formalizing among few large builders
items.quote: V-Guard's wires and Electricals business is largely retail. It means that almost 90% to 95% of the sales come from the trade. That is retail shops. We do not have a big business supplying to very large builders and infrastructure players.

items.statement: Filling critical vacancies in Sunflame; A&P spend up 30-40% YoY in Q1; investing in talent, technology, digitization
items.quote: If you look at the current year, our A&P for Q1 has gone up by some 30% to 40% in revenue. It has gone up faster than the revenue. So, we are pressing the foot on the accelerator for A&P.

items.statement: Annual sales volume target of 2,10,000 tons for FY25
items.quote: As I said, sales volume has crossed 50,000 tons this quarter and we are in the vicinity of achieving our annual… not in the vicinity, it is likelihood that we will achieve our annual target of 2,10,000 tons of steel.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs.7,000-10,000 for FY25 and Rs.8,000-11,000 post-capex
items.quote: This year, Rs. 7000 to Rs. 10,000, next year maybe Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 11,000.

items.statement: Billet capacity tested at 2,60,000 MT per annum in Q4 FY24 and Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, in Q4 FY24 and in Q1 FY25 we tested our capability to achieve the target of 2,60,000 MT per annum, that has been tested and we have been able to achieve these targets.

items.statement: Kocks block and new re-heating furnace expansion on track with two planned shutdowns in July and Q3/Q4
items.quote: So, those are like capacity expansion by putting up Kocks block and new Re-heating furnace is going on as per plan and things at this moment look quite under control.

items.statement: 55 MW solar power plant purchase agreement signed, expected by March 2025
items.quote: we have already signed our purchase agreement for setting up 55 MW power plant. Hopefully, it will be in place by March '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs.48 crores, up 31.71% YoY; realization Rs.82,000 per ton
items.quote: EBITDA is a good number; it is Rs. 48 crores, and it has increased by 31.71%

items.statement: Raw material prices up 8-10% in Q1, neutralized by inventory valuation; prices fell in July, inventory loss possible in Q2
items.quote: Raw material prices in Q1, raw material prices was up by 8% to 10%. Its impact on profitability was neutralized by the compensate increase in inventory valuations.

items.statement: Gas cost lower by 40-45% after switching from THINK Gas to GAIL
items.quote: It is currently lower by about 40%, 45% in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Power tariff increased 3% from June 15, 2024; expected 3% annual increase
items.quote: the increase in tariff by 3% of power, which is effective from 15th of June 2024.

items.statement: Maruti indicated EV penetration scaled down from 25-30% to 15%, supporting IC engine demand
items.quote: We had a conference our team attended with Maruti, which they have shared that maybe in the things to come the EV penetration, which was envisaged at 30% or 25%, will be about 15%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 sales volume 50,298 MT; production 55,000-57,000 MT with inventory build for shutdowns
items.quote: In-house and outside, both put together, we have been able to roll more than 55,000 tons to 57,000 tons and our sales in this quarter is 50,000 tons

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio at 0.12, expected to remain in same range with expansions
items.quote: our debt-equity ratios are well within the range; it is close to 0.12. And going forward also with the expansions we are expecting to be in the same range

items.statement: 80% scrap sourced domestically, 5-10% imported; end-of-life vehicle policy to boost domestic supply
items.quote: As far as we are concerned, 80% of our scrap is recycled. So, that means our raw material is recyclable scrap, out of which a large part is from domestic market

items.statement: Exports ~10% of total sales including indirect exports to Aichi; Thailand market subdued, Europe potential for green steel
items.quote: our exports are in the vicinity of around 10% of the total sales including the indirect export of Aichi.

items.statement: Geographical concentration: 65-75% sales in North and West zones
items.quote: total I think 65% to 70% of the sales will be in both these areas.

items.statement: EAF route gives CO2 emissions of 0.73 tons/ton vs blast furnace; solar plant to reduce below 0.45
items.quote: as of today we are having 0.73 CO2 emissions per ton of steel. After setting up the solar plant our CO2 emissions will come down below 0.45.

items.statement: Blast furnace cost Rs.6,000-8,000/ton lower but more capital intensive; EAF has comparable or better RoCE
items.quote: It is always Rs.6,000 to Rs.8,000 a ton lower cost in blast furnace, but on the capital employed side it is much, much capital intensive than electric arc furnace. On the RoCE front, we are comparable or even better.

items.statement: Budget impact minimal; ferro nickel import duty cut provides minor benefit
items.quote: On ferro nickel, some of the minor additions which we make in our steel making, on that, some relief on custom duty has been given.

items.statement: Over 95% sales to automobile sector; focus on auto unless larger expansion
items.quote: Majority is in the automobile industry, more than 95%.

items.statement: Aichi Steel technical cooperation progressing well with three representatives on-site
items.quote: three of their representatives are stationed at our works. So, that is going on and accordingly, our teams are working with them very closely

items.statement: OEM price negotiations ongoing; raw material price volatility and availability a key risk
items.quote: most of the things will depend on the raw material prices, price finalization with the OEMs.

items.statement: Billet-to-rolled yield 90%; 25% of rolled product peeled for bright bars
items.quote: Yield is 90% from billet to rolled product. So, you can say if we will be using 100 tons, rolled product coming out will be 90 tons

items.statement: Greenfield plant still under discussion, no final decision
items.quote: Greenfield plant is still under discussion. No final decision has been taken.

items.statement: Circular economy initiative with major OEM to source scrap and supply steel back
items.quote: Circular economy means that we will be getting the scrap from them which will be coming to us and we will be using that scrap to make the steel for them and steel so made will go back to them.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 18-20% for FY25; EBITDA margin expected around 15-16% depending on cost movement
items.quote: We will be -- as of now, the same guidance which we have given, that 18%, 20% i n the revenue guidance. And EBITDA last quarter was 16.6%, which was higher than our average margin. But we believe that we should be in the range of approximately 15%, 16%, but everything will depend upon how the cost moves from here

items.statement: Domestic laminate demand expected to normalize in Q2 after election and heat disruptions in Q1
items.quote: our sense is that even this month is looking pr etty decent. So our sense is it should be kind of normalized quarter in Q2, at least on the domestic demand side

items.statement: Laminate EBITDA margin fell 120 bps YoY and 300 bps QoQ to 13.6% due to higher employee costs and unsold export inventory
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the laminate business stood at 13.6% in this quarter, a degrowth of 120 basis points on a year-on-year basis and a degrowth of 300 basis points on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Plywood prices increased ~4% effective July; laminate price hike under review; export freight cost increases largely passed to customers
items.quote: On the plywood business, we passed on certain costs to the market effective July. So about close to 4% price increases we've done. On the laminate side, we are still reviewing the cost impact and whether we can offset it with higher volume and better value mix.

items.statement: Kraft paper and deco paper costs rising due to sea freight increases from Southeast Asia, East Asia and Europe; base prices stable
items.quote: Certain kraft paper costs have gone up like -- so it will have an impact, any costs going up, will have an impact. And certain deco paper costs, not as base price, but because of the sea freight increase from both Southeast Asia, East Asia and Europe.

items.statement: Laminate utilization at 83% in Q1; plywood utilization at 24%; particleboard plant expected to start in Q3 FY25; Gujarat laminate plant near full capacity
items.quote: Production volume were at 5.08 million sheets and at a utilization level of 83%. Sales volume for the quarter stood at 4.67 million sheets.

items.statement: Particleboard project capex ongoing; peak debt estimated at INR925-950 crores in FY25; brownfield laminate expansion possible at Gujarat and Naidupeta
items.quote: As per our estimate, peak debt will be in this year only because the project particleboard project will get over in this year. So we believe that our peak debt will be in the range of around INR925 crores to INR950 crores, in that range.

items.statement: Export laminate volume grew 13.8% YoY; 1.5 lakh sheets held back in June due to container unavailability; situation slightly better in July
items.quote: in the Q1, we have already mentioned in our communication that in Q1 -- still at the towards the end of June, we could not be able to ship some of the material, nearly 1.5 lakh sheets, we would not be able to ship

items.statement: Particleboard project targets 15-18% ROCE at full utilization (year 3-4) with 20-24% EBITDA margin at 90%+ utilization
items.quote: We believe that in terms of when we reach the full utilization level, which will happen in t he third or fourth year kind of a thing, then we can have that margin in the range of around 15% to 18% ROCE

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 65 days in Q1 FY25 from 72 days in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Our net working capital days stood at 65 days in this quarter as compared to 72 days in quarter 1 last year.

items.statement: Net debt at INR922 crores including INR465 crores for particleboard project; peak debt expected in FY25 then declining
items.quote: Our net debt stood at INR922 crores, which includes debt of approximately INR465 crores on account of ongoing particleboard project.

items.statement: Laminate realization improved to INR1,105/sheet; focus on premiumization and value mix improvement in domestic and export markets
items.quote: Our average realization for the quarter was at INR1,105 per sheet.

items.statement: Export sales to channel distributors and large furniture producers; gaining market share in export geographies with new capacities and product sizes
items.quote: So it's a bit of a long phased discussion, but just brief, it will be channel distributors. It will be large furniture producers. Mostly these 2. At times, some large contractors, fabricators.

items.statement: Gaining export market share from India; taking share from international players in certain geographies; market share shift rather than overall market growth
items.quote: I think clearly, within the -- within exports from India, I think our market share has gone up. And the geographies we are operating in, not all geographies, certain geographies d o one more business maybe versus the regional local players

items.statement: Container availability and freight cost volatility persist due to geopolitical issues; no visibility on normalization timeline
items.quote: And it's difficult to, as of now, say when the situation will become normal because it's not in our hand, it's more of a geopolitical situation, which is creating this trouble.

items.statement: Plywood business targeting EBITDA breakeven at ~INR40 crores quarterly sales; timber costs up substantially over last 6-9 months
items.quote: So plywood, so we are in the upper premium segment of the market. We're not in the middle or lower end of the market. And quarter after quarter, I think the loss is reducing. And if you see now nearly at about INR40-odd crores of sales in the quarter, we should become EBITDA positive, approximately slightly lower than that.

items.statement: Employee cost increased ~INR10 crores QoQ due to annual bonus and increments booked in Q1
items.quote: If you see that employee cost has gone up by INR10 crores. So that will be -- and that is on account of like onetime annual expense, which happens bonus in the quarter 1 and the annual increment.

items.statement: Management aims to deliver sustainable VNB growth by balancing business growth, profitability, risk and prudence.
items.quote: With the strong business fundamentals, our endeavor will be to deliver sustainable VNB growth with our efforts pivoted towards balancing business growth, profitability, risk and prudence.

items.statement: Customer preference is shifting towards unit-linked products from non-linked products.
items.quote: Contribution from linked savings product to overall APE increased from 38.8% in Q1-FY2024 to 51.4% in Q1-FY2025 on account of customer preference shifting towards unit products from non-linked products.

items.statement: VNB margin stood at 24.0% in Q1-FY2025, driven by product mix shift.
items.quote: The Value of New Business grew by 7.8% year-on-year to ₹ 4.72 billion. With an APE of ₹ 19.63 billion, margins stood at 24.0%.

items.statement: Total APE grew 34.4% YoY to ₹19.63 billion; retail APE grew 42.2% to ₹16.66 billion.
items.quote: Our total APE grew by 34.4% year-on-year to ₹ 19.63 billion, and retail APE grew by 42.2% year-on-year to ₹ 16.66 billion for Q1-FY2025.

items.statement: Added more than 12,000 agents in Q1-FY2025; agency capacity up ~20% YoY.
items.quote: We continue to build capacity and have added more than 12,000 agents during Q1-FY2025 spread across geographies.

items.statement: Partnership distribution (multi-insurance) contributes ~23% of business; proprietary channels contribute ~55% of retail APE.
items.quote: In fact, just to add here, actually Bancassurance partners or non-bank partnerships CABR that we have, they contribute ~ 23% of our business. So, remaining part of our business is mostly proprietary apart from ICICI Bank which as you know focuses on protection and Standard Chartered Bank, which also is single insurance.

items.statement: Cost to TWRP for savings business at 19.2%; overall cost to TWRP at 32.6% in Q1-FY2025.
items.quote: Our overall cost to TWRP ratio stood at 32.6% in Q1-FY2025. Our cost to TWRP on the savings line of business has shown a marginal increase and stood at 19.2%.

items.statement: IRDAI revised surrender value norms effective Oct 1, 2024; company has launched products with level/trail commission to align stakeholder interests.
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we welcome IRDAI's efforts to increase insurance penetration by improving the customer's value proposition for non-linked products. It will lead to an improvement in the surrender value in case of early exits and comes into force effective October 1, 2024.

items.statement: 13-month persistency at 89.7%; 49-month persistency at 70.7%.
items.quote: 13-month persistency stood at 89.7%, and 49-month persistency stood at 70.7%.

items.statement: Claim settlement ratio 99.2% for FY2024; average turnaround 1.3 days for non-investigative claims.
items.quote: We have an industry leading claim settlement ratio of 99.2% for FY2024, with an average turnaround time of 1.3 days for settling non-investigative claims.

items.statement: Mr. Sandeep Batra re-designated as Chairman effective June 30, 2024; Mr. Suresh Vaswani appointed as Independent Director effective July 4, 2024.
items.quote: Mr. Sandeep Batra has been re-designated as Chairman with effect from the same date. I am also pleased to inform you that Mr. Suresh Vaswani has been appointed as an additional Independent Director effective July 4, 2024, subject to the approval of the Shareholders.

items.statement: 71% reduction in cases with higher propensity for fraud and early claims for savings policies via data analytics.
items.quote: Our focus on data analytics to mitigate insurance risk at onboarding stage has led to 71% reduction in cases with higher propensity for fraud and early claims for savings policies.

items.statement: Expense allocation methodology change (₹446 crore impact on policy liabilities) has no material impact on VNB; no par impact.

items.quote: The Board recently g ave approval to raise up to INR 1,000 crores through QIP process which was done through a board meeting end of June. And most part of the funds will be used for capex

items.statement: Long-term debt ~INR 7.5 crores (ECB), final payment by Oct 2024; working capital ~INR 150-160 crores
items.value: INR 7.5 crores long-term; INR 150-160 crores working capital
items.quote: On the debt side the long-term debt in the company is at this moment close to around INR7.5 crores which is going to be over by end of October. That's the final tranche of payment. It's an ECB which we had taken a few years ago. And working capital, that would be around INR150 crores to INR160 crores.

items.statement: Prices generally stable; hikes only if major raw material cost change; gross margins high enough to absorb shocks
items.quote: No. If there is a big change in raw material cost then definitely we'll take a price hike. And overall we have experience of now 27 years of running the company. So what we have seen is that prices are more or less steady because we don't see too much changes. As our gross margins are pretty high so we are able to manage any raw material shocks which come in the market.

items.statement: High competition; price delta vs MNCs ~20-25% on comparable quality
items.quote: See, It depends on product-to-product very hard to say what is the delta. But I would say, maybe 20%, 25% price differential for sure between Indian companies and large multinational companies.

items.statement: Container shortage/freight rates elevated till Oct-Nov; mitigated by geographic and product diversification
items.quote: And as we hear from industry sources that this container shortage or export freight rates will only come down by October, November. So next two months, three months it's challenging. But we are very hopeful that we will be able to mitigate this risk and continue with the good growth here so far in the export business.

items.statement: China plant (<USD 2M revenue, 40-50 people) may shut in 18-24 months due to high costs and lease expiry; PAT impact positive
items.quote: Look so China plant is a very small plant with less than 40, 50 people and the revenue is under USD2 million from China plant. And the reason we will probably close it down is because of current cost structures in China are much, much higher as compared to India. And also, the plant lease is expiring in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Vision 2030 targets India growth 22-25% vs market 12-15%; current hospital coverage 40%
items.quote: Vision 2030 is mainly focusing on Indian market, that what is happening in India and how we can actually outsmart the growth, which is 12% to 15%. And can we do around, let's say, 22% to 25% growth in India.

items.statement: Added ~75 plant/regulatory/R&D/manufacturing staff in addition to 40 sales hires in Q1
items.quote: Of course, we have also added maybe around 75 people in the plants across different you know, in regulatory, quality, manufacturing R&D, and other services. But mainly we are calling out more on the sales side because this is something we want to build more strongly.

items.statement: Sales volume increased 4% QoQ and 14% YoY to 2.09 million tons in Q1 FY25, driven by higher HSM product sales.
items.quote: Sales volume for the quarter witnessed increased by 4% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and 14% on a Y-on-Y basis and that to 2.09 million tons.

items.statement: Steel sales realization saw a slight uptick of around 1% QoQ in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Our steel sales realization also saw slight upstick of around 1% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Management expects a 1% softening in NSR in Q2 FY25 compared to Q1 FY25.
items.quote: As we progress into second quarter of the financial year '25 we feel slight level of softening of NSR by 1%.

items.statement: SMS costs dropped considerably in Q1 FY25 due to lower coking coal and thermal coal prices and superior productivity.
items.quote: Our SMS costs in the quarter witnessed a considerable drop owing to lowering of both coking coal price and thermal coal price along with superior productivity in our operations.

items.statement: Expecting coking coal price savings of $30-35 per ton in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Further, we are expecting savings in coking coal price in Q2, '25 by around $30 to $35 per ton.

items.statement: Recent auctions show iron ore price reduction of INR500-1,000 per ton.
items.quote: So the steel price, we have seen the recent auctions, and we are seeing around INR500 to INR1,000 per ton reduction in iron ore price as well.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA was INR2,831 crores in Q1 FY25, up 13% QoQ due to higher volumes, realization, and cost efficiency.
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the first quarter, was INR2,831 crores, which is 13% higher on a quarter-on-quarter basis, mainly on account of higher sales volume, higher sales realization and cost efficiency achieved at our plants.

items.statement: PAT surged 43% QoQ to INR1,338 crores in Q1 FY25 due to higher EBITDA and lower subsidiary losses.
items.quote: Our PAT surged by 43% on a quarter-on-quarter basis to INR1,338 crores. This is mainly due to higher EBITDA and lower losses at our subsidies.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt reduced to INR10,462 crores at end of Q1 FY25 from INR11,203 crores previous quarter due to repayments; net debt-to-EBITDA at 1x.
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt is INR10,462 crores at the end of quarter 1, which has dropped from INR11,203 crores reported during the last quarter. This is mainly due to repayment made during the quarter. This has further helped to ease already strong net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1x, which is by far the best as per the industry standards.

items.statement: Target to maintain net debt-to-EBITDA at 1.5x after project completion.
items.quote: So we have maintained that we will maintain 1.5x of net debt to EBITDA that we will be maintained. That is our target, and we will be within that range.

items.statement: Capex in Q1 FY25 was INR2,796 crores; cumulative capex incurred on 6 MTPA expansion is INR17,500 crores.
items.quote: Our capex in the quarter stood at INR2,796 crores.

items.statement: Cumulative capex incurred on expansion projects is around INR17,500 crores.
items.quote: So from the capex side, we have already incurred around INR17,500 crores on these projects.

items.quote: We are targeting to complete the major facility that is blast furnace, BOF, CRM, well, JIND/l r/ STEEL & POWER Jindal Steel & within timeline by Q4 of financial year '25. The remaining ancillary facility will be completed in another 9 to 12

items.statement: Pellet plant current run rate close to 4 million tons per year.
items.quote: If I was to give you the current level, we are close to a run rate of 4 million tons for the year.

items.quote: We are sitting on a plan of close to 3 million tons. As of now, we did in quarter 1 versus roughly around 450 kt.

items.statement: Product mix shifted to 57% long and 43% flat in Q1 FY25 from 68% long and 32% flat a year ago.
items.quote: So as compared to the last year of 68% to long and 32% flat. In the first quarter, this financial year, we have been 57% long and 43% flat, if that answers your question.

items.statement: RINL MoU progress affected by strike at Gangavaram port forcing blast furnace shutdowns; supplies not yet stable.
items.quote: RINL, MoU progress is quite well. But unfortunately, some uncontrollable factors at RINL level because of some strike at Gangavaram port that derailed the entire stuff because they have to put off their blast furnaces, two of them.

items.quote: If you add all of them together it will probably be Rs. (+3,000) crores worth of launches that we will have minimum for the rest of the financial year.

items.statement: Pan-India sales momentum continues; premium and mid-premium segments now constitute over 70% of the market, aligning with company focus.

items.quote: My feel is from the next financial year, not from the F25 but F26 onward you will start to see the new portfolio projects starting to kick in which will try to absorb the drag a lot more than right now.

items.quote: We are costing it conservatively. Knowing that there's always inflation and escalation and surprises. We also keep contingencies.

items.quote: If we go into more society redevelopment or JDA kind of projects this will be a slightly lower number other than that it would probably be a healthy Rs. 700 to 800 crores towards land as well.

items.quote: My goal is definitely do more than Rs. 4,400 crores that we did last year.

items.quote: We will share the details as soon as they are concrete from all perspective.
