items.statement: Ramkrishna Titagarh JV project cost now INR 1,800 Crores, first production batch expected Q4 FY26 for railway validation
items.quote: the project cost of the Ramkrishna Titagarh side the project is around INR 1,800 Crores right now. So, the project cost is INR 1,800 Crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin 23.1% adjusted for INR 17.5 Crores one-off election contribution, up 70 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '25 stands at 23.1%, adjusted for impact of one-off expense of INR 17.5 Crores as compared to 22.4% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Subsidiary margin improvement driven by operational efficiency at JMT Auto (now Ramkrishna Casting Solutions), Multitech and ACIL
items.quote: only operational efficiency. Mitul Shah: Okay. Naresh Jalan: And, Mitul, just to update you it is just a start. I think we had -- when we acquired these companies also we had said that it is a start of a new journey for us

items.statement: Export realization improved due to product mix change and new customer traction; domestic realization down due to raw material price decrease
items.quote: In terms of exports, I think, in terms of product mix change and addition of new customers, wherein order announcements had been made in previous years have started showing traction and that is the reason realization in exports have improved.

items.statement: Raw material prices fully passed through; domestic steel prices not linked to global markets, driven by domestic supply-demand
items.quote: raw material prices is completely pass on for us. And basically, we cannot comment how the market will shape up into coming quarters. And in India steel prices is completely not in sync with the global market.

items.statement: Shipping costs hardened due to Red Sea crisis, impact INR 20-25 Crores per quarter now regular course of business
items.quote: I think impact was INR 20 Crores and I think still the impact remains similar in the similar range and that has become a regular precedent. I think Red Sea issue unless the war stops, I think there is nothing which can be done.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle at 90 days, expected to remain at this level
items.quote: Working capital is around 90 days. Net working capital is around 90 days, and that will continue to remain at 90 days cycle.

items.statement: Gross and net debt elevated by ~INR 100 Crores on consolidated basis due to subsidiary investments; full year debt expected at FY24 levels
items.quote: the gross debt and net debt for the quarter if you look at it is a little bit elevated by almost INR 100 Crores on the consol basis due to the investment made in the subsidiaries. And we have already shared earlier also the debt levels will remain at the level what we are in the FY '24 in the full year by the end of full year.

items.statement: Acquired legal entity in Mexico (Resortes Libertad) to establish operations, no manufacturing operations currently
items.quote: We will acquire this company to start up in Mexico. This company has no business and help to set up a legal entity in Mexico for us it would have taken us 1 year time and to start business.

items.statement: Order inflow breakdown: North America INR 526 Cr (CV 201, LV 109, EV 16, non-auto 200), Europe INR 287 Cr (mostly CV), India INR 442 Cr (CV 362, non-auto 80) + Railways INR 284 Cr, Rest of World INR 140 Cr (CV)
items.quote: To be specific the order inflow are to be executed over a period of 4 years except railways, where it is as per contract value. Against the current order flow that we have received in this quarter, it is worth INR 1,679 Crores

items.statement: Global forging market projected to grow from INR 94.74 Billion (2023) to INR 132.06 Billion (2028) at 6.7% CAGR; volume to reach 17.6 lakh metric tonnes by 2028-29 at 5.4% CAGR
items.quote: The global forging market had experienced robust growth in recent years and with a projected increase from INR 94.74 Billion in 2023 to INR132.06 Billion by year 2028 t hat reflects a CAGR growth of 6.7% over this

items.statement: Red Sea crisis impact INR 20-25 Crores per quarter ongoing; shipping costs not softening, dependent on war resolution
items.quote: shipping costs are right now hardened already and it's not softening so far. I think it has a lot to do with the Red Sea crisis and the ship movement. So it depends upon that.

items.statement: No acquisitions currently in pipeline; company policy to look for incremental growth opportunities
items.quote: As a company, as a policy, we are always looking for opportunities wherein we can incrementally grow. So, as of now, we don't have anything in pipeline.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 3.5% to 3.7% for FY25
items.quote: our guidance to the market, which we have always said, is that we would be between 3.5% to 3.7% and we stay within the guidance as far as this is concerned.

items.statement: ROA guidance maintained at 1.2% to 1.4% for FY25
items.quote: we have given the guidance of 1.2% to 1.4%, and we believe that we will be able to continue in this range.

items.statement: ROE target of 15% to 17% for FY25
items.quote: We always said that we would be in the 15% to 17% range, but for this aberration that happened due to this capital raise.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 0.9% to 1%
items.quote: We are still targeting at closer to about overall 1%. This has been our annualized target. But we will be happy if it is a little lesser. But I think we are prepared to digest up to 0.9% to 1%.

items.statement: Gross advances target of Rs. 1 lakh crore by March 2026
items.quote: the aspiration still remains to be that Rs. 1 lakh crore gross advances by March 26, and we stay committed to that.

items.statement: Deposit growth expected at 13% to 15% for FY25
items.quote: deposits we have grown between 13% to 15% and we believe that we will stay in the same trajectory.

items.statement: Advances growth expected at ~19% for FY25
items.quote: we are growing our advances book about 19%, which will continue for this year.

items.statement: PCR target of 80% in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We believe that our next target to reach as far as PCR is concerned would be the 80% in the next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: NIM increased 22 bps QoQ to 3.54% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On the NIM, we have increased it by almost 22 bps from the previous quarter, where we are at 3.54% for Q1FY25 compared to 3.32%.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 5.57% in Q1 FY25 vs 5.55% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The cost of funds for the Bank was at 5.57% for Q1 FY25 and when compared to the previous quarter it was 5.55%.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 3.36% QoQ to Rs. 75,455 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: gross advances, we clocked the highest is the Bank's history of Rs. 75,455 crores as on June 30th, 2024, as against Rs. 73,002 crores as of March 31, 2024, reflecting a growth of 3.36% on a Q-on-Q basis

items.statement: Retail advances contributed ~50% of incremental gross advances growth in Q1 FY25
items.quote: out of the Rs. 2,454 crores that we have grown, closer to 1,290 which is about 50% has come from retail advances.

items.statement: Aggregate deposits grew 2.15% QoQ to Rs. 1,00,164 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On aggregate deposits, we have clocked a record magic number of Rs. 1,00,163.92 crores. And this is again, ladies and gentlemen, the highest in the history of the Bank, as against Rs. 98,057.83 crores as of 31st March 2024, reflecting a Q-o-Q growth of a 2.15%.

items.statement: CASA ratio declined to 30.54% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The CASA deposit stands at about 30.54% - this has decreased and this is an area where we need improvement.

items.statement: GNPA stable at 3.54% in Q1 FY25 vs 3.53% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The stressed assets, our GNPA is more or less at the same steady level. There is no real increase or decrease. It remains stable at 3.54% and 3.53% between this quarter and the previous quarter.

items.statement: NNPA increased to 1.66% in Q1 FY25 from 1.58% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: On the net NPA: There has been a slight increase from 1.58% last quarter to 1.66% and this is primarily on account of some recoveries which were slated for Q1 that has got shifted to Q2.

items.statement: Gross slippages dropped to 0.59% in Q1 FY25 from 0.79% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: this has resulted in our gross slippages, which has really dropped down to 0.59% in June '24, compared to the previous quarter of 0.79%.

items.statement: Standard restructured advances declined to Rs. 1,161 crore in Q1 FY25 from Rs. 1,339 crore in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The Bank has done well, where the number has come down to Rs. 1,160.94 crores compared to the previous Rs. 1,338.78 crores as of 31st March, 24th of the previous quarter.

items.statement: PCR at 77.97% in Q1 FY25 vs 79.22% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The PCR, which is the Provision Coverage Ratio, stands at about 77.97% for Q1FY25 when compared to 79.22% of the previous quarter.

items.statement: CD ratio increased to 75.33% in Q1 FY25 from 74.45% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: On the CD ratio, we've been continuously increasing and we stand currently at 75.33% up from 74.45% as of March and 72.46% as of June 23.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 52.76% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The Bank clocked a cost to income ratio of 52.76%.

items.statement: Opened 13 new branches in July 2024, total branches now 940
items.quote: While as of 30th June, we had declared only 927, but we have opened 13 new branches in the last couple of weeks. So, the overall number of branches is 940 as of today.

items.statement: Implemented RBI investment classification changes; transferred Rs. 131.56 crore to AFS reserve
items.quote: transitional adjustments on account of 'Available For Sale' ('AFS') portfolio and other securities has been credited to "AFS Reserve" and opening "Revenue Reserve" to the extent of Rs. 106.88 crore and Rs. 24.68 crore respectively.

items.statement: Guided revenue and earnings growth of 30% to 35% for FY25
items.quote: With our strong performance in Q1, and a positive outlook for the upcoming quarters, we feel we are well placed to deliver on our guided growth of 30 % to 35% on revenue and earnings.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 1000+ Cr with 70% executable in 12 months and 90% in 18 months
items.quote: So, order book in terms of duration, it is roughly, I would say 85% to 90% of the order book will consume over 18 months. I would say 70 odd percent would come over 12 months.

items.statement: Order book split 65% TIG and 35% Banking; expected to grow 5-15% in Q2
items.quote: Right now, the split is most 65:35 in terms of the order book with TIG something in the range of 65% and banking something in the range of 35%.

items.statement: Margins to stay flat for next 2-3 years as R&D investment increases; long-term target 40-50% EBITDA
items.quote: So, the game plan is for the next two, three years to not focus on margin expansion. I don't think this is the time for Aurionpro to do it.

items.statement: Data center services capture 30-50% of project CAPEX depending on contract scope
items.quote: Most of the contracts is include design and program management thing you are getting to probably 30%, 35%, 40% of the spend. But you would never get to the 100% of the spend overall.

items.statement: TIG mix shifting: Data center and Transit growing strongly, Smart City shrinking
items.quote: And this year, data center will grow stronger than the TIG overall growth number, transit will go stronger than the TIG overall growth number and smart cities will shrink, will not grow.

items.statement: US revenue expected to grow 50-60% in FY25 to mid-teens million USD
items.quote: We expect this year US to get to let's say a double digit million dollar , more around the mid-teens number which should be a strong growth.

items.statement: Acquired Arya.AI to build global enterprise AI for banking and insurance; integration underway
items.quote: We concluded the acquisition of Arya.AI, which is again a game changer for our strategy to create a global enterprise AI player that is sharply focused on creating the next generation of AI offerings for banks and insurers globally.

items.statement: AS Software (Omnifin) acquired for retail SME lending gap; targeting global expansion in SE Asia and Middle East
items.quote: So, lending as you know, we have been very strong on the corporate loan origination side , collateral management, limit management, et cetera , we did not have an offering on the retail SME digital lending space. That's where AS 's Omnifin fits in.

items.statement: Received final RBI authorization for online payment aggregator license (AuroPay)
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce that we have received final authorization from RBI on the online payment aggregators.

items.statement: AuroPay focused on high-margin embedded payments (software + payments), not commoditized B2C gateway
items.quote: So, we will try to first build a business around spaces that we are strong in , transit payments where we own the contract end-to-end, this becomes a fantastic lever for margin expansion in those businesses because we have been using third party gateways anyway.

items.statement: Successfully concluded QIP with participation from prominent global and Indian institutions
items.quote: We concluded a succe ssful QIP and it's very encouraging to attract prominent global and Indian institutions to join us in this mission to create a global tech player rooted in India.

items.statement: Transit business has strong global pipeline across US, Latin America, Australia, UK via MasterCard and Vix partnerships
items.quote: So, we see a very strong pipeline on the transit side, it will certainly grow very strongly this year.

items.statement: AMC revenue streams are sticky, permanent, indexed at 3.5-4.5% annually; not included in order book but in guidance
items.quote: So, your stream would probably go up between, let's say, 3.5% to 4.5% or so every year because of being indexed to CPI and stuff like that.

items.statement: Sales channel doubled in last year; sales & marketing spend kept below 5% of revenue
items.quote: So, we typically keep it below 5%. For us, having said that the channel is now twice the size it was last year.

items.statement: Aurobees SME platform is a 3-5 year play; not a meaningful revenue contributor currently
items.quote: But I would say this is a three to five year play , don't expect a meaningful revenue contribution this year or the next.

name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd

items.statement: Maintains FY25 domestic CV market guidance of single-digit growth; expects market to degrow ~3% for calendar year but company targets 10% outperformance via content per vehicle
items.quote: As of now, we maintain the same guidance because in the OE market, if you look at the changes, the marginal de-growth are actually factored in our forecast itself.

items.statement: Maintains export growth guidance of 15-20% for FY25; new compressor and brake chamber projects from August expected to offset Q1 headwinds
items.quote: On the export front, we are launching a new compressor project to one of the global customers, also a break chamber to another customer. So these are supposed to offset some of the headwinds that we face with another Customer.

items.statement: Domestic CV industry (>6t) degrew 3.5% in Q1 FY25 to 98,007 units due to election disruptions, rising costs, high inventory, and adverse mix shift to ICVs
items.quote: Commercial vehicle production (> 6 tons) in Q1 of FY 2024-25 registered a degrowth of 3.5% at 98,007 units in the corresponding quarter of the previous FY.

items.statement: EV bus sales dropped 53% in Q1 FY25 to ~550 units vs ~1,250 units in Q1 FY24; expects recovery from July as tender-driven programs resume
items.quote: Last year we were in the range of 1,200 plus compressors. This year it is almost 53% drop in the first quarter.

items.statement: Export order book growing due to bus segment growth in Europe, electric trucks in US, and new projects like clutch compressor and actuator assemblies for OE customers
items.quote: However, the future looks positive due to increasing order books due to growth in the Bus segment in Europe and electric trucks in US. Additionally, there are new projects in the pipeline such as clutch compressor assembly and actuator assembly for OE customers.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 19.7% in Q1 FY25 from 18.8% in Q1 FY24; PBT margin 16% vs 15.5%; driven by productivity, price increases (INR 7 cr), and raw material cost stabilization
items.quote: Our PBT in Q1 FY 2024-25 is 16% of product sales as against 15.5% in Q1 2023 -24 and our EBITDA for this quarter is 19.7% as against 18.8% in the same quarter of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Expects margins to progressively improve quarter by quarter through cost measures and customer negotiations despite market pressure
items.quote: We expect to keep on progressively improving our margins quarter by quarter. We have strong measures in place to be a ble to tackle both on the cost front as well as negotiations with our customers

items.statement: Achieved overall price increase of INR 7 crores in Q1 FY25 vs Q1 FY24
items.quote: An overall price rise of INR 7 crores is what we have seen in this quarter compared to the previous year's quarter.

items.statement: Raw material cost stabilization contributed to material productivity improvement and margin expansion
items.quote: The improvement in margin is largely driven by our productivity, price increases to customers and the fact that we are facing an RM stabilization in the RM cost which is leading to our material productivity being better.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 domestic sales mix shifted unfavourably to ICVs (lower content per vehicle) and away from trailers (down 13%); expects mix to normalize in coming quarters
items.quote: Particularly in this Q1 quarter there's a drop of about 13% with the overall mix of trailer production 13% less than the previous number, but that is specifically because the industry was affected because of all this election and the shortage of some of the other things.

items.statement: Launching high-content products: lift axle control, ECAS ECU, e-compressor, AMT, APU, Actuator 4.0, twin-cylinder compressor for DAF, compressor for Daimler Trucks
items.quote: Already, we have s tarted selling some lift -axle control systems, also electronic control for air suspension, some of the buses to one of the bus customers. These are all very high -content products

items.statement: Export sales largely inter-company via ZF Group; BMW (passenger car air suspension) is sole direct customer, saw 12% demand drop due to stock correction; expanding compressor supply to Volvo, DAF, Daimler Trucks
items.quote: Actually, our main issue last quarter was one of our important customers BMW to whom we are supplying the air supply unit. There is a demand reduction it is gone to the tune of about 12%.

items.statement: Aftermarket growth driven by Door Control Systems with ARAI-approved builders, OES spares up 46% on BS VI and EV products; new wins: ADAS/DBMS for corporate bus fleet, Trailer Pulse for corporate fleet, DEF supply for Bangalore STU
items.quote: OE Spares (OES) segment growing at 46% due to increased consumption of BS VI and electric vehicle products, particularly e-compressor kits, and filters.

items.statement: Export goods sales INR 277.7 cr, down 2.1% YoY due to sea shipment delays (lead time 6 to 8-9 weeks) and slowdown at major overseas customer; export services up 16% to INR 107 cr on engineering support
items.quote: The company registered export sales of Rs 277.7 crores in Q1 FY 2024 – 25, a drop of 2.1% over the same quarter in FY 2024.

items.statement: Red Sea logistics challenges factored into plan; realigned logistics including air freight to protect export top line
items.quote: No, now it has factored all these things in our plan. So this Red Sea impact had some challenges. We've also realigned our logistic planning, certain items we're trying to pick up through air.

items.statement: Ramping up Oragadam plant: producing e-compressors, Hydraulic ESC, ASP cartridge assemblies; added smart machining cells, DDSBA and ASA assembly lines for export footprint rationalization; added sixth line for actuator back-order clearance
items.quote: We set up assembly cells for Double Diaphragm Spring Brake Actuators (DDSBA) and Automatic Slack Adjusters (ASA) in the plant. These additions were aimed at supporting footprint rationalization for exports.

items.statement: Inaugurated Electronics Testing lab and design office at Oragadam to accelerate product development; rolling out Digital Manufacturing Platform across India sites, started at Ambattur, extending to Oragadam
items.quote: The company inaugurated an Electronics Testing lab and design office, strategically aligning with our footprint planning in India. These new facilities will enhance our capabilities and accelerate product development.

items.statement: ESC for buses already mandated; expects higher ESP supply tenders; AEBS and lane departure regulations ready but await government call; ESP likely to extend to trucks after 1-2 years of bus implementation
items.quote: See, one aspect is on the bus segment, the application of Electronic Stability Control. It's already mandated. We have now, the new government, the new tender and we have got some indications that we have to get ready for a higher ESP supply.

items.statement: Digital business revenue ~INR 80 cr/year (OE hardware + aftermarket subscription); grew 31.9% in Q1 FY25 on 100% connected vehicles from lead OE customer and new state empanelments
items.quote: Digital, we have two types of revenues. One is we sell the hardware systems at the time of fixing the system in the trucks and buses. Then we also have a subscription revenue in the market. So, all put together in the range of about INR 80 crores for a full year.

items.statement: MD P. Kaniappan retiring by year-end; extended 6 months for smooth transition; accepted board position at Sundaram Clayton with ZF permission
items.quote: Actually, you'll be knowing in the public domain that I will be retiring by this year end. So actually, my term ended by June itself. But then the ZF leadership wanted me to continue for more six months to ensure that the transition is smooth.

items.statement: Employee cost increase driven by R&D headcount addition of ~120 people; offset by higher engineering service revenue
items.quote: On the increase of the employee cost that cost is largely attributed to our R&D business with a headcount increase of about 120 people.

items.statement: ZF parent appointed India-focused board member 2 years ago; India board chairmanship moved to ZF nominee; expects better leverage of India footprint for export growth but no immediate new business quantified
items.quote: Yes. one of the Board members is responsible for India. It was a new arrangement in the last two years. And of course, the purpose or the idea is to focus on India and grow the ZF business in India.

items.statement: Signed MoU with IIT Madras for 'Mobility and Intelligent Transportation' initiative to develop Bharat Multi-Modal Mobility Stack (BM3S) aligned with UN SDGs
items.quote: In May 2024, the company signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras (IITM), to collaborate on the 'Mobility and Intelligent Transportation' (MInT) initiative.

items.statement: Target 10,000 operational rooms by FY30; on track despite Q1 slippage
items.quote: The goal of reaching 10K rooms by FY30 I think that is what we had articulated. From our perspective, we are well on track while some of you might look at the Q1 number as a negative number, but that is a slippage of the quarter.

items.statement: Funding 10,000-room target primarily from internal cash of Rs 1,437 crore; debt only if needed
items.quote: Currently we have a cash balance of about Rs. 1,437 crores and we continue to generate cash consistently year-on-year. So initially, of course, the first order of business would be to use this internal capital, to fund the CAPEX needs as we go towards the 10,000 room target and that is something which eventually, then finally, if we do reach a situation where that is not sufficient, maybe we would

items.statement: Net 387 keys added in Q1; FY25 net additions to exceed FY24; initial 2 years lower, then catch-up over 3 years
items.quote: I think our resort occupancy was stable at 90%. Mind you, this is on a higher inventory base compared to what it was last year we added about net 387 keys. So including that I think we have been able to maintain occupancy, which kind of talks to the demand pattern and the kind of customer response we are seeing as we continue to add inventory.

items.statement: Member additions 3,692 in Q1 FY25 (down 21% YoY); total membership crossed 3 lakh
items.quote: I think we added about 3,692 members and crossed the milestone of 3 lakh membership count in the quarter.

items.statement: Average unit realization (AUR) up 31% YoY to Rs 4.9 lakh due to product rationalization and offer optimization
items.quote: The highlight is really that there was a big focus on higher realization and so our average AUR, our average unit realization is up by 31% Y-o-Y to 4.9 lakhs.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 29.5%; PAT margin up 110 bps to 11.8%
items.quote: EBITDA was at Rs. 113 crores, which is up 17% year-on-year and our EBITDA margin also expanded by 220 bps to 29.5%. Profit after tax was at Rs. 45 crores, which is up 19% and our margin was at 11.8% which is again 110 bps up year-on-year.

items.statement: Pruned low-AUR products, tightened down-payment norms, removed incentives to improve quality of sales
items.quote: I think we actually pruned out quite a few of these offers during the course of the quarter. I think that obviously is a change which in some cases obviously brought the impact down, impact on member addition.

items.statement: Deferred revenue increased by Rs 60 crore to Rs 5,655 crore; cash yield 7.73% p.a.
items.quote: Deferred revenue after adding about Rs. 60 crores is at Rs. 5,655 crores. Our cash position also improved to Rs. 1,437 crore and as of now we are generating a yield of about 7.73% per annum.

items.statement: Member-to-room ratio ~56; target to bring it below 85% occupancy for better availability
items.quote: In my mind, I think the question is how do we bring down the 56 members per room because I think we need to bring that down, bring the kind of occupancy down to a level which is more manageable and so that there is more availability for members.

items.statement: Member retirals expected to rise; quarterly run-rate budgeted at 1,200-1,300 vs 1,000 in Q1
items.quote: So from my perspective, I think the way to look at it is that there are members retiring, but there are options to sell back to them, but the baseline in my mind should be higher than the 1,000 per quarter. Probably I would, from a budgeting perspective, probably take closer to 1,200 to 1,300 as a quarterly average.

items.statement: No active inorganic opportunities; HCRO stabilizing, will evaluate over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Right now there are none, I want to clarify. Secondly, I think from a perspective of a broader picture, I think these are opportunities which obviously evolve during special circumstances which I think as you correctly said, maybe it is not the right time frame, so that something will be open to, but as of now, as I said, it was for completeness that I mentioned it, but there is nothing active at

items.statement: HCRO revenue fell from EUR 160M to ~140M due to COVID and Russia-Ukraine war; focusing on operating metrics and Timeshare sales grew 34% YoY
items.quote: It was running as historically at 12 Million EURO EBITDA and then because of COVID, because of some Russia-Ukraine war, revenues were 160 million at that point and of course it is down to 140 odd million now.

items.statement: Reviving Corporate Fun Days program for B2B employee benefits and rewards
items.quote: So clearly, we do have a corporate offering and it is called Corporate Fun Days where what it does is companies can buy a pool of days and offer it to their employees as benefits. That program, I think because of COVID and other reasons, I think it was on the backburner. I think that is what we are reviving right now in terms of and in fact, we have put an organization again in place to focus a lo

items.statement: Exploring PPP opportunities with central and state governments for resort development
items.quote: We are working with various governments to partner with them in terms of developing PPP opportunities. As you know, it is a core area for overall the Indian economy. It has been highlighted by various leaders of various states as well as from the center in terms of how this could be a real growth area for India in the future and as we want to be part of it through these PPP initiatives.

items.statement: Solar capacity now 28% of total energy demand; 6 resorts net zero waste to landfill, 10 platinum-certified green resorts in Q1
items.quote: We have increased our solar capacity. Now it is 28% of our total energy demand. This of course makes sense from a sustainability perspective, but also is a huge driver for cost efficiency as we come more and more online of this.

items.statement: Targets 10,000+ wagon sales in FY25 and is on track to achieve it
items.quote: As we had guided that this year, we are targeting to achieve a sale of 10,000 wagons plus, and we are completely on track. And we are confident to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands close to INR 10,000 crores as of the call date
items.quote: So as already mentioned in the opening remarks, today our order book is strong . It stands close to INR 10,000 crores

items.statement: Expects wagon demand from Indian Railways above 30,000 wagons annually
items.quote: So again, we expect a strong wagon demand from IR, the expectations anything above 30,000 wagons is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Confident that consolidated EBITDA margins around 15% are sustainable and will improve with backward integration
items.quote: Definitely, these margins are sustainable, and I had mentioned in my previous calls also, this year, you will see the wheel business contributing significantly as well as the braking business.

items.statement: Adding 1,000 tons of foundry capacity by end of Q3 FY25 (calendar year 2024) to support 1,000 wagons/month target
items.quote: See, as I mentioned by the beginning of fourth quarter, we will be adding another 1,000 tons of foundry capacity, and we are on track towards that.

items.statement: Bonatrans capacity to machine 28,000 wheelsets in FY25 and 40,000-50,000 by FY26; targets 1 lakh wheelsets annually by 2027 with integrated forging line
items.quote: In the short, medium term, we plan to expand BIPL capacity to machine 28,000 wheelsets in FY '25 and up to 40 ,000 to 50,000 wheelsets by FY '26. These wheelsets will support JWL freight car orders

items.statement: Completed QIP raising INR 800 crores with INR 2,800 crores demand; capital for wheel and axle manufacturing plant
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the successful completion of our qualified institution placement, raising INR 800 crores. The QIP received an overwhelming response with total demand reaching approximately INR 2,800 crores

items.statement: JEM TEZ 1-ton electric LCV received ARAI approval; commercial production starts October 2024 (Q3 FY25) with 500 units target for FY25
items.quote: Production is set to begin in October Q3 FY '25 with the initial plan t o manufacture 500 vehicles in the inaugural year.

items.statement: Secured LFP auxiliary battery order for Vande Bharat from Siemens; RDSO certified; developing next-gen battery packs for Indian Railways
items.quote: Additionally, we secured a purchase order for LFP auxiliary batteries for Vande Bharat trainset from Siemens and have technically qualified for rail tenders.

items.statement: Brake segment revenue target for FY25 is INR 200-250 crores (including Stone India); incremental orders being added monthly
items.quote: When we talked about INR 200 crores, INR250 crores, we also included Stone India. And as I have just mentioned that in the next couple of months, we will be starting commercial production there.

items.statement: Plans integrated wheel and axle forging facility targeting 1 lakh wheelsets annually by 2027; exports to EU and global players expected post-commissioning
items.quote: We are also in advanced discussion to establish our fully integrated forging line for wheels axles in India with a target to manufacture around 1 lakh wheelsets annually and expect it to be commissioned and completed by 2027.

items.statement: Domestic wheelset demand estimated at 6 lakh annually (replacement + OEM); current domestic capacity only 1-1.5 lakh; India is major importer
items.quote: So, we expect annual demand to be nothing less about 6 lakh wheelsets. And today, if you look at the manufacturing capacity in the country, it is close to about 1- 1.5 wheelsets in the maximum.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt ~INR 450 crores; net debt ~INR 300 crores
items.quote: Our gross debt in consol basis is around INR 450 Crore and the net debt will be around INR 300

items.statement: Bonatrans supplies wheelsets to Indian Railways (LHB, Vande Bharat), metro players (Siemens, Alstom, BMRCL), other wagon manufacturers, and exports to Tatravagonka
items.quote: We are also selling wheel sets to Indian railways for the LH B and Vande Bharat applications and to the various leading metro players in India such as Siemens, Alstom, and Bengaluru Metro Rail ( BMS).

items.statement: Freight wheelset ASP INR 2.7-3 lakhs; Vande Bharat wheelset ASP INR 6-8 lakhs; high-speed applications command higher margins
items.quote: So, freight is around anything between INR 2.7 lakh to INR 3 lakhs. It depends on the raw material prices. And for Vande Bharat, it is I do not know again the exact numbers. But I would assume that it is anything between INR 6 lakh to INR 8 lakhs

items.statement: Container business fully utilized for FY25; supplying integrated BESS containers (INR 60 lakh - 2 crore) to major players; exporting to North America
items.quote: So again, completely integrated containers can be anything depending upon the size and the type of battery capacity, can range between INR60 lakh up to INR2 crores.

items.statement: Targets >50% revenue from non-wagon businesses by FY28; non-wagon revenue to grow significantly
items.quote: See, as I've mentioned that by '28, we expect at least more than 50% of our revenues to come from our non-Wagon business. And again, I stand by that.

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery backward integration plans being finalized; will announce once firmed up
items.quote: Yes, we have a plan to backward integrate, and we are in the process of finalizing the same. So right now, we are focusing on developing the right technology and getting ourselves certified.

items.statement: Significant competitive edge from forward integration (design capabilities, GATX/Tatravagonka partnerships) and backward integration (wheels, brakes)
items.quote: But we believe we have a significant edge because of forward integration in terms of the design capabilities, which we have and the kind of partnerships we have with people like GATX and the design feedback which we get from Tat ravagonka

items.statement: Strong private sector order inflows continuing monthly; Indian Railways expected to release significant tenders in coming months
items.quote: As I have told you again from the private sector, we are continuously adding incremental order books. And we expect Indian Railways also to come out with significant tenders in the coming months.

items.statement: Stone India brake commercial production expected in next couple of months; infrastructure upgraded, awaiting railway licenses
items.quote: Further on Stone India, again we expect railways to grant us licenses very shortly. We have already upgraded our infrastructure, and we expect commercial production to start in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Wheelset exports to Europe (Tatravagonka needs 50,000/year) and other EU players to begin after forging facility commissioning by 2027
items.quote: Our partner, Tatravagonka, they themselves require about close to 50,000 wheelsets annually. And plus, we are already in discussions with other European players who themselves are looking at alternative sources for wheel set procurement.

items.statement: Bonatrans revenue target INR 300-400 crores for FY25; Q1 revenue INR 74 crores, fivefold increase YoY
items.quote: We aim for a turnover of INR 400 crores from BIPL for FY '24-'25. In the short, medium term, we plan to expand BIPL capacity to machine 28,000 wheelsets in FY '25

items.statement: EV (JEM TEZ) seeing significant B2B/aggregator demand; no competition in segment; order books expected to fill immediately post-launch
items.quote: We are confident that we have -- that once we launch, we'll immediately fill up all our order books. So, we do not see any challenge in terms of the demand.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle volumes stable YoY; Q1 dip due to elections/summer; expects growth post-monsoon vs last year
items.quote: So, there is no significant -- this was a legacy business for us . it is not that we are not focused, and we want to continuously grow this business. But as you see , there is no significant drop in numbers.

items.statement: Q1 production impacted by 7-phase general elections across multi-location plants and extreme summer weather; execution picked up post-elections
items.quote: So, as I mentioned very clearly, see if you look , from Q1 FY '24 there has been a significant jump. But yes, from the last quarter there has been a drop and I have mentioned very clearly that this is because of the disturbances because of elections.

items.statement: BESS container market >5 GW globally, projected 10 GW in 3 years ($1B+); India policy push creating opportunity; exporting to North America/Europe
items.quote: So overall, I think globally today, it is a business of more than 5 gigawatts, and it will be -- I think it's projected in the next 3 years to be about a 10 -gigawatt business.

items.statement: Management expects to nearly double the original 10% full-year growth forecast based on Q1 performance and order book strength.
items.quote: But Quarter 1, we stand at 24%. The order book is currently 24% up as compared to same period last year. So, at this juncture, we believe we should be able to nearly double the original growth rate that we had foreseen for ourselves for the entire year.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 4,813 crore, up 24% year-on-year.
items.quote: Further, as we stand today, our order book is at Rs. 4,813 crore, which is approximately 24% higher as compared to same period last year.

items.statement: Topline grew 24% YoY to Rs. 2,621 crore; GMV grew 28% YoY to Rs. 3,898 crore.
items.quote: We achieved a topline of Rs. 2,621 crores, clocking a growth of 24% year over year, with a gross margin of 20.8%, which is an expansion of about 211 basis points.

items.statement: Routine capex budgeted at $4-5 million for the year, excluding last year's London property purchase.
items.quote: So, our CAPEX is usually to the tune of within $4 to $5 m illion is what we budget across our different verticals. And I guess that is where it should be for this financial year as well

items.statement: Manufacturing operations grew 54% YoY; Q2 capacities running full with similar outlook for Q3.
items.quote: Happy to report that the manufacturing operations achieved a growth of 54% over the same period last year. And as we are talking to you today, the capacities for quarter 2 are running full and the outlook for Quarter 3 is also in a similar direction.

items.statement: Value-accretive businesses now contribute 15% of revenue, up from 10-12% a year ago.
items.quote: Our gross margin expansion journey continued as value -accretive businesses contributed 15% to total revenue. If we go back same time last year, these value -accretive activities were approximately 10% to 12%, and now the percentage has gone to 15% of the

items.statement: US sales grew 50% YoY; strategic sourcing deal signed with large US online fashion retailer targeting $50M then $100M annualized revenue.
items.quote: And if we talk about growth, the sales from US are 50% up as compared to the same period last year. As part of the new vertical investments that we have been making, investment in North America has been a key part of it.

items.statement: Ted Baker revenue $12.3M (~Rs. 102 crore), up 240% YoY; Gerry Weber revenue $22M (~Rs. 182 crore) in Q1, tracking toward Rs. 700+ crore annualized.
items.quote: Ted Baker, we have done $12.3 million, which is approximately Rs. 100 crores, Rs. 102 crores, and which is approximately 240% growth over the same period last year.

items.statement: New US e-commerce client (PDS Online Enterprise) targeting $30M in year one, scaling to $300-400M in 2-3 years at capped 4% net margin.
items.quote: First year we are considering almost $30 million of business in the financial year, but the numbers we have been given could go up to 300, 400 million easily in the next 2 to 3 years, once the supply chain is set up.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced from 7 to 2 days sequentially.
items.quote: We have further been able to reduce our net working capital days from 7 to 2.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 245 crore from Rs. 258 crore; net debt/EBITDA 0.6x, net debt/equity 0.2x.
items.quote: Moving to the balance sheet, our net debt as of June 30th 2024 stands at Rs. 245 crores, down from Rs. 258 crores as at the end of March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Ted Baker working capital debt (OD facility) to convert to insurance-backed factoring by mid-August, reducing Q2 debt.
items.quote: So, what is the OD facility should get translated into an insurance backed factoring facility. And to that extent, debt should come down.

items.statement: New vertical investments of Rs. 48 crore in Q1 (peak quarterly spend); expected to halve from Q3 and taper off.
items.quote: During the quarter, we continued to invest in new verticals, allocating approximately Rs. 48 crore to fund these new activities, new verticals.

items.statement: Cost optimization program targeting $15M annual savings (mainly procurement); central procurement team and IT systems (Project Weave) initiated.
items.quote: We have an EBITDA of about US $55 to $60 million. I am just speaking broad number. And the synergies that have been identified can lead to a $15 million annual savings and they are expected to largely come from procurement savings.

items.statement: Sourcing segment ROCE at 30% on gross capital employed of Rs. 1,112 crore.
items.quote: Our gross capital employed in this segment stands at Rs. 1,112 crores, delivering a return on capital employed of 30%.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBIT margin improved to 5.7% from 3.5% YoY despite Bangladesh wage hike.
items.quote: And in fact, what we have reported in Quarter 1, our factories achieved EBIT margin of 5.7%. And last year in the same quarter, the EBIT margin was 3.5%.

items.statement: Senior hire Dan Coen (ex-AlixPartners) joined as President Strategy & Market Position to leverage global retailer relationships.
items.quote: a very senior industry person, Dan Coen, who's been working with AlixPartners as a retail sector expert, he brings on board an extensive experience working in the retail sector and at the same time, an extensive network o f relationship across the global retailers

items.statement: Andrew Rini (ex-Boohoo Sourcing & Commercial Director) hired to lead PDS Online Enterprise for new US e-commerce client.
items.quote: One of the most competent teams in our industry, a guy called Andrew Rini who runs the sourcing of Boo hoo, one of the largest online retailers in the world, has joined us. He was the Sourcing and Commercial Director there to lead this initiative.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest caused 4-5 day disruption; estimated $15-20M shipment delay being recovered; factories reopened with partial then full attendance.
items.quote: And it's really up to quantify, we may have a delay of about $15 to $20 million of shipments because of these last 4-5 days of whatever happe ned. And we would be catching up on

items.statement: India seen as top China+1 sourcing destination; global retailers targeting 15% India sourcing share (from 5-7%) in 2-3 years.
items.quote: Indication we have got that this number could become easily 15% in the next 2 to 3 years. So, that means 5% to 15% it is 3x growth, 7% to 15% is doubling up the business.

items.statement: Market consolidating in UK/Europe/US; fewer but stronger retailers preferring solution providers like PDS over pure factories.
items.quote: So, on overall basis, the market is not shrinking, still growing 2%-3%, but is getting consolidated in fewer hands, which will then have a growth in their own business. So, those retailers who are growing are strategic customers of PDS.

items.statement: Bangladesh Taka depreciated >7% vs USD, causing Rs. 26 crore FCTR loss in OCI.
items.quote: This actually refers to we are just translating the foreign currency, our balance sheet, especially balance sheet related to Bangladesh, where the currency has been depreciated more than 7% in reference to this quarter, right? BDT to US dollars.

items.statement: Plan to consolidate ~17 legal entities; encourage new initiatives under existing top 10 verticals to reduce entity count.
items.quote: Internally, we have identified close to 17 entities which we believe can be consolidated. That is number one. Secondly, our existing verticals, top 10 are independently become sizable. So, more and more we are encouraging that can the new initiative be parked more with them so that the need to have independent legal entities keep coming down.

items.statement: Minority interest share of PAT expected to normalize to 20-25% (from current elevated levels) as new investments mature.
items.quote: In a steady state, we believe 75% to 80% should be the profit that should get attributable to public market shareholders and approximately 20% to 25%. If you take the last 1-1.5 years out, somewhere that has been the trend.

items.statement: Target AUM of Rs. 700 crores for FY25 as per plan submitted to banks and rating agencies
items.quote: So the target for the current year as per the plan that we have submitted to banks and rating agencies is to basically have a AUM of around Rs. 700 crores, that is what we are targeting

items.statement: Target Rs. 1000 crores AUM by December 2025 (four to six quarters)
items.quote: Well see, considering the growth rate that we have done, the ballpark quarter if you want me to tell you it should happen over the next four to six quarters. So, that is what we are targeting, so right now 30th June 2024 we are presenting, maybe 31st December 2025, we should be able to reach that milestone

items.statement: Target Rs. 2000 crores AUM over next 48 months (16 quarters)
items.quote: If you are talking about over the next 16 quarters adding the six quarters and the 10 quarters which we are talking about over the period of next 48 months, we should be able to have about Rs. +2000 crores of AUM that is what we are targeting

items.statement: Expect sustainable spread of 500-550 basis points between portfolio yield and cost of funds
items.quote: going on a steady state basis, we expect to keep a spread of around 500 to 550 basis points on a sustainable basis

items.statement: Rating upgrade expected after crossing Rs. 650-700 crores AUM over next four quarters
items.quote: maybe Rs. 650 crores, Rs. 700 crores plus of AUM if we are able to cross that should be a big , big signal for us to go back to the rating partners and then seek a rating upgrade

items.statement: Plan to expand branch network from 34 to 50+ branches by end of FY25
items.quote: right now we have 34 branches, our objective is to basically have +50 branch presence hopefully by the end of the current financial year

items.statement: Target 100+ branches on steady state basis to support Rs. 2000 crores AUM
items.quote: over the period of next, three to four +100 branches is something Star HFL should have on a steady state basis

items.statement: AUM grew 73.55% YoY to Rs. 471.41 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: The asset under management stands at Rs. 471.41 crores as of 30th June 2024 compared to Rs. 271.62 crores on June 30th 2023, thus reflecting a year-on-year growth of 73.55%

items.statement: Disbursements grew 76.61% YoY to Rs. 61.23 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter totaled at Rs. 61.23 crores making a year-on-year growth of 76.61% which was Rs. 34.67 crores for the corresponding period in the previous year

items.statement: Co-lending partnerships contribute ~12% of AUM
items.quote: Around 12% of our asset under management comes from co-lending partnerships

items.statement: Borrowings at Rs. 335.35 crores from 6 banks and 11 financial institutions; debt-to-equity 2.43x
items.quote: Our current borrowing stands at Rs.335.35 crores through six banks and 11 financial institutions, thus giving us a set debt to equity ratio of 2.43 x

items.statement: Added two small finance banks this year; exploring NCDs and hybrid debt for liability diversification
items.quote: we have added two more banks this financial year and they are from the small finance bank fraternity, besides that from a diversification perspective, we will continue to explore and engage our lending fraternity in issuing instruments like NCDs, we are also looking at seeing a situation where if we could look at more something like a hybrid Star Housing Finance Limited July 26, 2024 debt kind of

items.statement: Board recommended 50% dividend increase from Rs. 0.05 to Rs. 0.075 per share, subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: the board has recommended a 50% increase in the dividend payout for this year, this is subject to shareholder approval in the ensuing EGM. The dividend payout has increased from Rs.0.05 to Rs.0.075 per share

items.statement: Board approved second ESOP scheme for eligible employees
items.quote: Star Housing Finance Limited Board has approved the ESOP scheme for eligible employees. This is the second scheme implemented by the company

items.statement: Affordable housing segment insulated from sector headwinds; budget announcements (PMAY 2.0, 3 crore houses, Rs. 10 lakh crore outlay) provide tailwinds
items.quote: Recent budgetary announcement to provide right framework , assisting in creation of more than three crore houses across the length and breadth of India, including the outlay of more than 10 lakh crore and re -launch of PMAY through PMAY 2.0 as well as restarting the credit linked subsidy scheme should add to the favorable macros to the housing space

items.statement: Branch economics: minimum Rs. 50 lakhs monthly disbursement to open branch; steady state target Rs. 1.5 crores (medium) to Rs. 2.5-3 crores (large) per branch
items.quote: steady state run rate of around Rs. 1.5 crores is something which the branch should aspire to achie ve. Once it crosses Rs. 2.5 to 3 crores, in the bigger centers for that matter. At that point of time, we would want to have a second branch

items.statement: Collection efficiency: 95% collection in first month post-COVID moratorium
items.quote: even Corona for that matte r when our circuits got tested, when were in so many shocks at that point of time also, the appraisal that we did basically gave us that confidence given that after the moratorium the collected addition will be shot back to 95% in the first month itself

items.statement: Expects no sales growth in FY25; volume to increase 4-6% next quarter from debottlenecking; running at 95-97% utilization
items.quote: We do not anticipate any sales growth this year, a little bit, we are doing some de-bottlenecking and volume from next quarter will increase vis-à-vis this quarter, by 4% to 5%, 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Targets 15-17% EBITDA margin as reasonable for standalone spinning; currently at 12% with room for improvement if demand recovers
items.quote: As I said in a previous question, for us 15%-17% is what we expect as a reasonable margin and a good margin for a standalone spinning company.

items.statement: Sees sustained demand recovery with western retailer inventories at three-year low; expects festive season traction and demand improvement in second half
items.quote: We see a sustained demand recovery going forward as sales to inventory with index of most of the western countries is at a three-year low.

items.statement: Yarn spreads increased consistently over 4 quarters from INR98 to INR110; expects spreads to stabilize or improve with demand recovery in H2
items.quote: The spreads of the yarn for us, for all the total basket has increased. So last year, this quarter, it was around INR98 and last quarter was around INR105 and this quarter, it has gone up to INR110.

items.statement: Cotton prices stabilized at INR55,000-60,000 range for 8-9 months; currently ~INR57,000; expects stable to lower prices as new crop arrives
items.quote: So, we have seen them highly stabilized in last 8 to 9 months. There was a brief uptick in February, March. But other than that, they have been in a price range of 55,000 to 60,000.

items.statement: Debottlenecking to increase production by 6% operational by October-November; major volume expansion only with new projects
items.quote: The volume can only come if you go for a new expansion. So, within what we have right now, the drivers are, the debottlenecking that we are doing which will increase our production by 6%.

items.statement: Running at 95-97% utilization (maximum feasible); 25 MW rooftop solar operational generating 15% of power needs
items.quote: We are already running at 95%, which is, 95% to 97% is the highest you can run at.

items.statement: Short-term debt reduced from INR400-450 crore to ~INR100 crore; repaid INR350 crore short-term and INR40 crore long-term; quarterly long-term repayment INR15-16 crore
items.quote: So, the short-term debt has come down from a level of almost 400 crores, 450 crores as on 31st March 2024 to around 100 crores as of today. So, we have repaid almost 350 crores of short-term debt

items.statement: Cotton inventory held below current market price; no fixed inventory policy but generally stock for season till March; no inventory loss expected for 2-3 months
items.quote: Ma'am, right now, I cannot tell you the exact quantity we are holding, but whatever quantity we are holding is below the market price as of today.

items.statement: Exports 47% of revenue (up from 41% Q4); exports grew 16% YoY to INR290 crore; Bangladesh incentives for local yarn reduced sharply benefiting Indian exports
items.quote: Shared export of revenue was 47% as compared to 41% in the previous quarter. Exports have grown by 16% Y-o-Y from INR250 crores to INR290 crores.

items.statement: RoDTEP extended to advanced authorizations enabling better raw material and inventory management; Punjab power tariff increased marginally 1-2%
items.quote: The tailwinds we are anticipating is, first, the import is less positive with the RoDTEP being extended to advanced authorizations.

items.statement: Key risks: increased MSP making Indian cotton less competitive globally; volatile freight costs from Red Sea/logjam issues (though easing expected by Aug-Sept)
items.quote: The biggest uncertainty right now is the increased MSP which is a big challenge going forward as world prices being lower can make Indian cotton less competitive.

items.statement: Volume mix: 65% cotton yarn, 30-32% polyester-cotton yarn, 2-3% synthetic yarn; synthetic portfolio under pressure from Chinese dumping for 6-8 quarters
items.quote: So, in volume wise, almost 65% is cotton yarn and about 30%-32% is polyester cotton yarn and rest is synthetic yarn, 2%-3%.

items.statement: Global spinning consolidation with 4-5 million spindles permanently shut in 2 years; inefficient capacities exiting; buyers rewarding consistent quality suppliers
items.quote: We see a lot of consolidation happening in the spinning sector across the world with inefficient capacities getting permanently shut. The unofficial number itself is close to 4-5 million spindles in the last two years

items.statement: EBITDA margin 11.6% in Q1 FY25 (up 240 bps YoY, 66 bps QoQ); gross margin expanded 232 bps YoY; PAT margin 5% (up 165 bps YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR73.8 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11.6%. EBITDA increased by 48.15% Y-o-Y and 10% Q-to-Q.

items.statement: Board approved 1:10 stock split (INR10 to INR1 face value) to make shares more affordable for retail investors
items.quote: The Board has also considered and approved a sub-division/split of 1 Equity Share having face value of INR10 each into 10 equity shares having face value of INR1 each

items.statement: Power cost flat YoY despite higher production due to 25 MW rooftop solar (15% of needs); solar reduced power bill by 15%
items.quote: So, electricity cost Y-o-Y has come down because we have implemented a new a rooftop solar plant. So, we are generating almost 15% of our power in-house.

items.statement: Bangladesh operations resumed after 4-5 day shutdown; minimal impact as garment industry can make up lost production
items.quote: There was a complete shutdown from last Thursday till yesterday. So, there was no contact. But the business has resumed since yesterday morning.

items.statement: International Security margins expected at 4%-4.5% steady state for the year
items.quote: I think you should work with the 4%-4.5% range. That's the reason which International business is being performing generally. And I think broadly that's where I see it.

items.statement: India FM margins targeting 5% range within two quarters
items.quote: On FM also, we just mentioned that we hope to reach the 5% range by the end of the year in around two quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected to break out of current range by Q3 FY25
items.quote: And I think in Q3 or so, we should have -- you should start seeing us breaking out of this particular range.

items.statement: International Security EBITDA down 14% YoY due to labor shortage, wage hike, leadership changes and loss of profitable contracts in Australia
items.quote: As a result, while the top line of the Security Solutions – International business segment grew 2.7% Y-o-Y, EBITDA took a hit and was down 14% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: India Security revenue INR1,338 crores, up 8.8% YoY with 5.4% EBITDA margin
items.quote: India Security reported a revenue of INR1,338 crores in this quarter, an 8.8% growth Y-o-Y and an EBITDA margin of 5.4% stand-alone.

items.statement: Facility Management revenue INR530 crores, up 2.2% YoY with 4.2% EBITDA margin, up 30 bps sequentially
items.quote: Facility Management reported a revenue of INR530 crores, 2.2% growth on a Y-o-Y basis and EBITDA margin of 4.2%, which is actually 30 basis points higher than the last quarter.

items.statement: Cash Logistics revenue INR171 crores, up 12% YoY with 17% EBITDA margin and 8.1% PAT margin
items.quote: The Cash business expanded its EBITDA by 130 basis points, at a 17% EBITDA margin, and a PAT of INR14 crores translating to 32% Y-o-Y growth and a PAT margin of 8.1% in this quarter.

items.statement: Demand for integrated Facility Management solutions remains strong
items.quote: The demand for integrated Facility Management solutions continues to remain strong in

items.statement: VProtect business at INR10 crores monthly billing with ~20% EBITDA margin, over 25,000 installations and rapidly growing
items.quote: VProtect business is tracking very well. It has a good pipeline of contracts. It's run rating close to INR10 crores for monthly billing, monthly invoices INR10 crores, close to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: India Security added 4 branches in Q1 FY25, total 156 branches as of June 2024
items.quote: So I'm sorry, I don't have the numbers at absolutely so to tell you in terms of the employee headcount. But what I can say is that if you look at our branch count, on 31st March '24, we had 152 branches in SIS Security, which as of June is 156. So we've added four branches.

items.statement: Australia minimum wage increased 3%, pass-through occurs at contract renewals over 1-2 quarters
items.quote: And I would say that basis the last management catch-up that I did a few days back, it would take one to two quarters to bed this in, which means to pass through the higher wage cost as and when they come up for renewal.

items.statement: India wage hikes passed through instantly from effective date, no negotiation or waiting period
items.quote: With regards to India, the mechanism is straightforward from the date that the pay hike is effective, the minimum wage hike is effective. Even if it is retrospective, we instantly pass through. There is no negotiation. There is no timeline. There is no waiting for a time table.

items.statement: Budget provisions for first-time job entrants and PF support seen as positive, awaiting fine print for implementation details
items.quote: we're very happy to report that the key provisions related to benefits for professionals entering for the first time in the job market, PF support being given by government to the employers are very positive initiatives and they are going to have a positive impact on us in the near future

items.statement: DAM Capital appointed for Cash Logistics demerger process, documentation nearly ready, clarity expected next quarter
items.quote: Well, DAM Capital has just been appointed to run the process and documentation is more or less ready. Hopefully, in the next quarter, we'll have good clarity around that.

items.statement: No acquisitions currently on the horizon to disclose
items.quote: Well, I think at this point in time, there is nothing on the acquisition front that I can disclose to you.

items.statement: Henderson Singapore business annualized revenue ~$40M, near breakeven, no further cash consumption from parent
items.quote: Today, the business is fixed up and is back run rating at $40 million plus on an annualized basis. At its worst point, it was losing close to $5 million in terms of annual losses. Today, annual losses are zero.

items.statement: International Security facing 1-2 quarters of turbulence due to Australia labor shortage and 3% wage hike
items.quote: So yes, I think there is going to be two quarters of turbulence on the International Security, particularly in Australia.

items.statement: Railway FM contracts awarded post-COVID with unfavorable terms creating drag, exit limited by government tender rules
items.quote: There is a bunch of railway contracts, which we are trying to exit. But obviously, being a government tender, there are limitations, and there is only limited flexibility for vendors to step out.

items.statement: SXP Australia leadership disruption: CEO health issues, COO left after 3-4 months, business now in stable hands
items.quote: The guy who is running SXP for us, which is a $150 million business, he unfortunately came down with serious health issues. He suddenly stepped back, led to a chaos. We didn't have leadership in place for succession. We inducted a CEO and a COO as a replacement, which lost us three to four months. Once both of them came on Board, the COO got a better offer, so decided to step out.

items.statement: Cash Logistics 5-year CAGR: revenue 17%, EBITDA 48% (Q1 FY20 to Q1 FY25)
items.quote: If you see this quarter onwards, we've started doing a very detailed note on the cash logistics segment in our earnings note. So if you refer to those pages, you will see that it has since Q1 of FY 2020 till Q1 of FY 2025, our Cash business has maintained a 17% CAGR on revenue growth and a 48% CAGR on EBITDA growth.

items.statement: SXP Australia had invoicing and collections issues this quarter
items.quote: SXP reported 1% EBITDA this quarter. They also had some issues on their invoicing and collections.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR3,130 crores (+5.1% YoY), EBITDA INR137 crores (-1.2% YoY)

items.statement: Bhiwadi greenfield project Phase-1 to complete in 15 months with trial production in Q4 FY25, fully available next financial year.
items.quote: We have said 18 to 24 months, but I think we will be able to complete the Phase-1 project in 15 months, and we are likely to start the trial production in Q4 of this year. So, this will be fully available for next financial year.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire Fronberg high-tech foundry assets in Germany for EUR 5.5M plus EUR 0.5M debt; plan additional INR 60 Crore investment over 15 months.
items.quote: We have signed a definitive agreement to acquire high technology foundry, the assets of high technology foundry in Germany in Fronberg and this has got marquee customers for the engine blocks for industrial engines.

items.statement: MoU signed for second acquisition (Sunbeam) in aluminium business with 20-year export history to North America; due diligence near completion.
items.quote: The second acquisition target, still it is under work in progress. There is no definite agreement signed. There is an MoU signed. Due diligence is close to be completed.

items.statement: DR Axion integration on track after 17 months; no significant capex needed, cash flow excellent, all Korean expatriates retained.
items.quote: DR Axion is now practically 17 months; it has been completed. I think it is not a capital intensive. We are not looking at CAPEX there. It is only maintenance CAPEX and a very marginal CAPEX. The cash flow is excellent, and the management is intact.

items.statement: M&HCV still declining; tractor showing green shoots end of Q1; two-wheeler robust; passenger vehicle slowed after one-year growth.
items.quote: M&HCV is still not showing any respite. It's still on a declining trend, whereas there have been green shoots in the tractor industry at the end of the 1st Quarter. Two-wheeler has been very robust. Passenger vehicle has slowed down after a good one-year growth period.

items.statement: Aluminium commodity prices up 12-15% QoQ inflating top line and optically lowering EBITDA margin by 1-1.5%; underlying margins intact.
items.quote: Aluminum, there is actually, as I mentioned, some market research shows that 15% of commodity prices have gone up even quarter-on-quarter. Some say, it is 12-13%. Let us take the lower number 12-13%. So, artificially, the top line is inflated by 12-13%. That is maybe the EBITDA optically looks 1% to 1.5% lower.

items.statement: Export orders for passenger vehicle aluminium parts: two trial shipments done, third next week, production from Q4 FY25 targeting INR 125 Crore revenue next year.
items.quote: We have done two trial shipments already completed. Third trial shipment is going next week and production is slated to start from Q4 onwards. Next year we are looking at an upward revenue of around INR 125 Crore from the export of this particular product to Korea.

items.statement: Consolidated aluminium casting capacity currently 60,000-70,000 tons; tonnage misleading due to product mix variation (INR 2-4 lakh per ton).
items.quote: So, overall, when you look at the tonnage currently, we are having, it is close to around 60,000-70,000 tons. Depending on product mix, we are at that range currently.

items.statement: Powertrain standalone revenue mix: CV 54%, off-highway 16%, tractor 14%, passenger SUV 16%; PV grew, others stagnated or de-grew.
items.quote: On the powertrain, the break-up is, top line is 54% on the commercial vehicle break-up, off highway is 16% and tractor is 14% and in the passenger segment mainly SUV is 16%. So, passenger vehicle has seen growth and all other things have stagnated or de-grown.

items.statement: Fronberg foundry revenue: CY21 INR 232 Cr, CY22 INR 255 Cr, CY23 INR 257 Cr, CY24 ~INR 250 Cr; high single-digit EBITDA.
items.quote: Calendar year '21 was EUR 23 Million. So, we will just take a number of Rs. 100. So, to convert it was INR 232 Crore in '21 calendar year, '22 was INR 255 Crore and calendar year '23 was INR 257 Crore and calendar year '24, as I understand from the management, it is around a similar number. So, it's around INR 250 Crore is the top line. And they have been having high single-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Powertrain industrial engine segment revenue expected from FY27 Q4 onwards; FY26 Q4 initial sales; long-term growth strong regardless of CV cycle.
items.quote: So, when will the potential happen? It will happen from FY '27 onwards. FY '26, from Q4 onwards it will start seeing, but after that we will see, I think, many years of good growth on the Powertrain, regardless of the commercial vehicle business.

items.statement: QIP proceeds: INR 250 Cr for DR Axion acquisition, INR 300 Cr general corporate, INR 650 Cr for debt reduction; FY25 gross debt outlook depends on Sunbeam outcome and capex.
items.quote: One is INR 250 Crore was for the acquisition of DR Axion and it is very clear in the stated proceeds. And 25% was for general corporate, which is around INR 300 Crore. So, only INR 650 Crore was going to debt reduction.

items.statement: Management bandwidth assessed as sufficient; no new top management hires needed for Fronberg (self-contained) or Sunbeam (strong existing team); step-by-step approach to capex.
items.quote: We are not going to put any management in Europe. We are not going to recruit any management in Europe. We may recruit somebody here on a visit basis, not even permanently putting up there.

items.statement: Fronberg asset purchase via insolvency avoids past pension/worker liabilities; share purchase for land/building via separate real estate entity.
items.quote: When we are buying an insolvent company, it doesn't come with the baggage of old liability of the worker liability. Of course, the worker agreements survive, but we are not saddled with the past liability of the pension and things like that, which is part of the insurance, which has been already paid off.

items.statement: Fronberg customers are marquee global industrial engine OEMs (USD 10-50B revenue); single-source supply; customers supported acquisition and participated in meetings.
items.quote: We were in touch with the customers and some of the customers also asked us to acquire this with the promise of continuing the business and they have participated in the meetings also.

items.statement: Consolidated aluminium export share only 5-10%; Fronberg gives European footprint; Sunbeam has 15-20% direct export to North America; targeting global PV and industrial engine markets.
items.quote: Now, there is an export which is hardly 10% even on a consolidated basis, not even 10%, 5% to 10% on the aluminum segment of the business currently. With possibly Sunbeam, I think Sunbeam has got a good exposure to export. It is almost 15%, 20% direct export.

items.statement: Fronberg acquisition includes EUR 2M for liquid assets (WIP and inventory); additional INR 60 Crore earmarked for working capital over 15-18 months.
items.quote: We have earmarked totally INR 120 Crore, out of that around INR 60 Crore for the acquisition plan and another INR 60 Crore to further put into investment for working capital, and this is an approximate number because considering the exchange rates which are prevailing at that particular time.

items.statement: Kothavadi recruitment ongoing, hitting P&L for last two quarters; Fronberg retains all 140-141 staff including two head-office placements; only IT/accounts centralized previously.
items.quote: The Kothavadi plant is a very strategic investment. Yes, there has been new recruitment, and that is also hitting our P&L for the last two quarters, I would say.

items.statement: Aluminium commodity price increase 12-15% QoQ passed through to top line; structural parts pricing INR 3-4 lakh/ton vs two-wheeler covers INR 2 lakh/ton.
items.quote: Aluminum, there is actually, as I mentioned, some market research shows that 15% of commodity prices have gone up even quarter-on-quarter. Some say, it is 12-13%. Let us take the lower number 12-13%. So, artificially, the top line is inflated by 12-13%.

items.statement: Storage business showing good growth but margins still elusive.
items.quote: Storage business has shown good growth, but I think the margins are still elusive.

items.statement: Demand recovery seen from Q1 FY25 across both Crop Protection and Pigment segments after prolonged sluggishness
items.quote: After a prolonged period of sluggish global demand, we are witnessing a gradual sign of demand recovery from Q1 FY25. Our both the segments, i.e. Crop Protection and Pigment, reported healthy volume growth during the quarter, fostering positive sentiment for FY25.

items.statement: Launched 8 new products in fertilizers, biofertilizer, biostimulant category in Crop Nutrition segment
items.quote: During the quarter under review, in our Crop Nutrition segment, we have successfully launched 8 new products in fertilizers, biofertilizer, biostimulant category, providing a comprehensive one stop solution for our farmers to improve the productivity and nutrient use efficiency.

items.statement: Titanium Dioxide plant stabilized and running continuously; quality stabilized with approvals from new customers in ceramic, plastic, rubber, paint
items.quote: In Titanium Dioxide segment, now we have stabilized the plant, and it is running continuously. Quality of the product has been stabilized as well, and we have also received approval from few end new customers in different categories like ceramic, plastic, rubber and paint.

items.statement: Expecting interim antidumping duty on Titanium Dioxide from China probably in Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are also expecting interim antidumping duty on Titanium Dioxide from China probably in the Q3 of FY25.

items.statement: Revenue flat at INR 411 crore; EBITDA INR 14 crore up 194% YoY and 40% QoQ; profitability impacted by lower product price realization
items.quote: Company's revenue from operations remained flat at INR 411 crore, while our EBITDA stood at nearly INR 14 crore, increasing by 194% YoY and 40% on QoQ basis. However, our profitability for the quarter was impacted by lower product price realization across the markets.

items.statement: Optimistic that price improvement will be seen in coming quarters along with demand recovery momentum enhancing profitability
items.quote: We are optimistic that in the coming quarters, price improvement will be seen along with the momentum in the demand recovery, which will enhance our profitability.

items.statement: Crop Protection: production ~10,000 tonnes up 20% YoY, capacity utilization 73%, revenue ~INR 272 crore, EBITDA INR 11.3 crore vs INR 300 crore revenue and INR 0.5 crore EBITDA YoY
items.quote: In Crop Protection segment, production stood at nearly 10,000 tones, up by nearly 20% YoY. Capacity utilization for the segment stood at 73%. The segment reported revenue of close to INR 272 crores and EBITDA of INR 11.3 crores against the revenue of INR 300 crores and EBITDA of INR 0.5 crores in the corresponding previous year.

items.statement: Pigment: production 3,736 metric tonnes up 9% YoY, capacity utilization ~45%, revenue INR 138 crore, EBITDA INR 9.4 crore vs INR 121 crore revenue and negative INR 8.4 crore EBITDA YoY
items.quote: For pigment segment, production stood at 3,736 metric tone, up by nearly 9% YoY. Capacity utilization for the segment stood at about 45%. The segment reported the revenue of INR 138 crore and EBITDA of INR 9.4 crore against the revenue of INR 121 crores and the EBITDA of negative INR 8.4 crore in the corresponding previous year.

items.statement: Demand picking up across markets in Crop Protection after inventory destocking; Brazil market positive with reasonable inventory levels and good rain expectations
items.quote: We are getting very positive response, particularly from the Brazil market. And if we look at the inventory level, for majority of the products, barring few products, the inventory level has become reasonable. items.quote: So it has been running at flattish level, at the bottom most level. And I would say from the industry perspective, people predict that now once the demand will pick up, there will be definitely increase in the price as well because at this price level, it is not sustainable for any industry.

items.statement: China market prices at rock bottom; logistics costs substantially increased due to freight diversion; expects normalization from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Rahul bhai even today, the China market price is at rock bottom level. So from this level, it cannot go down, maybe 1% or 2% here and there. But from this level, they cannot go down because they are also bleeding. And regarding the freight related matter, yes, it is one of the major factor where you can see in our numbers also there has been substantial increase in the logistic costs. And we hope

items.quote: So those products, commercially, we are all set. From the regulatory approval point of view, we have started getting approval in the different, different markets. Going forward, over a period of next 2 to 3 years, we'll be getting lot many approvals in different, different markets for these new products. And regarding the product names, what products we have launched, we have launched cyfluthrin,

items.quote: Particularly in the case of Agrochemical segment, we are already running our plant in the Q1 at about 70% plus capacity. We'll try to maintain 75% plus capacity utilization probably in the second, third quarter onwards also. So we see the demand is going to be there as well as the plant utilization will be better going forward. In the case of Pigments segment, yes, the plant utilization is in the

items.statement: Agrochemical prices down ~25% in Q1 FY25 vs Q1 FY24; QoQ improvement expected from Q2 onwards in both volume and value
items.quote: So in the Q1, the price reduction, particularly in the case of agrochemical, was drastically compared to the first quarter of last financial year. I would say it is in the range of about 25%.

items.statement: Pigment underperformance due to Copper phthalocyanine pressure; Azo pigment seeing improvement from Heubach matter; raw material volatility in Q1; better realization expected from Q2/Q3
items.quote: Jainam Ji, the thing is particularly in the Pigment segment, we are particularly in Copper phthalocyanine based pigment, where still there is a lot of pressure in terms of supply point of view. The price realization and the demand improvement is taking place is more into Azo pigment. So currently, Heubach related matter globally, what we have seen, that is helping first in the Azo Pigment segment.

items.statement: Total CapEx INR 1,140 crore across 3 projects: Crop Protection INR 400 crore (INR 800+ crore revenue potential), Crop Nutrition INR 150 crore (5 crore bottle capacity, INR 1,000 crore revenue at full utilization), Titanium Dioxide INR 600 c
