In the Crop Nutrition segment, where we have spent about INR 150 crores, so it's a 5 crore bottle capacity plant where we can generate revenue on the full capacity utilization basis, I

items.statement: INR 600 crore Titanium Dioxide CapEx includes Phase 1 and some Phase 2 elements (captive power plant, layout); Phase 2 CapEx to be announced later; focus on sweating assets for 1-1.5 years before Phase 2
items.quote: So Aniketh Ji, because in the chemical plant, we cannot do 100% Phase 1 and Phase 2 separation. So certain things, we need to combine it. So like captive power plant, we have put up looking at the Phase 2 expansion. So we don't need to spend in future for the captive power plant. Likewise, in the current plant, manufacturing capacity, certain plant, equipments and the layout we have kept from the

items.statement: Debt repayment of ~INR 173 crore in FY25 and similar in FY26; target to substantially reduce debt in next 2 years
items.quote: So from the debt reduction plan point of view, in the first -- in this financial year, we'll be repaying about close to INR 173 crore of loan repayment, so which will bring us to quite reasonable level. Similarly, in the next financial year also, it will be close to same amount repayment will be there. So our target is to bring down the debt level substantially low in next 2 years' time.

items.statement: Expect return to profitability from Q2 FY25 after 4-5 quarters of losses; committed to growth and profitability
items.quote: Yes. So yes, I'm sorry, for continuously 4 to 5 quarters, we were in loss. From the Q2 onwards, there are very good chance we'll be in profitability, and we are committed for the same for the growth point of view as well as profitability point of view.

items.statement: Titanium Dioxide: ~35% utilization in Q1, targeting ~70% from H2 FY25 (near breakeven); Nano Urea: targeting 35-40% utilization in first year
items.quote: So the Titanium Dioxide from the second half of the year in the FY25, we predict that the plant will run at about 70% capacity. In the Nano Urea plant, because it's a relatively new concept, and it's a huge capacity, so it's not going to run at very high capacity. Initially, we predict that in the first year, we'll be running at about 35-40% capacity.

items.statement: No demerger plans in near future; focus on making Titanium Dioxide and Nano Urea segments profitable first
items.quote: No, nothing on the card from the demerger point of view because we would like to first make sure that all the segments, particularly Titanium Dioxide and Nano Urea segment, we would like to generate good revenue, good profitability, so not in the near future for sure.

items.statement: Nano Urea acceptability growing through field trials and promotions; government push via PM Pranam Yojana incentivizing states to promote nano fertilizers; substantial movement expected over next 2 years
items.quote: So Niharika Ji, it's a new concept, no doubt about it. But we have been doing a lot of promotional activity and field trials where we give the field trials to the farmers down the line and convince them the effectiveness of the product. It is very effective product, no doubt about it. And looking at that only, now a lot of companies, even in the private segment like Coromandel and all, they are al

items.statement: Nano Urea non-subsidized but government promoting via PM Pranam Yojana: 50% of subsidy savings passed to states; Gujarat example: INR 22,000 crore subsidy, INR 4,000 crore savings yields INR 2,000 crore to state
items.quote: So it is a non subsidized product. So directly, we don't get any support from the government. But indirectly, yes, we do get support from the government like every state because it is under the vision of our Prime Minister, Mr. Narendra Modi, he himself is promoting this product. So every state is coming with a different, different scheme where they would like to promote this product in a better w

items.statement: Titanium Dioxide: expect ~20% margin at INR 300 crore revenue with antidumping duty; Nano Urea: 15-17% margin target supported by 8 new products in basket
items.quote: So Madhur Ji, at about INR 300 crores revenue, along with the antidumping duty, which is going to come probably on the third quarter, we expect that there will be reasonable margin. It is a little early to mention at this juncture, but we predict that we should be having about 20% margin.

items.statement: Ilmenite raw material for Titanium Dioxide available in Kerala/Tamil Nadu but sourced imported/local; finished goods market in western India balances logistics; Gujarat infrastructure advantage
items.quote: So, Nishant Ji, yes, one of the raw material, which is ilmenite, it is available in that state, Kerala, no doubt about it. But we are getting the raw material either imported or local, no issues. At the same time, when we talk of the finished product, the major market is in the western part. So we are able to sell in this market. So if we are paying little more on raw material logistics, then ulti

items.quote: No, IFFCO is a much bigger organization. They have their own channel. So I would say it's a collectively, IFFCO and Meghmani because the market potential is tremendous. Indian market size for the particularly urea is 34 million tones. So it cannot be replaced 100% with the Nano Urea, but yes, it can be replaced substantially with Nano Urea. name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.statement: Overall Average AUM including alternate assets reached ₹3.68 lakh crores, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Overall Average Assets under Management including alternate assets, reached ₹3.68 lakh crores, reflecting a 19% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Mutual Fund Quarterly Average AUM reached ₹3.53 lakh crores with Equity quarterly average AUM at ₹1.62 lakh crores
items.quote: Our Mutual Fund Quarterly Average AUM reached ₹3.53 lakh crores, with Equity quarterly average AUM about ₹1.62 lakh crores.

items.statement: SIP numbers crossed ₹1,300 crores mark, showing 39% YoY increase from ₹987 crores to ₹1,367 crores
items.quote: SIP numbers during the quarter further moved up to cross ed ₹1,300 crores mark, showing a 39% year -on-year increase, from ₹987 crores in June 2023 to ₹1,367 crores in June 2024.

items.statement: Added around 8.39 lakh new SIPs, mainly a 3x increase from previous year
items.quote: We added around 8.39 lakh new SIPs, mainly we have seen a 3x increase from the previous year.

items.statement: Added around 9 lakh new folios during the quarter, total serviced folios at 94 lakhs
items.quote: We have witnessed healthy growth in our investor's folio. Have added around 9 lakh new folios during the quarter bringing our total serviced folios to 94 lakhs.

items.statement: Quarterly folio growth was 9% compared to industry's 7% growth
items.quote: Our quarterly folio growth was 9% compared to the industry's 7% growth.

items.statement: Passive assets total approximately ₹29,900 crores with customer base of 7.53 lakh folios and 44 products
items.quote: On the passive front, as of June 2024, our passive assets total approximately ₹29,900 crores. Our customer base has grown to about 7.5 3 lakh folios and have a diverse product portfolio of about 44 products.

items.statement: ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund touched size of close to ₹400 crores, will close in next few months
items.quote: We have launched and are currently under a fundraising plan for funds for ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund which invests in emerging markets. We have already touched the size of close to about ₹400 crores. We will soon be closing the fund in the next few months.

items.statement: Quant Fund NFO mobilized assets of around ₹2,400 crores, one of the largest in category and highest collection in many years
items.quote: We had a successful NFO collection of Aditya Birla Sun Life Quant Fund mobilizing assets of around ₹2,400 crores. It is now one of the largest funds in this category. And for us, also, it was one of the highest collections we have had in the last so many numbers of years.

items.statement: Achieved highest-ever quarterly profit in Q1 FY25 driven by improvement in asset mix and cost management
items.quote: Moving on to financials, we at ABSLAMC are happy to inform you that we have achieved our highest-ever quarterly profit in Q1 of FY25. This has been driven by improvement in the asset mix, overall asset mix and a strong focus on cost management.

items.statement: Total revenue ₹481 crores vs ₹389 crores in Q1 FY24, up 24% YoY; PAT ₹232 crores vs ₹185 crores, up 26% YoY
items.quote: Our total revenue is about ₹481 crores vs ₹389 crores in Q1 of FY24, up 24% Y-o-Y. Our profit after tax is at ₹232 crores vs ₹185 crores in Q1 FY24 up 26% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Opex guidance: employee cost growth 10-12%, other Opex growth 10-12% over the period
items.quote: So, the expenses, mainly we have been generally projecting that the expenses will grow in the inflation plus something. So maybe the cost of employees will be in the range of around 10%-12%. Other than that, other Opex will grow in the range of around 10% -12%, which is the administrative Opex.

items.statement: ESOP cost in range of around ₹3-odd crores, already part of employee benefit cost
items.quote: So Dipanjan, the ESOP cost is in the range of around ₹3-odd crores which is already a part of the employee benefit cost.

items.statement: Number of employees as of June is 1,520
items.quote: And number of employees as of June is 1,520.

items.statement: Equity yield around 68 bps; new fund yield lower than overall yield as share ~65% of DTR with distributors
items.quote: On yield, equity is in the range of around 68 bps. And new, generally, depending on a scheme to scheme, but we generally share around 65% of our DTR with the distributors. So, the yield on the new will be lower than the overall yield on the old stock.

items.statement: Debt yield around 25-26 bps; liquid yield around 12-13 bps
items.quote: Debt is in the range of around 25-26 basis and liquid is in the range of around 12-13 basis.

items.quote: Our business verticals in the alternative segment has also showcased healthy growth driven by AIF and PMS product launches and the AUM growth thereon. Passive business has also grown progressively through new product launches and scaling up the existing products.

items.statement: GIFT City presence established to manage overseas investments; launching ESG Engagement Fund, index-linked funds, thematic funds, Flexi Cap Fund, Global Blue-chip Fund of Fund for NRI investors
items.quote: By establishing our presence in GIFT City, we aim to manage and attract overseas investments into India to meet the growing needs of NRI and foreign investors. items.statement: ESG Engagement Fund seed capital coming in, will take off next quarter; ABSL Global Emerging Market Fund at ₹400 crores closing soon; ABSL Index Linked Fund and ABSL India Opportunities Fund for NRI investors launching
items.quote: We are also preparing to launch funds in GIFT City including ABSL India ESG Engagement Fund. This I had highlighted in the past, the ESG Engagement Fund, but finally, we are seeing the seed capital coming in and this fund will take off in the next quarter in order to drive funds from the rest of the investors in India.

items.statement: SIP flows coming from MFD channel, digital channel, and direct; majority from MFDs and digital channels
items.quote: I think with respect to the the SIP flows, largely we are seeing the flows coming from one Mutual Fund Distribution (MFD) channel, which is our traditional channel, then the digital channel, and then come from the rest of the channels, including direct. items.statement: FY25 inventory days target of 90-95 days

items.statement: FY25 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin target of 19-20%

items.statement: A&P spend guidance at 2% of revenue for FY25

items.statement: Pledge release targeted between August and December
items.quote: So we are looking to clear the pledge between the window of August and December.

items.quote: Largely it's because of that. So these are the two main reasons. The major reason is the lower cotton price.

items.statement: Expect further gross margin improvement in coming quarters
items.quote: We, as management, are confident that it should maintain or maybe even get better.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue at INR220 crores, up 16% YoY

items.quote: So we typically require about INR50 crores of annual investment in our business for adding 120 to 130 stores, which should very well be taken care by our internal accruals itself.

items.quote: In a normalized situation, in a year-through basis, we look to add about 100 to 150 LFS stores.

items.statement: No plans to change product pricing to drive volume

items.statement: Leggings and churidars contribute 40-45% of sales
items.quote: Leggings and churidars together should be about 45% -- 40% to 45% of sales.

items.statement: Trousers, pants and jeggings are key value-added categories

I think in the value-added products that category does well, and even the jeggings category. Even the jeggings side, it has done really well for us.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 104 to 87 days in Q1 FY25

items.quote: We achieved a strong pre-Ind AS operating cash flow of INR32 crores in June '24.

items.statement: INR220 crores cash on balance sheet invested in FDs and liquid funds
items.quote: As of now, as per our treasury policy, we have this invested in fixed deposits and liquid funds.

items.quote: Our tie up with Apparel Group in the Middle East is on track, and we should open our first door in this financial year.

items.quote: You would like to see another year of strong free cash flow and then we will be taking our call on dividend distribution.

items.quote: Despite this, we have maintained momentum on our touch point additio ns in our Cash Logistics business, where we added 3,000 points in Q1, and we totally now have 140,000 points
